Case MDAPY OVITO ASE Read a LAMMPS dump mdapy.io.read(path) import_file(path).compute() ase.io.read(path, format="lammps-dump-text") Write a LAMMPS dump mdapy.io.write(path, system) export_file(data, path, "lammps/dump", columns=[...], precision=17) ASE writes no dumps Read a LAMMPS data file mdapy.io.read(path) import_file(path, atom_style="atomic").compute() ase.io.read(path, format="lammps-data", atom_style="atomic", units="metal") Write a LAMMPS data file mdapy.io.write(path, system) export_file(data, path, "lammps/data", atom_style="atomic", precision=17) ase.io.write(path, atoms, format="lammps-data", atom_style="atomic", masses=True) Read extended XYZ mdapy.io.read(path) import_file(path).compute() ase.io.read(path, format="extxyz") Write extended XYZ mdapy.io.write(path, system) export_file(data, path, "xyz", columns=[...], precision=17) ase.io.write(path, atoms, format="extxyz")

The gzipped cases are the same calls with a path that ends in .gz.

The system is fcc copper with its atoms displaced at random by 0.1 Å along each axis. The dump holds the columns id type x y z; the data file the atom style atomic, with the mass of copper; extended XYZ the species and the positions.

MDAPY writes every number with as many digits as it takes to read it back exactly, at most 17. OVITO is asked for 17 significant digits. ASE writes the positions of a data file in full and those of extended XYZ with 8 decimals, so its extended XYZ is about a third smaller.

docs.title: How it is measured
docs.text:
• Each program runs in a process of its own. MDAPY and OVITO have 40 threads (MDAPY_NUM_THREADS, OVITO_THREAD_COUNT); ASE reads and writes in Python on one.
  • Before the timings, a separate process checks each program. Reading: the positions it reads are those MDAPY reads within 1e-12 Å, and the types and elements are the same. Writing: MDAPY reads back the file the program wrote, and finds the positions within 1e-12 Å (1e-8 Å for the extended XYZ of ASE) and the same types and elements. A program that differs is not timed.
  • The file to read is written by MDAPY before the timings, so it is in the file cache of the operating system: the times are those of reading and parsing, not of the disk. Writing goes to the local disk of the node as the operating system takes it.
  • The times of MDAPY for LAMMPS data files were measured last, on another node of the same kind.
  • Each process first reads or writes a system of 500 atoms, so that loading libraries and starting threads are not timed, then three times the system; the shortest time counts.
  • Making the system, and converting it into OVITO's data collection or ASE's atoms for writing, are not timed.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
The comparison is benchmarks/comparison.py in the source repository, the group files of its cases. It needs OVITO (pip install ovito) and ASE (pip install ase).

python benchmarks/comparison.py run --group files \
    --sizes 4000 32000 256000 2048000 9841500 \
    --threads 40 --memory 170 --timeout 1800 --output files.json   # as above
python benchmarks/comparison.py table files.json
python benchmarks/comparison.py plot files.json files.png

docs.title: Elements
docs.text:
mdapy.elements holds the chemical symbols, standard atomic weights and radii used everywhere in MDAPY. The atomic weights are those of IUPAC (Meija et al. (2016)); for an element without stable isotopes, the mass of its longest-lived isotope. The covalent radii are those of Cordero et al. (2008), with sp³ carbon and low-spin manganese, iron and cobalt; the van der Waals radii those of Alvarez (2013).

from mdapy import elements

elements.atomic_numbers(["Cu", "Ni"])  # array([29, 28])
elements.atomic_masses(["Cu", "Ni"])  # array([63.546 , 58.6934])
elements.element_from_mass(26.98)  # 'Al'

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: Name Meaning SYMBOLS The 118 chemical symbols, indexed by atomic number. Index 0 is "X", an unknown element. ATOMIC_MASSES Standard atomic weights in amu, indexed by atomic number. Read-only. ELEMENT_DTYPE The polars type of the element column. atomic_numbers(symbols) Atomic numbers of chemical symbols. atomic_masses(elements) Atomic weights of symbols or atomic numbers. COVALENT_RADII, VDW_RADII Covalent and van der Waals radii in Å, indexed by atomic number; NaN where there is none. Read-only. covalent_radii(elements), vdw_radii(elements) The radii of symbols or atomic numbers; InvalidParameter for an element without one. element_from_mass(mass, *, tolerance=0.01, candidates=None) The element whose atomic weight matches a mass.

docs.title: The element column
docs.text:
Per-atom chemical symbols are stored with the polars type ELEMENT_DTYPE, an enumeration of SYMBOLS in order of atomic number. Each atom takes one byte, symbols are checked when the column is created, and the underlying integer of each value is its atomic number:

import polars as pl

s = pl.Series(["Cu", "Ni"], dtype=elements.ELEMENT_DTYPE)
s.to_physical()  # [29, 28]

docs.title: Identifying elements from masses
docs.text:
Some files, such as LAMMPS data files, give masses but no chemical symbols. element_from_mass returns the element whose atomic weight lies within tolerance (0.01 amu by default) of the mass, and raises InvalidParameter when no element or more than one element matches.

By default only elements with a standard atomic weight are considered: those with at least one stable isotope, H to Bi except Tc and Pm, and Th, Pa and U. No two of them have atomic weights within 0.02 amu of each other, so the match is unique. Other radioactive elements must be listed in candidates, because their atomic weights can be almost equal to another element's: ²⁰⁹Po and Bi differ by 0.002 amu, ²⁴⁷Cm and ²⁴⁷Bk by 0.00004 amu.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: These are the names MDAPY uses. Every module follows them, so a concept has one name everywhere.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Name Meaning System One atomic configuration: a Box, a table of per-atom properties and global information. Immutable: operations return a new System. Box The simulation box: three lattice vectors, an origin and periodicity flags. box.matrix (3, 3) array whose rows are the lattice vectors a, b, c. box.pbc (3,) bool array, True where the box is periodic. Trajectory A sequence of frames, read lazily. frame One System of a Trajectory. table The per-atom table of a System, a polars DataFrame with one row per atom. system["name"] The values of a column, a component or an expression over the columns, one per atom, as a read-only NumPy array. condition A Python expression over the columns of a system that System.filter keeps atoms by, such as "positions.z > 10 and element == 'Cu'". See Selecting and ordering atoms. component One value of an array column, written column.component: x, y, z for 3 values, x, y, z, w for 4, xx … zz by rows for 9, and the index from 0 for any number, such as positions.z or group.1. info Global information of a System, such as energy or timestep. NeighborList Pairs of atoms within a cutoff, the nearest neighbors of each atom, or the atoms that share a Voronoi face, including periodic images. pair One entry of a NeighborList: atoms i and j and the periodic image shifts of j. shifts Periodic image of the second atom of a pair, (3,) int8: the pair vector is x[j] - x[i] + shifts @ box.matrix. index_dtype Integer type of atom indices in results such as NeighborList.j: int32, or int64 in a build with 64-bit indices. TriangleMesh A mesh of triangles, which may cross the periodic boundaries of a box: vertices, faces and the periodic image shifts of each corner. Topology Bonds, angles, dihedrals and impropers of a system; each a table with atoms (0-based row indices), type and optional type_label. format Name of a file format, passed as format=, such as extxyz. See Reading and writing files. Calculator Interface that computes energy, forces and virial for a System. interop The module that converts to and from the objects of other packages: to_ase, from_ase, to_ase_calculator, from_ase_calculator, to_ovito, from_ovito, to_pymatgen, from_pymatgen, to_freud, from_freud. average atom The single species of an average-atom potential, standing for a random alloy; A in potential files. Result Base class of the objects returned by analyses. reference A reference configuration, for example in atomic strain analysis. unwrapped positions Positions moved by whole periodic images so that no cluster or molecule is cut by the periodic boundaries, or, along a trajectory, so that atoms move continuously through them; with an image column, the positions plus the image flags times the lattice vectors. affine transformation A map of positions x to M x + t, with a (3, 3) matrix M and a translation t: a rotation, shear, scaling or move, or a mix of them; vectors such as velocities turn with M alone. selection Some atoms of a system, given as a boolean mask of one value per atom or as their indices. mask (N,) bool, true for the atoms of a selection; System.where gives the mask of conditions, and analyses take one as atoms. overlapping atoms Atoms closer than a distance to another, such as the copies of an atom or the atoms where structures put together clash; find_overlapping selects them. spline A curve through values, cubic between neighboring points, whose first and second derivatives are continuous; Spline along a line and GridSpline on a grid. least squares A fit that makes the sum of the squared residuals, the values less the curve, as small as it can, each weighed by 1/σ² when the values have standard deviations σ; fit_polynomial, fit_surface, fit_curve. equation of state The energy of a crystal as a function of its volume, of four parameters: the energy and the volume at the minimum, the bulk modulus there and its derivative with respect to the pressure; fit_eos. orthogonal cell A box of the same crystal whose lattice vectors lie along x, y and z: along each, the shortest combination of the lattice vectors of the box that lies along it; orthogonal_cell makes one. copy One of the systems replicate places side by side; copy (i, j, l) of (na, nb, nc) is number i + na(j + nb l). lag The number of frames between two frames of a trajectory. time average The mean of a quantity over the frames of a trajectory, of each atom for a column of the atoms. time series A quantity in each frame of a trajectory, such as a column reduced to one number. reduction One number from the values of a column of the atoms, such as their mean or sum; reduce and its OPERATIONS. histogram The counts of the values of a column in bins of equal width. frame difference The change of a column of each atom from a reference frame, the atoms matched by id; the column <name>_change. frozen value The value a column has in a reference frame, given to the atoms of another by freeze; the column <name>_frozen. smoothed trajectory The frames of a trajectory with their positions and other real numbers averaged over a window of frames about each. trajectory line The path of an atom over the frames of a trajectory, followed through the periodic boundaries. combined system The atoms of two systems in one, in the box of the first, as combine makes it; OVITO calls it combining datasets. drift The motion of the center of mass of all the atoms, or of some, over a trajectory; remove_drift moves each frame to keep the center of mass where it is in a reference frame. file pattern A file name with *, standing for the files it matches, in the order of the numbers in their names, such as dump.*.lammpstrj. topology of a trajectory A system, usually read from a LAMMPS data file, whose bonds, charges, molecules and other columns the frames of a trajectory take, their atoms matched by id. spanning cluster A cluster that joins a periodic image of itself through its bonds, so that it has no unbroken position. ring A closed path of bonds through distinct atoms; a shortest-path ring has no two atoms closer through the network than along it. covalent bond A pair of atoms closer than the sum of their covalent radii and 0.45 Å, as pictures draw them. bond length distribution The counts of the lengths of the bonds of a topology, each measured to the nearest periodic image, in total and for each pair of elements. isosurface The surface where a field over the box, such as a binned property of the atoms, equals a level; it bounds the regions where the field is above it. voxel A cell of a grid that divides the box along its vectors, with the value of a field. coordination polyhedron The convex hull of the neighbors of an atom, such as the octahedron of oxygen about the titanium of a perovskite. vector arrow An arrow drawn from an atom along a vector of it, such as its displacement, velocity or force: a shaft and a head 2.5 times as wide and 4.5 times as long as the radius of the shaft. color column The color column of a system, (N, 3) sRGB from 0 to 1, that color_coding, color_by_type and assign_color set and render draws by default; a radius column likewise sets the radii. colormap A map of values to colors, one of COLORMAPS: rainbow, viridis, magma, jet, hot, blue_white_red and gray as OVITO computes them, plasma and coolwarm, and labels for discrete values. file of a frame Trajectory.file_of(i), the path of the file that holds frame i of a trajectory, without reading the frame. molecular polycrystal A polycrystal of whole molecules, from a unit with a molecule column: build_polycrystal. gradient polycrystal A polycrystal whose grain size changes along one direction, from the seeds of gradient_seeds. pressure-temperature diagram The stable phase of one element at each pressure and temperature, from the free energies of its phases: pressure_temperature_diagram, its boundaries with their slopes by the Clausius-Clapeyron relation. label colors LABEL_COLORS, twelve distinct colors given in turn to the values of a column colored by type or through the discrete colormap labels. type colors TYPE_COLORS, the nine colors of OVITO in turn for atom types without elements, named Type 1, Type 2 and so on by atom_names when drawn. global illumination Light that reaches a surface after bouncing off others, as the shiny style of pictures traces it. showing a picture show_image puts a picture from render, or a file, on the page of a notebook. style of a picture Its lights, shadows, occlusion and outlines together: fast (as the viewports of OVITO), matte (as its Tachyon renderer), shiny (after its OSPRay renderer) or flat (outlined, as ASE draws atoms). highlight The light of a lamp mirrored by a surface toward the viewer: a bright spot on a sphere. metalness From 0 to 1, how much a surface behaves as a metal: it reflects less light diffusely and its highlights take its color. depth of field In a picture through a lens, the range of depths that looks sharp around the plane in focus; nearer and farther things blur. soft shadow A shadow cast by a light of some size: dark where all of the light is hidden, fading where part of it is. ionic step One configuration of a VASP relaxation or molecular dynamics, with its energy, forces and virial; one frame of an OUTCAR file. training set Frames with reference energies, forces and virials, usually from DFT, in extended XYZ, to fit a machine-learned potential. SOAP The smooth overlap of atomic positions: the power spectrum of the Gaussian density of the neighbors of an atom, a descriptor of its neighborhood that does not change when it is turned, moved or reordered. structure descriptor The mean of the descriptors of the atoms of a frame, one point per frame. farthest point sampling Choosing points one by one, each the farthest from those chosen before. label A reference energy, force or virial of a frame, usually from DFT, that a model is trained to predict. parity plot The predictions of a model against the labels, one point each; on the diagonal where they agree. committee Several models of one system, such as models trained with other seeds; the spread of their predictions marks where they were not trained enough. model deviation The largest over the atoms of a frame of the spread of the forces of a committee, as DP-GEN chooses frames by it. novelty The distance of a frame from the nearest frame of a training set in the space of descriptors. net force The sum of the forces on all atoms of a frame: zero for a crystal or a cluster in vacuum. crystal cluster Neighboring atoms of one structure whose neighbors map onto each other by rotations of the lattice: one region with one lattice frame, as the dislocation analysis joins them. ideal vector The vector between two atoms in the perfect, unstrained crystal, in the lattice frame of a crystal cluster. spatial correlation function The mean of one property of the atoms at a place times another at a distance r from it, ⟨P₁(0) P₂(r)⟩; of two properties equal to 1, the radial distribution function. elastic strain The strain of the lattice about an atom of a crystal against the ideal crystal of given lattice constants, from the deformation gradient that maps the ideal vectors onto its neighbors; it leaves out the slip of dislocations. good tetrahedron A tetrahedron of the Delaunay tessellation whose six edges have ideal vectors that add up to zero around each face: crystal there maps onto the perfect lattice. interface mesh The triangles between the good tetrahedra and the rest, on which Burgers circuits run. Burgers circuit A closed path along the edges of the interface mesh; the sum of the ideal vectors of its edges is the Burgers vector of the dislocations it encloses. defect mesh The surface around the defects that are not dislocations: the interface mesh without the triangles the lines took, closed over their free ends. family of Burgers vectors The Burgers vectors of one kind, the same in any order and sign of their components, such as 1/2<110> or 1/6<112>.

docs.title: Names of functions and methods
docs.text:
• Analyses are classes named after what they compute, such as CommonNeighborAnalysis. Parameters are given to the constructor and validated there; compute(system, ...) returns a result object.
  • Changing a System uses with_* methods and select, which return a new System; a System itself has no other methods. Geometric transformations such as replicate and wrap are functions in mdapy.transform.
  • Building structures uses build_* functions.
  • Reading and writing uses read, write and read_trajectory.
  • Conversion to other packages lives in mdapy.interop, as to_* and from_* functions.
  • get_* only reads a value; it never starts a computation.

Units and sign conventions are listed in Units and conventions.

docs.text:

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text: MDAPY uses one unit system everywhere: in inputs, outputs, files written by MDAPY, and stored properties. Readers convert from a file's own units when reading, and writers convert back when writing.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Quantity Unit length Å energy eV time ps mass amu temperature K charge e velocity Å/ps force eV/Å stress, pressure GPa virial eV elastic moduli of 2D materials N/m frequency of vibrations THz

These match LAMMPS metal units except stress and pressure, which LAMMPS reports in bar. Files from GPUMD, which uses fs and Å/fs, are converted on reading and writing.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
The tables and the Python API give exact types, the same on every page:

Written Means float64, float32 a real number of 64 or 32 bits int8, int32, int64, uint8, uint64 an integer of that many bits (N, 3) float64 an array of that shape and type mdapy.index_dtype atom indices: int32, or int64 in MDAPY built with 64-bit atom indices indices an array of atom indices, of any integer type

As an argument, a Python float is a float64, a Python int stands for an int32 or int64 that holds it, and lists and arrays of other numeric types are converted. Pictures are computed in float32, so their options are given as float32.

docs.title: Sign conventions
docs.text:
• Stress is positive under tension: \(\sigma_{\alpha\beta} = \frac{1}{V}\frac{\partial E}{\partial \varepsilon_{\alpha\beta}}\).
  • Pressure is \(p = -\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\sigma\), positive under compression.
  • Virial is \(W = -V\sigma\), in eV, positive under compression (the GPUMD convention).
  • Voigt order of symmetric tensors is xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy.
  • Burgers vectors are those of OVITO's dislocation analysis: along the sense of the line, the sum of the steps of a counterclockwise circuit around it in the perfect crystal, the opposite of Hirth and Lothe's (FS/RH). The structure builder puts dislocations in by the same.

docs.title: Conversion factors
docs.text:
All conversions in MDAPY use the constants in mdapy.units. A factor named A_TO_B converts a value in unit A to unit B by multiplication:

from mdapy import units

stress_ev_per_a3 = 0.01
stress_gpa = stress_ev_per_a3 * units.EV_PER_A3_TO_GPA  # 1.602 GPa

The defining constants are the exact 2019 SI values (elementary charge, Boltzmann, Planck and Avogadro constants); the atomic mass constant is the CODATA 2022 value.

docs.title: build_crystal
docs.text:
build_crystal(structure, a, *, c=None, elements='X', orientation=None, repeat=(1, 1, 1))

A perfect crystal in a periodic box, optionally along chosen crystal directions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default structure str

One of mdapy.build.STRUCTURES: "sc", "bcc", "fcc", "diamond", "cscl", "rocksalt", "zincblende", "fluorite", "l1_2", "perovskite", "hcp", "wurtzite", "lonsdaleite", "graphite" or "graphene".

required a float64

Lattice constant in Å.

required c float64

Lattice constant c of a hexagonal structure in Å; by default the ideal sqrt(8/3) a, and needed for graphite and graphene.

None elements str or sequence of str

The element of every atom, or of each sublattice of the structure. Default "X".

'X' orientation sequence of three directions

The crystal directions along the three box vectors: [hkl] in the cubic cell, orthogonal; or [uvw] or [hkil] in the hexagonal cell, linearly independent. Default the cell itself.

None repeat int32 or sequence of 3 int32

Number of periods along each box vector, or along all three. Default (1, 1, 1).

(1, 1, 1)

Returns:

Type Description System

The crystal, ordered by z, then y, then x.

docs.title: random_alloy
docs.text:
random_alloy(system, fractions, *, seed=None)

The system with its elements drawn at random in given fractions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The sites, for example a crystal from build_crystal.

required fractions mapping of str to float64

Fraction of each element, positive; they are normalized to sum to 1.

required seed int64 or Generator

Seed of the random order; the same seed gives the same alloy.

None

Returns:

Type Description System

The system with a new element column. The number of atoms of each element is its fraction of the atoms, rounded so that the counts add up, the largest remainders rounded up.

docs.title: sqs_alloy
docs.text:
sqs_alloy(system, fractions, *, shells=3, weights=None, steps=100000, temperature=1.0, seed=None, progress=None, cancel=None)

A special quasirandom structure: elements in given fractions on the sites of a perfect lattice, arranged so that the pairs of the nearest shells of neighbors are those of a random alloy.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The sites, a perfect lattice such as from build_crystal.

required fractions mapping of str to float64

Fraction of each element, positive; normalized to sum to 1, with the counts of random_alloy.

required shells int32

The number of shells of neighbors made random, 1 to 10. Default 3.

3 weights sequence of float64

The weight of each shell in the deviation minimized. Default all 1.

None steps int64

Number of swaps of two atoms tried. Default 100000.

100000 temperature float64

The starting temperature of the annealing, in units of the typical change of a swap; 0 accepts only improvements. Default 1.

1.0 seed int64 or Generator

Seed of the starting alloy and of the swaps.

None

Returns:

Type Description System

The system with a new element column.

docs.title: insert_dislocation
docs.text:
insert_dislocation(system, burgers, *, line=2, normal=1, center=None, poisson=1 / 3, elastic=None, orientation=None)

The system with a straight dislocation along a box axis, its atoms displaced as isotropic or anisotropic elasticity predicts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The atoms.

required burgers array_like

(3,) float64 Burgers vector in Å, in the plane of cut: its part along line is the screw part, the rest the edge part.

required line int32 or str

The Cartesian axis along the dislocation line, 0, 1, 2 or x, y, z. Default z.

2 normal int32 or str

The Cartesian axis normal to the plane of cut, other than line. Default y.

1 center array_like

(3,) float64, a point of the dislocation line in Å. Default the center of the box.

None poisson float64

Poisson's ratio, from -1 to below 0.5, for isotropic elasticity. Default 1/3.

1 / 3 elastic array_like of float64

Elastic constants of a cubic crystal for anisotropic elasticity: (C11, C12, C44) or the (6, 6) Voigt matrix, in any unit, in the axes of the cubic cell. Default isotropic elasticity.

None orientation array_like

The crystal directions along x, y and z, orthogonal, with elastic. Default the axes of the cubic cell.

None

Returns:

Type Description System

The same atoms, displaced; the box is unchanged.

docs.text:
edge_dislocation(cell, repeat)

An edge dislocation between two crystals, with one more period along x below its line than above.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cell System

An orthogonal periodic cell whose period along x is the Burgers vector, such as fcc along [1-10], [11-2], [111].

required repeat tuple of int32

(nx, ny, nz): above the line nx periods along x, below it nx + 1; ny along y, the line; nz along z in all, at least 2.

required

Returns:

Type Description System

The lower crystal compressed and the upper one stretched along x to nx + 1/2 periods, in a box periodic along x and y but not z; the line lies between them, at the middle of x.

docs.title: Dislocation dataclass
docs.text:
Dislocation(structure, orientation, burgers, *, partial=False, core=(0.5, 0.5))

A straight dislocation in a cubic crystal.

Attributes:

Name Type Description structure str

A cubic structure of build_crystal, such as "bcc", "fcc" or "diamond".

orientation tuple of three directions

The crystal directions along x, y and z, orthogonal and right-handed: x in the glide plane, y normal to it, z along the line.

burgers tuple of float64

The Burgers vector in the axes of the cubic cell, in units of the lattice constant, in the glide plane: the one the dislocation analysis, as OVITO's, finds along +z.

partial bool

A single Shockley partial, which bounds a stacking fault on its -x side. Default False.

core tuple of float64

Where the line lies: (s, t), s rows of atoms along x from a row of the plane of atoms below it and t of the way to the plane above. Default (0.5, 0.5).

docs.title: build_polycrystal
docs.text:
build_polycrystal(unit, box, grains, *, orientations=None, min_distance=None, seed=None)

A polycrystal: each grain the crystal of a unit cell, rotated, filling the Voronoi cell of its seed in a periodic box. With a molecule column in the unit, the molecules stay whole.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default unit System

The crystal of every grain, in a periodic box: a unit cell or any periodic arrangement, such as twin lamellae. Its other columns, such as charges, are kept. With a molecule column, a molecule belongs to the grain that holds its center, the atoms too close are removed by whole molecules, and the topology is kept; a molecule must be shorter than half the box of the unit.

required box Box or array_like

The box of the polycrystal, periodic in every direction: a Box or its lattice vectors. Along an axis no longer than the box of unit, the polycrystal is columnar: every grain spans that axis, its box takes the length of the unit there, and the grains turn about it.

required grains int32 or array_like

Number of grains, with seeds at random positions, or the (G, 3) positions of the seeds in Å.

required orientations array_like

(G, 3, 3) float64 rotation of each grain, taking the axes of unit to those of the box; in a columnar polycrystal rotations about its axis. Uniformly random by default.

None min_distance float64

No two atoms stay closer than this, in Å, with as few removed as possible, as mdapy.neighbor.find_overlapping does: atoms of neighboring grains that come too close, and the copies of atoms on the faces of a cell. Default 0.7 times the nearest distance in unit, between different molecules if there are any.

None seed int64 or Generator

Seed of the random seeds and orientations.

None

Returns:

Type Description System

The atoms with a grain column, numbered as the seeds; each seed is a site of the unit in its grain. info["seeds"] holds the (G, 3) positions of the seeds. With molecules, molecule numbers them from 1, and image tells how to put together those the box wraps.

docs.title: check_calculator
docs.text:
check_calculator(calculator, system, *, displacement=0.0001, rtol=1e-06, atol=1e-06, num_atoms=3, seed=0)

Checks that a calculator is consistent with itself and with physics.

The checks are: atomic energies and atomic virials sum to the energy and the virial; forces and the virial agree with finite differences of the energy; translation, rotation and reordering of the atoms change nothing beyond rotating vectors; a doubled cell has twice the energy (for systems periodic along a); and a neighbor list given to the calculator gives the same result.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default calculator Calculator

The calculator.

required system System

A small system, a few dozen atoms, that the calculator handles.

required displacement float64

Step in Å (and strain step) of the finite differences.

0.0001 rtol float64

Relative and absolute tolerances of the comparisons, in the units of each quantity.

1e-06 atol float64

Relative and absolute tolerances of the comparisons, in the units of each quantity.

1e-06 num_atoms int32

Number of atoms whose forces are checked by finite differences.

3 seed int32

Seed of the random rotation, translation and atom choice.

0

Raises:

Type Description AssertionError

If a check fails; the message names it and the largest deviation.

ChemicalSpecies(radii='covalent', *, scale=None, tolerance=None, cutoffs=None)

Molecules: atoms joined by bonds shorter than their radii allow, and their chemical formulas.

Two atoms of radii r_i and r_j are bonded when closer than scale * (r_i + r_j) + tolerance, or than the cutoff given for their pair of elements.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default radii (covalent, vdw)

The radius of each element: the covalent radii (Cordero et al. 2008), as Jmol bonds atoms; the van der Waals radii (Alvarez 2013), as VMD and OVITO bond atoms, two hydrogen atoms never bonded unless cutoffs say so; or radii in Å by element. Default "covalent".

"covalent" scale float64

Factor on the sum of the radii. Default 0.6 with van der Waals radii, 1 otherwise.

None tolerance float64

Length added to it, in Å. Default 0.45 with covalent radii, 0 otherwise.

None cutoffs dict

Bond length in Å for pairs of elements (a, b), in either order, instead of the radii; 0 for pairs never bonded.

None

remove_drift(frames, reference=0, *, atoms=None, unwrap=True)

The frames of a trajectory moved so that the center of mass of the atoms stays where it is in a reference frame, as OVITO's center of mass correction.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frames sequence of System

The same atoms in every frame, such as a Trajectory: matched by the id column where the first frame has one, else in the same order. The masses are the mass column of the first frame, else those of its elements, else all equal.

required reference int32

The frame whose center of mass is kept. Default 0.

0 atoms array_like

A boolean mask or indices of the atoms of the first frame whose center of mass is kept. Default all.

None unwrap bool

Follow the atoms through the periodic boundaries to find the center of mass (True, default), or take the positions as they are.

True

Returns:

Type Description sequence of System

The frames, read when they are used, each with all its atoms moved by one translation; the boxes do not move. Its shifts are the (T, 3) translations in Å.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

If there are no frames, the reference frame is not one of them, no atoms are chosen or their masses add up to zero, or the frames do not hold the same atoms.

docs.title: smooth_trajectory
docs.text:
smooth_trajectory(frames, window)

The positions and other real numbers of each frame averaged over a window of frames about it, the atoms followed through the periodic boundaries, as OVITO's smooth trajectory.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frames sequence of System

The same atoms in every frame, such as a Trajectory: matched by the id column where the frames have one, else in the same order. Without an image column, atoms must move less than half the box between frames.

required window int32

The number of frames averaged: the frame, (window - 1) // 2 frames before it and window // 2 after it, the first and last frames repeated beyond the ends; 1 leaves the positions as they are.

required

Returns:

Type Description sequence of System

The frames, each computed when it is used: the mean positions about the atoms of that frame, the mean of every other column of real numbers (velocities, forces, values of analyses) matched by atom; columns of integers or text as they are.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

If the window is not a positive integer or there are no frames.

docs.title: Spline
docs.text:
Spline(x, y, *, boundary='not-a-knot', slopes=None, extrapolate=False)

A cubic spline through values at points on a line: piecewise cubic, with continuous first and second derivatives, through every point.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x array_like

(n,) float64 points, strictly increasing, two or more.

required y array_like

(n,) float64 values at the points, or (n, m) for m curves through the same points.

required boundary str

At the two ends: "not-a-knot", the third derivative continuous at the second and the second-last point; "natural", second derivatives zero; "clamped", first derivatives given by slopes; "periodic", a periodic curve whose first and last values are equal. Default "not-a-knot".

'not-a-knot' slopes array_like

(2,) or (2, m) float64 first derivatives at the two ends, for "clamped".

None extrapolate bool

Continue the end cubics beyond the points; otherwise values there are NaN, or for "periodic" repeat with the period. Default False.

False

Attributes:

Name Type Description x ndarray

(n,) float64 points.

y ndarray

(n,) or (n, m) float64 values.

boundary str

The condition at the ends.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For points that are not strictly increasing, values of another length, an unknown boundary, slopes that are missing or of the wrong shape, or periodic values whose ends differ.

required boundary str or sequence of 2 str

The condition at the ends along each axis, as for Spline, except "clamped"; "periodic" for a surface repeating with the grid, such as an energy over the cells of a lattice. Default "not-a-knot".

'not-a-knot' extrapolate bool

False

Raises:

docs.text:
fit_curve(model, x, y, guess=None, *, sigma=None, absolute_sigma=False, max_steps=500, tolerance=1e-12)

The parameters of a function that fit values best, by the Levenberg-Marquardt method of nonlinear least squares.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model Model or callable

One of MODELS, a Model, or a function f(x, *parameters).

required x array_like

The points, as the function takes them: (n,) float64, or for a function of several variables any array it takes.

required y array_like

(n,) float64 values at the points.

required guess array_like

(p,) float64 first guess of the parameters; by default the guess of the model, which a plain function must be given.

None sigma array_like

(n,) float64 standard deviations of the values; all equal by default.

None absolute_sigma bool

As for fit_polynomial. Default False.

False max_steps int32

The most steps. Default 500.

500 tolerance float64

The fit has converged when a step changes the sum of squares by less than this fraction of it. Default 1e-12.

1e-12

Returns:

Type Description CurveFit

The parameters, their errors and covariance, and the residuals.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For values that are not finite, a plain function without a guess, a function whose values are not finite at the guess, or a fit that does not converge within max_steps.

docs.title: exponential module-attribute
docs.text: exponential = Model('exponential', lambda x, amplitude, time: amplitude * np.exp(-x / time), ('amplitude', 'time'), _guess_exponential)

docs.title: stretched_exponential module-attribute

GrainSegmentation(threshold=None, *, method='graph', min_grain_size=100, stacking_faults=True, adopt_orphans=True, structures=('fcc', 'hcp', 'bcc'), rmsd_cutoff=0.1)

Grains of a polycrystal: groups of crystalline atoms of nearly the same lattice orientation, from polyhedral template matching, as OVITO's Grain segmentation modifier finds them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default threshold float64

With method="graph", the largest log merge distance of the merges kept; by default chosen from the merges. With method="spanning_tree", the largest misorientation in degrees, needed.

None method str

"graph": clusters merged by node pair sampling of the graph of bonds weighted by their misorientation; "spanning_tree": merged along the bonds of least misorientation. Default "graph".

'graph' min_grain_size int64

Clusters of fewer atoms are no grains. Default 100.

100 stacking_faults bool

The atoms of stacking faults and twin boundaries, hcp in fcc and hexagonal in cubic diamond or the other way round, join the grains around them. Default True.

True adopt_orphans bool

Atoms in no grain join the grain nearest along their bonds. Default True.

True structures iterable of str

The structures polyhedral template matching looks for. Default fcc, hcp and bcc.

('fcc', 'hcp', 'bcc') rmsd_cutoff float64

Atoms whose root-mean-square deviation from the best template is larger are of no structure; 0 for no cutoff. Default 0.1.

Bases: Result

The grains of a polycrystal.

Attributes:

Name Type Description grain ndarray

(N,) int64 grain of each atom, an index into the arrays of the grains, -1 for none.

sizes ndarray

(G,) int64 number of atoms of each grain; the grains are ranked by size before the atoms in no grain join them.

structure ndarray

(G,) int8 structure of each grain, an index into names.

names tuple of str

Names of the structures, those of polyhedral template matching.

orientation ndarray

(G, 4) float64 mean lattice orientation of each grain as a quaternion (x, y, z, w).

center ndarray

(G, 3) float64 center of mass of each grain in Å, inside the box.

radius ndarray

(G,) float64 radius in Å of the smallest sphere about the center that holds the grain.

radius_of_gyration ndarray

(G,) float64 radius of gyration in Å.

colors ndarray

(G, 3) float64, a color for each grain, RGB from 0 to 1.

threshold float64

The threshold applied: the log merge distance of graph clustering, or the misorientation in degrees of the spanning tree.

merge_distance ndarray

(M,) float64 merge distance (graph clustering) or misorientation in degrees (spanning tree) of each merge of two clusters of at least 20 atoms, in the order of the merges.

merge_size ndarray

(M,) float64 number of atoms of the smaller cluster of each of these merges.

docs.text:
elastic_constants(system, calculator, *, strain=0.001, relax=True, max_force=0.0001, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None)

Elastic constants from the stress under small strains.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The crystal, periodic in every direction, or a sheet: periodic along two vectors in the x-y plane and not along a third along z. Best at zero stress (relax its box first with minimize(..., cell="full")).

required calculator Calculator

Computes the virial, and energies and forces to relax the positions.

required strain float64

Magnitude of the strains applied in each direction, positive and negative; shear strains are engineering strains. Default 1e-3.

0.001 relax bool

Relax the positions under each strain. Default True.

True max_force float64

Convergence of each relaxation in eV/Å. Default 1e-4.

0.0001 max_steps int32

Largest number of steps of each relaxation. Default 5000.

5000 symmetry bool

Take the stress under a strain that a symmetry operation of the crystal, found by spglib, makes from another one as the image of its stress: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed.

None

Returns:

Type Description ElasticResult or SheetElasticResult

The (6, 6) elastic constants in GPa; of a sheet, the (3, 3) elastic constants in N/m.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

If the box is neither periodic nor that of a sheet, the strain is not positive, the calculator has no virial, a relaxation does not converge, or symmetry is True without spglib.

docs.title: thermal_elastic_constants
docs.text:
thermal_elastic_constants(qha, calculator, *, method='quasi-harmonic', strain=0.005, supercell=None, mesh=20, displacement=0.01, max_force=1e-06, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None)

Isothermal and adiabatic elastic constants of a crystal at the temperatures of a quasi-harmonic calculation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default qha QuasiHarmonicResult

The quasi-harmonic calculation of the crystal, with its cells; the cells around the volumes of its temperatures are strained.

required calculator Calculator

Computes energies and forces, as in the quasi-harmonic calculation.

required method (quasi - harmonic, quasi - static)

Second derivatives with respect to strain of the static energy and the free energy of the vibrations, from phonons of strained cells, or of the static energy alone, at the volume of each temperature. Default "quasi-harmonic".

"quasi-harmonic" strain float64

Magnitude of the Lagrangian strains of the finite differences. Default 5e-3.

0.005 supercell optional

Of the phonons of the strained cells, as in phonons and Phonons.thermal.

None mesh optional

Of the phonons of the strained cells, as in phonons and Phonons.thermal.

None displacement optional

Of the phonons of the strained cells, as in phonons and Phonons.thermal.

None max_force float64

Convergence of the relaxation of the positions in each strained cell in eV/Å. Default 1e-6.

1e-06 max_steps int32

Largest number of steps of each relaxation. Default 5000.

5000 symmetry bool

Compute one of each set of strains that the symmetry operations of the cells, found by spglib, make from each other, and use symmetry in the phonons too: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed.

None

Returns:

Type Description ThermalElasticResult

The isothermal and adiabatic elastic constants at each temperature.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For an unknown method, a strain that is not positive, a result without cells, a relaxation that does not converge, a pair of atoms that reaches the cutoff of the calculator between the strained cells of the quasi-harmonic method, imaginary frequencies in a strained cell, or symmetry True without spglib.

Isothermal elastic constants of a crystal at a temperature, from the mean stress of molecular dynamics in LAMMPS under small strains.

0.0 strain float64

0.01 timestep float64

Time step in ps. Default 0.001.

0.001 equilibration int32

Steps before each average. Default 10000.

10000 production int32

Steps of each average. Default 20000.

20000 every int32

Steps between the stresses and boxes averaged. Default 10.

10 blocks int32

Number of blocks of each average for its standard error. Default 5.

5 barostat (iso, aniso, tri)

How the box changes while it finds its mean shape under pressure. Default "tri".

docs.title: phonons
docs.text:
phonons(system, calculator, *, supercell=None, displacement=0.01, symmetry=None)

Harmonic phonons of a crystal, from the forces on atoms displaced in a supercell.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The cell of the crystal, periodic in every direction, or of a sheet, periodic along two vectors in the x-y plane and not along a third along z, with atoms at rest (relax it first); best its primitive cell. Each atom needs an element or a mass.

required calculator Calculator

Computes the forces.

required supercell int32 or array_like

Repeats of the cell along its vectors, one or three, or a (3, 3) integer matrix whose rows times the vectors of the cell are the vectors of the supercell; a sheet repeats along its plane only, and one integer means both of its vectors. Default the supercell nearest a cube that is at least twice the cutoff of the calculator thick in every direction, nearest a square across the plane for a sheet.

None displacement float64

Displacement of the atoms in Å. Default 0.01.

0.01 symmetry bool

Move only the atoms and along the directions that the symmetry of the cell, found by spglib, does not relate to others: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed.

None

Returns:

Type Description Phonons

The force constants, which give frequencies, polarization vectors, band structures, densities of states and thermal properties.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

If the box is neither periodic nor that of a sheet, there are no atoms, an atom has no mass, the calculator does not compute forces, the supercell is not positive integers or a matrix of them with a positive determinant, the displacement is not positive, or symmetry is True without spglib.

docs.title: Phonons
docs.text:
Phonons(cell, supercell, force_constants, masses, reference=None)

Harmonic phonons of a crystal from its force constants.

Made by phonons. Wave vectors are in units of the reciprocal lattice vectors of the cell: q = (h, k, l) is h b1 + k b2 + l b3 with a_i · b_j = 2π δ_ij.

Attributes:

Name Type Description cell System

The crystal whose vibrations these are.

supercell ndarray

(3, 3) int64 matrix of the supercell in which the force constants were found: its vectors are the rows of the matrix times the vectors of the cell.

force_constants ndarray

(n, n S, 3, 3) float64 second derivatives of the energy in eV/Å² with respect to the positions of each atom of the cell and of each atom of the supercell, which holds S cells, each with the atoms of the cell in their order, the first cell that of the cell itself.

docs.title: thermal_phonons
docs.text:
thermal_phonons(cell, potential, temperature, *, supercell=None, pressure=0.0, timestep=0.001, equilibration=10.0, production=100.0, num_frames=200, symmetry=None, seed=1, progress=None, cancel=None)

Phonons of a crystal at a temperature, from molecular dynamics in LAMMPS: the force constants that best give the forces on the moving atoms, which change with the temperature as the vibrations feel the crystal further from its minimum.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cell System

The cell of the crystal, relaxed, with an element column, periodic in every direction; best its primitive cell.

required potential LAMMPS

The interaction.

required temperature float64

Temperature in K, positive.

required supercell int32 or array_like

Repeats of the cell along its vectors, one or three, or a (3, 3) integer matrix. Default the supercell nearest a cube that is at least twice the cutoff of the potential thick in every direction.

None pressure float64 or None

Pressure in GPa at which the box takes its mean size first; None to keep the box of cell. Default 0.

0.0 timestep float64

Time step in ps. Default 0.001.

0.001 equilibration float64

Time in ps of each equilibration. Default 10.

10.0 production float64

Time in ps over which the frames are taken. Default 100.

100.0 num_frames int32

Number of frames. Default 200.

200 symmetry bool

Average the force constants over the symmetry operations of the cell, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed.

None seed int32

Seed of the random numbers, positive. Default 1.

1 progress callable

Called as progress(done, total) with the steps run.

None cancel CancelToken

Stops the calculation, which raises mdapy.errors.Cancelled.

None

Returns:

Type Description Phonons

The phonons, whose cell has the mean box at this temperature.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For invalid options, a box not periodic in every direction, too few frames, or if LAMMPS fails.

MissingProperty

If the system has no element column.

Cancelled

If cancelled.

docs.title: phonons_from_frames
docs.text:
phonons_from_frames(cell, frames, *, supercell, symmetry=None)

Phonons from atoms displaced in a supercell and the forces on them, from molecular dynamics of any kind: the force constants that best give the forces, which hold the temperature of the frames.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cell System

The cell of the crystal, periodic in every direction, with the atoms at their places at the volume of the frames, each with an element or a mass; best its primitive cell.

required frames iterable of System

The atoms of the supercell, in its order, with a forces column: cells in the order of Phonons.force_constants, as phonons makes them; far enough apart in time to differ.

required supercell int32 or array_like

Repeats of the cell along its vectors, one or three, or a (3, 3) integer matrix whose rows times the vectors of the cell are the vectors of the supercell.

required symmetry bool

Average the force constants over the symmetry operations of the cell, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed.

None

Returns:

Type Description Phonons

The force constants, which give frequencies, polarization vectors, band structures, densities of states and thermal properties.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

If the box is not periodic, an atom has no mass, the supercell is not valid, a frame has another number of atoms, or there are too few frames for the force constants.

MissingProperty

If a frame has no forces column.

docs.title: quasi_harmonic
docs.text:
quasi_harmonic(system, calculator, temperatures, *, volumes=None, pressures=None, pressure=0.0, supercell=None, mesh=20, displacement=0.01, max_force=1e-06, max_stress=0.0001, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None)

Thermodynamic properties of a crystal in the quasi-harmonic approximation: harmonic phonons at several volumes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The cell of the crystal, periodic in every direction, best relaxed and primitive. Each atom needs an element or a mass.

required calculator Calculator

Computes energies and forces.

required temperatures array_like of float64

Temperatures in K, not negative.

required volumes array_like of float64

The volumes at which to compute the phonons, five or more, as ratios to the volume of system; at each the box keeps its volume while its shape and the positions relax. Default 9 from 0.97 to 1.09.

None pressures array_like of float64

Instead of volumes, the pressures in GPa under which the box and the positions relax, five or more.

None pressure float64

Pressure in GPa. Default 0.

0.0 supercell int32 or array_like

Repeats of the cell for the phonons, as in phonons.

None mesh int32 or array_like

Mesh of wave vectors for the thermal properties. Default 20.

20 displacement float64

Displacement of the atoms for the force constants in Å. Default 0.01.

0.01 max_force float64

Convergence of the relaxation at each volume in eV/Å. Default 1e-6.

1e-06 max_stress float64

Convergence of the relaxation of the box under each pressure in GPa. Default 1e-4.

0.0001 max_steps int32

Largest number of steps of each relaxation. Default 5000.

5000 symmetry bool

Use the symmetry of the cells in the phonons, as in phonons. Default whenever spglib is installed.

None

Returns:

Type Description QuasiHarmonicResult

Per atom: the equilibrium volume, Gibbs energy, entropy, bulk modulus, thermal expansion and heat capacity at each temperature, and the static and vibrational energies at each volume.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For a box not periodic in every direction, a negative temperature, both volumes and pressures, fewer than five of them, a relaxation that does not converge, a pair of atoms that reaches the cutoff of the calculator between the volumes, imaginary frequencies at a volume, or an equilibrium volume outside the volumes.

docs.title: SteinhardtParameters
docs.text:
SteinhardtParameters(degrees=(4, 6), *, num_neighbors=None, cutoff=None, voronoi=False, weighted=False, average=False, solid=False, solid_degree=6, bond_threshold=0.7, min_solid_bonds=7)

Steinhardt bond-orientational order parameters q_l.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default degrees sequence of int32

The degrees l, from 0 to 20. Default (4, 6).

(4, 6) num_neighbors int32

The neighbors of an atom are its num_neighbors nearest; default 12 unless cutoff or voronoi is given.

None cutoff float64

The neighbors of an atom are those closer than cutoff, in Å.

None voronoi bool

The neighbors of an atom are those that share a face of its Voronoi cell. Default False.

False weighted bool

With voronoi, weight each neighbor by the area of its face. Default False.

False average bool

Average the harmonics of each atom with those of its neighbors first (Lechner and Dellago). Default False.

False solid bool

Also tell solid-like atoms from liquid-like ones by their bonds (ten Wolde, Ruiz-Montero and Frenkel). Default False.

False solid_degree int32

With solid, the degree l of the harmonics of the bonds. Default 6.

6 bond_threshold float64

With solid, a bond is solid-like when the normalized product of the harmonics of its two atoms exceeds it. Default 0.7.

0.7 min_solid_bonds int32

With solid, an atom is solid-like with at least so many solid-like bonds. Default 7.

7

Minimizes the energy over the positions, and optionally the box, with FIRE 2.0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The starting configuration, with a mass or an element column; a movable column, (N, 3) bool, keeps each atom still along the directions where it is False.

required calculator Calculator

Computes energies and forces, and the virial when the box relaxes.

required max_force float64

Convergence: the largest force on any atom, in eV/Å. Default 1e-3.

0.1 timestep float64

0.001 cell (None, isotropic, axes, full)

How the box may change along its periodic directions: not at all (default), by one scale factor, by a scale factor along each Cartesian axis, or by any strain without rotation.

0.0 max_stress float64

0.01 save_every int32

Keeps the configuration every this many steps, with the first and the last, in frames of the result. Default None, keeping none.

None callback callable

Called after every step as callback(step, system, energy, max_force); returning True stops the minimization.

Lists of nearest and of Voronoi neighbors have as cutoff the largest distance, slightly enlarged.

docs.title: free_energy
docs.text:
free_energy(system, potential, temperatures, *, phase='solid', pressure=0.0, timestep=0.001, equilibration=10.0, switching=50.0, scan=100.0, repeats=1, mixing=False, melt_temperature=None, barostat=None, seed=1, progress=None, cancel=None)

The free energy of a solid or a liquid, per atom, from molecular dynamics in LAMMPS, with classical atoms.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default system System

The atoms, with an element column, in a box periodic in every direction: for a solid at their places in the crystal (relax them first), for a liquid anywhere, as it is melted first.

required potential LAMMPS

The interaction. A liquid needs one pair style, not a hybrid.

required temperatures float64 or array_like

Temperatures in K, positive. The free energy is calculated at the first, and followed from there to the others, which must lie on one side of it, in order.

required phase (solid, liquid)

The phase. Default "solid".

"solid" pressure float64 or None

Pressure in GPa for the Gibbs energy; None for the Helmholtz energy in the box of system. Default 0.

0.0 timestep float64

Time step in ps. Default 0.001.

0.001 equilibration float64

Time in ps of each equilibration. Default 10.

10.0 switching float64

Time in ps of each switching between two interactions. Default 50.

50.0 scan float64

Time in ps of each run between the first and the last temperature. Default 100.

100.0 repeats int32

Independent calculations at the first temperature. Default 1.

1 mixing bool

Add the ideal entropy of mixing of a random solid solution, whose atoms do not exchange places in the dynamics. A liquid has it by itself. Default False.

False melt_temperature float64

Temperature in K at which a liquid is melted. Default twice the first temperature.

None barostat (iso, aniso, tri)

How the box of a solid changes, as in MolecularDynamics.run. Default "aniso", and "iso" for a liquid.

"iso" seed int32

Seed of the random numbers, positive. Default 1.

1 progress callable

Called as progress(done, total) with the steps run.

None cancel CancelToken

Stops the calculation, which raises mdapy.errors.Cancelled.

None

Returns:

Type Description FreeEnergyResult

The free energy, enthalpy, entropy and volume per atom at each temperature. A phase that changes on the way, as a crystal melts when it is too hot, leaves out the temperatures from there on, with a warning.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For invalid options, a box not periodic in every direction, a hybrid pair style for a liquid, a liquid that does not move as one, a phase that changes in every scan, or if LAMMPS fails.

MissingProperty

If the system has no element column.

Cancelled

If cancelled.

docs.title: melting_point
docs.text:
melting_point(crystal, potential, temperature, *, pressure=0.0, num_atoms=16000, repeat=None, timestep=0.001, equilibration=10.0, coexistence=500.0, tolerance=3.0, max_runs=8, barostat_damping=None, seed=1, progress=None, cancel=None)

The melting point of a crystal, from a first guess, by the two-phase method: a solid and a liquid share a box at constant enthalpy, where they reach their common temperature while the interface between them moves. A run in which one phase takes over gives a new guess, until the two last.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default crystal System

The crystal, relaxed, with an element column, in a box periodic in every direction; the interface between the phases is across its third vector.

required potential LAMMPS

The interaction.

required temperature float64

The first guess in K, positive.

required pressure float64

Pressure in GPa. Default 0.

0.0 num_atoms int32

About how many atoms the box holds, three times as long along its third vector as along the others. Default 16000; fewer for a slow potential, at the price of a larger spread between runs.

16000 repeat array_like

(3,) int32 repeats of crystal along its vectors, instead of num_atoms; the third is made even.

None timestep float64

Time step in ps. Default 0.001.

0.001 equilibration float64

Time in ps of each stage before the two phases meet. Default 10.

10.0 coexistence float64

Time in ps of each stretch of the two phases, of which a run has two or more, up to five, while the temperature drifts. Default 500; a larger box needs longer, as heat takes longer to cross it.

500.0 tolerance float64

How much in K the temperature may still drift, from the third quarter of a stretch of coexistence to the last and from the stretch before to this one, for it to be the answer; twice its statistical error, if that is larger. Default 3.

3.0 max_runs int32

Largest number of runs. Default 8.

8 barostat_damping float64

Damping time of the barostat in ps, as in MolecularDynamics.run. Default 1000 time steps.

None seed int32

Seed of the random numbers, positive. Default 1.

1 progress callable

Called as progress(done, total) with the steps run, of a total that takes every run to be the last.

None cancel CancelToken

Stops the calculation, which raises mdapy.errors.Cancelled.

None

Returns:

Type Description MeltingPointResult

The melting point, its error, the runs, and the temperature, pressure and fraction of solid atoms along the last run.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For invalid options, a box not periodic in every direction, if half of the crystal does not melt, if no run ends with two phases within max_runs, or if LAMMPS fails.

MissingProperty

If the system has no element column.

Cancelled

If cancelled.

docs.title: binary_phase_diagram
docs.text:
binary_phase_diagram(phases, temperatures, *, elements=('A', 'B'), points=1001, degree=4)

The phase diagram of two elements from free energies per atom, at constant pressure: at each temperature the stable phases at each composition lie on the lower convex hull of the free energies of all phases.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default phases mapping of str to mapping of float64

For each phase, its free energies by the fraction of the second element: each a FreeEnergyResult, or a pair of (T,) temperatures in K and (T,) free energies in eV per atom. A phase of one fraction is a compound of that composition. A phase of more is a solution between its lowest and its highest fractions: the free energy minus that of ideal mixing, at each temperature, is a polynomial of the fraction.

required temperatures array_like

(T,) the temperatures of the diagram in K, positive; beyond those of a free energy, it goes on along a straight line.

required elements sequence of 2 str

The elements, for the labels. Default ("A", "B").

('A', 'B') points int32

Number of fractions from 0 to 1. Default 1001.

1001 degree int32

Largest degree of the polynomials. Default 4.

4

Returns:

Type Description BinaryPhaseDiagram

The stable phase at each temperature and fraction, and the tie lines.

Raises:

Type Description InvalidParameter

For no phases, a fraction out of range, no phase at some fraction, invalid temperatures, points or degree.

docs.title: units
docs.text:
Physical constants and unit conversion factors.

MDAPY works in one unit system: length in Å, energy in eV, time in ps, mass in amu, temperature in K, charge in e, force in eV/Å, stress and pressure in GPa. Every conversion in the package uses the factors defined here.

A factor named A_TO_B converts a value expressed in unit A into unit B by multiplication.

docs.title: ELEMENTARY_CHARGE module-attribute
docs.text:
ELEMENTARY_CHARGE = 1.602176634e-19

Elementary charge in C (exact, 2019 SI).

docs.title: BOLTZMANN_SI module-attribute
docs.text:
BOLTZMANN_SI = 1.380649e-23

Boltzmann constant in J/K (exact, 2019 SI).

docs.title: PLANCK_SI module-attribute
docs.text:
PLANCK_SI = 6.62607015e-34

Planck constant in J·s (exact, 2019 SI).

docs.title: AVOGADRO module-attribute
docs.text:
AVOGADRO = 6.02214076e+23

Avogadro constant in 1/mol (exact, 2019 SI).

docs.title: ATOMIC_MASS_UNIT_SI module-attribute
docs.text:
ATOMIC_MASS_UNIT_SI = 1.66053906892e-27

Atomic mass constant in kg (CODATA 2022).

docs.title: BOLTZMANN module-attribute
docs.text:
BOLTZMANN = BOLTZMANN_SI / ELEMENTARY_CHARGE

Boltzmann constant in eV/K.

docs.title: PLANCK module-attribute
docs.text:
PLANCK = PLANCK_SI / ELEMENTARY_CHARGE * 1000000000000.0

Planck constant in eV·ps: the energy in eV of a quantum of 1 THz.

docs.title: EV_PER_A3_TO_GPA module-attribute
docs.text:
EV_PER_A3_TO_GPA = ELEMENTARY_CHARGE * 1e+30 / 1000000000.0

Stress: eV/Å³ to GPa.

docs.title: GPA_TO_EV_PER_A3 module-attribute
docs.text:
GPA_TO_EV_PER_A3 = 1.0 / EV_PER_A3_TO_GPA

Stress: GPa to eV/Å³.

docs.title: BAR_TO_GPA module-attribute
docs.text:
BAR_TO_GPA = 0.0001

Pressure: bar to GPa (exact).

docs.title: GPA_TO_BAR module-attribute
docs.text:
GPA_TO_BAR = 10000.0

Pressure: GPa to bar (exact).

docs.title: EV_PER_A2_TO_J_PER_M2 module-attribute
docs.text:
EV_PER_A2_TO_J_PER_M2 = ELEMENTARY_CHARGE * 1e+20

Energy per area: eV/Å² to J/m² (equal to N/m).

docs.title: GPA_A_TO_N_PER_M module-attribute
docs.text:
GPA_A_TO_N_PER_M = 0.1

Two-dimensional stress: GPa·Å to N/m (exact).

docs.title: FS_TO_PS module-attribute
docs.text:
FS_TO_PS = 0.001

Time: fs to ps (exact).

docs.title: PS_TO_FS module-attribute
docs.text:
PS_TO_FS = 1000.0

Time: ps to fs (exact).

docs.title: AMU_A2_PER_PS2_TO_EV module-attribute
docs.text:
AMU_A2_PER_PS2_TO_EV = ATOMIC_MASS_UNIT_SI * 10000.0 / ELEMENTARY_CHARGE

Kinetic energy: amu·Å²/ps² to eV (mass times velocity squared).

docs.title: KJ_PER_MOL_TO_EV module-attribute
docs.text:
KJ_PER_MOL_TO_EV = 1000.0 / (AVOGADRO * ELEMENTARY_CHARGE)

Energy: kJ/mol to eV.

docs.title: KCAL_PER_MOL_TO_EV module-attribute
docs.text:
KCAL_PER_MOL_TO_EV = 4.184 * KJ_PER_MOL_TO_EV

Energy: kcal/mol (thermochemical calorie, 4.184 J) to eV.

None bond_radius float32

None box bool

Draw the edges of the box. Default True.

True box_radius float32

Radius of the edges in Å. Default a tenth of the median atom radius.

None mesh TriangleMesh

None mesh_color optional

One color for the surface, or (F, 3) colors of its triangles. Default light blue.

'#8fb0d8' mesh_alpha float32

Opacity of the surface. Default 1.

1.0 dislocations DislocationResult

Dislocation lines to draw, such as those of mdapy.analysis.DislocationAnalysis: tubes in the color of the family of their Burgers vector, cut at the periodic boundaries, the parts outside moved in through the opposite faces.

None dislocation_radius float32

Radius of the tubes in Å. Default 0.5.

0.5 burgers_vectors bool

Also draw the Burgers vector of each line: an arrow from the middle of the line along the vector in space. Default False.

False burgers_scale float32

Length of the arrows in units of the Burgers vectors. Default 3.

3.0 burgers_radius float32

Radius of the shafts of the arrows in Å. Default 0.3.

0.3 burgers_color optional

One color for the arrows, or "family" for the color of each line. Default light gray.

(0.7, 0.7, 0.7) vectors str or array_like

A column of three components, such as displacement, velocities or forces, or (N, 3) vectors: an arrow for each atom shown.

None vector_scale float32

Length of the arrows in units of the vectors; negative reverses them. Default 1.

1.0 vector_radius float32

Radius of the shafts of the arrows in Å. Default 0.5.

0.5 vector_color optional

One color for the arrows, or "atom" for the color of each atom. Default yellow.

(1.0, 1.0, 0.0) vector_alignment (base, center, head)

The point of the arrow at its atom: its tail, its middle or its tip. Default base.

"base" lines array_like or sequence of array_like

Polylines to draw, such as the paths of mdapy.analysis.trajectory_lines: (M, T, 3) points, or (T, 3) points of each line.

None line_radius float32

Radius of the lines in Å. Default 0.1.

0.1 line_color optional

One color for the lines, or a color for each line. Default gray.

(0.6, 0.6, 0.6) wrap_lines bool

Cut the lines at the periodic faces of the box and move the parts outside in through the opposite faces (True), or draw them as they are (False, default).

A legend in a column of its own at the left of the picture, the scene framed in the rest, which needs matplotlib. True gives the names of the structures or elements of the atoms shown with their colors, or a bar with the values and the colormap of a column or of (N,) values. A string does the same with this title, as for values that have no name. A mapping gives its own names and colors. Default none.

docs.title: CIF
docs.text:
The format cif reads Crystallographic Information Files, the crystal of each data block: the atom sites of the asymmetric unit expanded by the symmetry operations into the whole cell. Files with extension .cif are recognized. MDAPY reads CIF files but does not write them.

from mdapy.io import read
from mdapy.transform import replicate
from mdapy.visualization import render

# rutile, TiO2: two sites and the sixteen operations of P4_2/mnm
text = """data_rutile
_cell_length_a 4.5937(2)
_cell_length_b 4.5937(2)
_cell_length_c 2.9587(1)
_cell_angle_alpha 90
_cell_angle_beta 90
_cell_angle_gamma 90
_symmetry_space_group_name_H-M 'P 42/m n m'
loop_
_symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz
'x, y, z' '-x, -y, z' '-y+1/2, x+1/2, z+1/2' 'y+1/2, -x+1/2, z+1/2'
'-x+1/2, y+1/2, -z+1/2' 'x+1/2, -y+1/2, -z+1/2' 'y, x, -z' '-y, -x, -z'
'-x, -y, -z' 'x, y, -z' 'y+1/2, -x+1/2, -z+1/2' '-y+1/2, x+1/2, -z+1/2'
'x+1/2, -y+1/2, z+1/2' '-x+1/2, y+1/2, z+1/2' '-y, -x, z' 'y, x, z'
loop_
_atom_site_label
_atom_site_type_symbol
_atom_site_fract_x
_atom_site_fract_y
_atom_site_fract_z
Ti1 Ti4+ 0 0 0
O1 O2- 0.30478 0.30478 0
"""
with open("rutile.cif", "w") as f:
    f.write(text)

rutile = read("rutile.cif")  # 2 Ti and 4 O
render(
    replicate(rutile, (3, 3, 4)),
    "images/rutile.png",
    representation="ball_and_stick",
    bonds=2.1,
    view=(-0.2, -1.0, -0.35),
    width=600,
    height=600,
    legend=True,
)

Rutile read from the CIF above and repeated 3 × 3 × 4 times: titanium (gray) in octahedra of oxygen (red).

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
Item In MDAPY data_name one frame per data block; info["name"] _cell_length_a, _b, _c, _cell_angle_alpha, _beta, _gamma box.matrix: a along x, b in the xy plane; periodic in all directions; angles 90° if absent _atom_site_fract_x, _y, _z, or _atom_site_Cartn_x, _y, _z positions of the sites _atom_site_type_symbol, or else _atom_site_label element: the letters before charges and numbers, such as Fe of Fe2+ or O of OW1 _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz the operations, such as -x+1/2,y,z+1/2

Each site is moved by every operation into the cell, fractional coordinates in [0, 1); an image closer than 0.01 Å to one before it is the same atom. The atoms follow the sites, and those of a site the operations. Without operations the sites are taken as they are, unless the file names a space group other than P1.

Numbers may carry standard uncertainties, as 4.5937(2). Names of tags are compared without regard to case, and CIF 2 names with a dot, such as _cell.length_a, are read as those with _. Values may be quoted with ' or ", or span lines between lines starting with ;; # starts a comment. Other items are read and left out. Occupancies are not kept: sites partly occupied by different atoms give atoms on top of each other, and reading warns of them.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: FileFormatError at the line of the fault for: a quote or text field not closed, a loop whose values do not fill its rows, a tag without a value, a word out of place, a file without a data block, a block without cell lengths, a cell without volume, a number that cannot be read, no atom sites or elements, an unknown element, a space group named without its operations, and an operation that is not three expressions in x, y and z.

docs.title: Extended XYZ
docs.text:
The format extxyz (extensions .xyz and .extxyz) stores one or more frames, each with per-atom columns, a lattice and global values such as the energy. MDAPY reads and writes the conventions of ASE (Larsen et al. (2017)) and GPUMD (Fan et al. (2022)).

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.io import write

system = mp.System(
    positions=[[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1.8, 1.8, 0.0]],
    box=mp.Box(3.6),
    elements=["Cu", "Cu"],
    info={"energy": -7.0, "config_type": "fcc"},
).with_columns(forces=np.zeros((2, 3)))
write("cu.xyz", system)
print(Path("cu.xyz").read_text())

writes

2
Lattice="3.6 0.0 0.0 0.0 3.6 0.0 0.0 0.0 3.6" Properties=species:S:1:pos:R:3:forces:R:3 pbc="T T T" energy=-7.0 config_type=fcc
Cu 0 0 0 0 0 0
Cu 1.8 1.8 0 0 0 0

Each frame is a line with the number of atoms, a comment line of key=value pairs, and one line per atom whose columns are described by the Properties key. Frames follow each other directly; blank lines may only end the file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Reading has no options. Writing has one:

Name Type Default Meaning columns list of str all columns Per-atom columns to write. element and positions are always written, first.

docs.title: Per-atom columns
docs.text:
Properties lists each column as name:type:width, with type R (real), I (integer), L (logical, T or F) or S (string). Some names become MDAPY columns:

Property MDAPY column Conversion species:S:1 element Symbols are capitalized, so CU becomes Cu. Z:I:1 element Atomic numbers; used when there is no species. pos:R:3 positions vel:R:3 velocities Å/fs (GPUMD) to Å/ps. momenta:R:3 velocities ASE momenta divided by the masses (from mass, or the standard atomic weights), from amu·Å per ASE time unit, Å·(amu/eV)1/2 ≈ 10.18 fs, to Å/ps. force:R:3, forces:R:3 forces mass:R:1, masses:R:1 mass charge:R:1, initial_charges:R:1 charge energies:R:1, energy_atom:R:1 atomic_energies atomic_virials:R:9 atomic_virials 3×3, row by row.

When several properties give the same column, a property named as the column gives it, such as forces beside force; otherwise the first one does, such as vel before momenta; the others keep their own names. Any other property becomes a column of the same name: a float64, int64, boolean or string column, or for a width above 1 an array column. Without Properties, a frame has species:S:1:pos:R:3, as plain XYZ files do.

When writing, element is written as species, positions as pos, velocities as vel in Å/fs, and atomic_energies as energies. Other columns keep their names; nested array columns are flattened row by row. Columns of other types, missing values, and strings that are empty or contain blanks cannot be written.

docs.title: The comment line
docs.text:
Key Meaning In MDAPY Lattice 9 numbers: the lattice vectors a, b, c, one after the other box.matrix pbc T or F for each direction; with a Lattice, the default is T T T box.pbc Origin 3 numbers: the corner of the box; written only when not zero box.origin Properties the per-atom columns, see above energy total energy, eV info["energy"] virial 9 numbers in Fortran order, or 6 in Voigt order (xx yy zz yz xz xy), eV info["virial"], 3×3 stress the same layout, eV/Å3, positive under tension info["stress"], 3×3, GPa

These keys are recognized in any letter case, as GPUMD writes them in lower case. A frame without Lattice gets a non-periodic box around its atoms (see Simulation box), and may then not have pbc true or an Origin. A Lattice of zeros with pbc false counts as no Lattice.

Every other key becomes an entry of info, keeping its case. Its value is read as an int64, a float64, a boolean (T, F, True, False, true, false, TRUE, FALSE), an array of one of these (separated by blanks or commas), JSON after the prefix _JSON, or else text. A key without a value is True. Values with blanks are quoted with "", '', {} or [], and a backslash makes the next character literal.

A comment line without = holds no key=value pair: it is the free comment of a plain XYZ file, such as water, relaxed with PBE, kept whole as info["comment"], and its words are not keys. Writing puts it back as comment="...".

When writing, numbers, booleans, text and 1-dimensional arrays are written as such. Other values (arrays of other shapes, mappings, None, and text that would read back as a number) are written as _JSON so that they read back unchanged. info cannot use the keys Lattice, pbc, Origin and Properties, in any case.

docs.title: Other programs
docs.text:
• ASE stores momenta rather than velocities; MDAPY reads them and writes vel, which ASE keeps as an array named vel. ASE reads a charge property as charges computed by a calculator.
  • OVITO writes velocities as velo, in the units it was given them, and reads MDAPY's vel as a property of that name. MDAPY keeps velo as a column of that name, since its units are not in the file; for velocities that came from LAMMPS in metal units, system.with_columns(velocities=system["velo"]) takes them in Å/ps.
  • GPUMD training files (train.xyz) give energy, virial in eV or stress in eV/Å3 with the sign above, and force per atom. GPUMD's dump_exyz writes its pressure tensor under the key stress; it is positive under compression, the opposite sign. MDAPY reads the value as written, so check the sign of stress from such files.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Extended XYZ specification, libAtoms: https://github.com/libAtoms/extxyz

docs.title: LAMMPS data
docs.text:
The format lammps-data reads and writes the data files of LAMMPS (Thompson et al. (2022)) read_data and write_data, following LAMMPS stable_30Sep2026, for the atom styles of molecular dynamics: atomic, charge, bond, angle, molecular and full. Files with extension .data or .lmp, or names starting with data., are recognized.

import numpy as np
import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.io import read, write

water = mp.System(
    positions=[[1.0, 1.0, 1.0], [1.96, 1.0, 1.0], [0.76, 1.93, 1.0]],
    box=mp.Box(10.0),
    elements=["O", "H", "H"],
    topology=mp.Topology(bonds=[[0, 1], [0, 2]], angles=[[1, 0, 2]]),
).with_columns(charge=[-0.8476, 0.4238, 0.4238], molecule=[1, 1, 1])
write("water.data", water)
same = read("water.data")
same.table["element"].to_list()  # ['O', 'H', 'H'], from the Masses comments

water.data is

LAMMPS data file via MDAPY 2.0.0, timestep = 0, units = metal

3 atoms
2 atom types
2 bonds
1 bond types
1 angles
1 angle types

0.0 10.0 xlo xhi
0.0 10.0 ylo yhi
0.0 10.0 zlo zhi

Masses

1 15.999 # O
2 1.008 # H

Atoms # full

1 1 1 -0.8476 1 1 1
2 1 2 0.4238 1.96 1 1
3 1 2 0.4238 0.76 1.93 1

Bonds

1 1 1 2
2 1 1 3
