docs.title: Special quasirandom structures
docs.text:
sqs_alloy places elements in given fractions on the sites of a perfect lattice so that the pairs of the nearest shells of neighbors are those of a random alloy, the best that a small cell can do for a random alloy.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal, sqs_alloy

sites = build_crystal("fcc", 3.6, repeat=(4, 4, 4))
binary = {"Cu": 1, "Ni": 1}
quinary = {"Co": 1, "Cr": 1, "Fe": 1, "Mn": 1, "Ni": 1}
cuni = sqs_alloy(sites, binary, shells=3, seed=1)
cantor = sqs_alloy(sites, quinary, seed=1)

import numpy as np
from mdapy.visualization import render, write_png

left = render(cuni, width=600, height=600, legend=True)
right = render(cantor, width=600, height=600, legend=True)
write_png("images/sqs.png", np.hstack([left, right]))

Left: equiatomic CuNi of 256 atoms whose pair correlations in the first three shells come as close as the cell allows to those of the random alloy. Right: the Cantor alloy on the same sites.

The Warren–Cowley parameters of every pair of elements, shell by shell, against those of a random alloy of the same atoms:

from mdapy.analysis import WarrenCowley
from mdapy.build import random_alloy
from mdapy.visualization import plot

order = WarrenCowley(num_neighbors=(12, 6, 24, 12, 24))  # five shells of fcc
shell = np.arange(1, 6)
with plot.style():
    fig, axes = plot.figure("double", 62, ncols=2)
    for ax, sqs, fractions in zip(axes, (cuni, cantor), (binary, quinary)):
        random = random_alloy(sites, fractions, seed=1)
        for k, (system, name) in enumerate(((random, "random alloy"), (sqs, "SQS"))):
            alpha = order.compute(system).alpha
            pairs = np.triu_indices(alpha.shape[1])  # each pair of elements once
            values = alpha[:, pairs[0], pairs[1]]
            x = np.repeat(shell + 0.15 * (2 * k - 1), values.shape[1])
            ax.plot(
                x, values.ravel(), "o", color=("0.6", plot.COLORS[0])[k], label=name
            )
        ax.axvspan(0.5, 3.5, color="0.93", zorder=0, linewidth=0)
        ax.margins(y=0.15)  # room for the label of the shaded shells
        ax.text(
            2,
            0.98,
            "made random",
            transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(),
            ha="center",
            va="top",
        )
        ax.axhline(0, color="0.3", linewidth=0.5)
        ax.set_xticks(shell)
        ax.set_xlabel("shell of neighbors")
        ax.set_ylabel("Warren–Cowley α of each pair")
        ax.set_title("".join(fractions))
    axes[1].legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/sqs-warren-cowley", formats=("png",))

Each point is the Warren–Cowley parameter of one pair of elements in one shell, 0 for a random alloy of infinite size. In the three shells made random, those of CuNi are 0 and those of the Cantor alloy within 0.03, where the random alloys of 256 atoms reach 0.016 and 0.35; the fourth and fifth shells, left out, are no better than at random.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
sqs_alloy(system, fractions, *, shells=3, weights=None, steps=100000, temperature=1.0, seed=None, progress=None, cancel=None)

Name Type Default Meaning system System the sites, a perfect lattice such as from build_crystal fractions dict of str to float64 the fraction of each element; the counts are those of random_alloy shells int32 3 the number of shells of neighbors made random, 1 to 10 weights sequence of float64 all 1 the weight of each shell in the deviation steps int64 100000 the number of swaps tried temperature float64 1 the starting temperature of the annealing, in units of the typical change of a swap; 0 keeps only improvements seed int64 or numpy.random.Generator None the starting alloy and the swaps progress, cancel None as for every analysis

The shells are the distinct distances between sites, nearest first, so the lattice must be perfect.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: The system with a new element column, the best arrangement found.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: sqs_alloy raises InvalidParameter for a number of shells out of range, weights that are not one per shell or negative, a negative number of steps or temperature, and the errors of random_alloy; Cancelled when cancelled.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
With \(N^{(s)}_{ab}\) the ordered pairs of shell \(s\) from an atom of element \(a\) to one of \(b\), \(P_s\) all pairs of shell \(s\) and \(x_a\) the fractions, the deviation from a random alloy

\[ D = \sum_s w_s \sum_{a,b} \left( \frac{N^{(s)}_{ab}}{P_s} - x_a x_b \right)^2 \]

is zero when the Warren–Cowley parameters \(\alpha^{(s)}_{ab} = 1 - N^{(s)}_{ab} / (x_a x_b P_s)\) of every shell vanish. Starting from a random alloy, pairs of atoms of different elements swap places when the swap lowers \(D\), or with the probability \(e^{-\Delta D / T}\) otherwise, while \(T\) falls linearly to zero; the arrangement with the lowest \(D\) is returned.

Please cite

Zunger et al. (1990).

docs.title: Periodic copies and images
docs.text:
mdapy.transform.replicate places copies of a system side by side along its periodic directions, as LAMMPS replicate does; wrap moves atoms into the box and unwrap puts them at their unwrapped positions.

import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.transform import replicate, unwrap, wrap

box = mp.Box([[4.0, 0, 0], [1.0, 4.0, 0], [0, 0, 4.0]])
system = mp.System([[0.5, 0.5, 0.5], [3.9, 2.0, 2.0]], box, elements="Cu")
system = system.with_columns(id=[1, 2], image=[[0, 0, 0], [-1, 0, 0]])

bigger = replicate(system, (2, 3, 1))  # 12 atoms, ids 1 to 12
bigger.box.matrix  # rows 2a, 3b and c
inside = wrap(system)  # fractional coordinates in [0, 1), image flags updated
moved = unwrap(system)  # the second atom at x = -0.1, image flags zero

The copies are numbered along a first. A cell of graphene, two atoms, replicated 4 × 3 times, each copy colored by its number:

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.visualization import render

cell = build_crystal("graphene", 2.46, c=10.0, elements="C")
sheet = replicate(cell, (4, 3, 1))
copy = np.arange(len(sheet)) // len(cell)  # the copy of each atom
render(
    sheet,
    "images/replicate.png",
    color=copy,
    colormap="labels",
    representation="ball_and_stick",
    view="top",
    legend="copy",
    width=900,
    height=560,
)

Seen from above, with one color for each copy: copy 0 at the origin, the next copies along a to its right, the rows of copies along b above.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Function Name Type Meaning replicate(system, repeat) repeat int32 or (3,) int32 copies along a, b and c, at least 1; above 1 only along periodic directions wrap(system) unwrap(system) needs an image column

Each returns a new System.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
replicate gives the copies in a box with lattice vectors \(n_a\mathbf a\), \(n_b\mathbf b\) and \(n_c\mathbf c\) and the same origin:

  • Copy \((i, j, l)\) is number \(k = i + n_a (j + n_b l)\), so the copy along a changes fastest; its atoms are rows \(kN\) to \(kN + N - 1\), in the order of the original.
  • Its ids are those of the original plus \(k\) times the largest id. molecule numbers above 0 are offset the same way; 0, no molecule, stays 0.
  • Bonds, angles, dihedrals and impropers of copy \(k\) join the atoms of copy \(k\).
  • With an image column, each atom is placed at its unwrapped position moved by \(i\mathbf a + j\mathbf b + l\mathbf c\) and wrapped into the new box, which gives its new image flags, so a molecule whole in unwrapped positions is whole in every copy. Without one, the atoms are moved by \(i\mathbf a + j\mathbf b + l\mathbf c\) and not wrapped.
  • Other columns are copied. energy and virial, which describe the original system, are left out of info; the rest is kept.

wrap moves each atom by whole lattice vectors so that its fractional coordinates along the periodic directions lie in \([0, 1)\); an image column changes by the same vectors, so the unwrapped positions stay where they were.

unwrap puts each atom at its unwrapped position, its position plus its image flags times the lattice vectors, and sets the image flags to zero.

Neither changes the topology.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: replicate raises InvalidParameter when repeat is not one or three positive integers, or is above 1 along a direction that is not periodic. unwrap raises MissingProperty without an image column.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • LAMMPS replicate.

docs.title: Curve fitting
docs.text:
mdapy.fitting fits curves to values by least squares: fit_polynomial a polynomial of one variable, fit_surface one of two, and fit_curve any function with parameters, such as the decay of a correlation, the peak of a distribution or a law of temperature. Each gives the parameters with their standard errors and covariance, and the residuals.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.analysis import RadialDistributionFunction
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.fitting import fit_curve, gaussian

# copper with every atom shaken by a normal distribution of 0.1 Å
copper = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(8, 8, 8))
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
shaken = copper.with_columns(
    positions=copper["positions"] + rng.normal(0, 0.1, (len(copper), 3))
)
rdf = RadialDistributionFunction(cutoff=4.0, bins=200).compute(shaken)

first = (rdf.r > 2.0) & (rdf.r < 3.1)  # the first peak
peak = fit_curve(gaussian, rdf.r[first], rdf.g[first])
peak["center"]  # Å, 2.548
peak[
    "width"
]  # Å, 0.143: the distance of two atoms each shaken by 0.1 Å spreads by 0.1 √2
peak.errors  # the standard errors of amplitude, center and width

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    ax.plot(rdf.r, rdf.g, label="g(r)")
    ax.plot(rdf.r[first], peak(rdf.r[first]), "--", label="Gaussian fit")
    ax.set_xlabel("r (Å)")
    ax.set_ylabel("g(r)")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/curve-fitting", formats=("png",))

The radial distribution function of shaken copper and the Gaussian fitted to its first peak.

docs.title: Polynomials and surfaces
docs.text:
from mdapy.fitting import fit_polynomial, fit_surface

temperature = np.array([300.0, 500, 700, 900, 1100])  # K
volume = np.array([11.81, 11.90, 12.00, 12.11, 12.24])  # Å³ per atom
line = fit_polynomial(temperature, volume, 2)
line.coefficients  # of 1, T and T²
line.errors  # their standard errors
line(800.0), line(800.0, 1)  # the volume and its slope at 800 K

x, y = rng.random((2, 50))
z = 1 + 2 * x - y + 0.5 * x * y
surface = fit_surface(x, y, z, 2)  # every term x^i y^j with i + j up to 2
surface.powers  # (6, 2): the powers (i, j) of the terms
(
    surface(0.5, 0.5),
    surface(0.5, 0.5, dx=1),
)  # 1.625 and 2.25: the value, the slope along x

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
fit_polynomial(x, y, degree, *, sigma=None, absolute_sigma=False) and fit_surface(x, y, z, degree, *, sigma=None, absolute_sigma=False):

Name Type Default Meaning x, y (n,) float64 the points; for fit_surface their two coordinates, and z the values degree int32 the degree, or the total degree of the terms of a surface, with fewer coefficients than points sigma (n,) float64 None the standard deviations of the values, which weigh them by 1/σ; all equal by default absolute_sigma bool False take σ as the true standard deviations for the errors; otherwise scale the errors so that the residuals have unit variance

fit_curve(model, x, y, guess=None, *, sigma=None, absolute_sigma=False, max_steps=500, tolerance=1e-12):

Name Type Default Meaning model Model or callable one of MODELS, a Model, or a function f(x, *parameters) x array the points, as the function takes them: (n,) float64, or any array for a function of several variables y (n,) float64 the values guess (p,) float64 None a first guess of the parameters; by default that of the model, which a plain function must be given sigma, absolute_sigma as above max_steps int32 500 the most steps tolerance float64 1e-12 the fit has converged when a step changes the sum of squares by less than this fraction of it

The models, with x along the curve:

Model Function Parameters exponential A e−x/τ amplitude, time stretched_exponential A e−(x/τ)β amplitude, time, exponent gaussian A e−(x−μ)²/2w² amplitude, center, width lorentzian A w² / ((x−μ)² + w²) amplitude, center, width arrhenius A e−E/kBT, T in K, E in eV prefactor, energy power_law A xb prefactor, exponent

Model(name, function, parameters, guess=None) makes a model of a function: parameters names them in the order the function takes them, and guess(x, y), if given, guesses them from the data.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Attribute or method Type Meaning coefficients (k,) float64 of PolynomialFit, of 1, x, x², ...; of SurfaceFit, of the terms in powers powers (k, 2) int64 of SurfaceFit, the powers (i, j) of each term xi yj parameters (p,) float64 of CurveFit, the fitted parameters, also by name: fit["width"] model Model of CurveFit, the function and the names of its parameters errors float64 the standard errors, NaN where as many values as parameters leave none to estimate them covariance float64 the covariance of the coefficients or parameters residuals (n,) float64 the values less the fit r_squared float64 the coefficient of determination, 1 for a perfect fit steps int32 of CurveFit, the steps the fit took fit(x) float64 the fitted curve at points; PolynomialFit(x, derivative) and SurfaceFit(x, y, dx=, dy=) give derivatives too

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: InvalidParameter for values that are not finite or of other shapes, a degree out of range, a σ that is not positive, a plain function without a guess, a guess of another length, a function that is not finite at the guess, and a fit that does not converge within max_steps.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: The fit minimizes the sum of squares of the weighted residuals, \(\sum_i \left(y_i - f(x_i; \mathbf p)\right)^2 / \sigma_i^2\). Polynomials and surfaces are linear in their coefficients and are solved at once; fit_curve takes steps of the Levenberg–Marquardt method from the guess. The covariance of the parameters is \((J^\mathsf{T} W J)^{-1}\), with \(J\) the derivatives of the function with respect to the parameters and \(W\) the weights \(1/\sigma_i^2\), multiplied by the variance of the residuals, \(\chi^2/(n - p)\), unless absolute_sigma.

docs.title: Equations of state
docs.text:
mdapy.fitting.fit_eos(volumes, energies, *, form="birch_murnaghan") fits an equation of state to energies at volumes: the energy at the minimum, the volume there, the bulk modulus and its derivative with respect to the pressure, with their standard errors, and the energy and the pressure at any volume.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.fitting import fit_eos

potential = EAM.zhou(["Cu"])
a = np.linspace(3.45, 3.80, 11)
cells = [build_crystal("fcc", s, elements="Cu") for s in a]
volumes = a**3 / 4  # Å³ per atom
energies = np.array([potential.compute(c, ("energy",)).energy / 4 for c in cells])

eos = fit_eos(volumes, energies)
eos.v0, eos.e0  # 11.80 Å³ and -3.540 eV per atom
eos.b0, eos.b0_prime  # 131.7 GPa and 4.7
eos.errors  # of e0, v0, b0 (GPa) and b0_prime
eos.pressure(11.0)  # GPa, under compression
vinet = fit_eos(volumes, energies, form="vinet")

from mdapy.visualization import plot

fine = np.linspace(volumes.min(), volumes.max(), 200)
with plot.style():
    fig, (top, bottom) = plot.figure("single", 100, nrows=2, sharex=True)
    top.plot(volumes, energies, "o", label="EAM")
    top.plot(fine, eos.energy(fine), label="Birch–Murnaghan")
    top.set_ylabel("Energy (eV/atom)")
    top.legend()
    bottom.plot(fine, eos.pressure(fine))
    bottom.axhline(0, color="0.6", lw=0.8)
    bottom.set_ylabel("Pressure (GPa)")
    bottom.set_xlabel("Volume (Å³/atom)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/equation-of-state", formats=("png",))

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Default Unit Meaning volumes (n,) float64 Å³ five or more volumes, of a cell or per atom energies (n,) float64 eV the energies at the volumes, of the same cell or per atom form str "birch_murnaghan" one of FORMS: "birch_murnaghan" (third order), "vinet" or "murnaghan"

docs.text:
An EquationOfState:

Attribute or method Type Unit Meaning form str the form fitted e0 float64 eV the energy at the minimum v0 float64 Å³ the volume at the minimum b0 float64 GPa the bulk modulus there b0_prime float64 its derivative with respect to the pressure errors (4,) float64 the standard errors of e0, v0, b0 and b0_prime residuals (n,) float64 eV the energies less the fit r_squared float64 the coefficient of determination energy(volume) float64 eV the energy at volumes pressure(volume) float64 GPa −dE/dV at volumes

docs.title: Errors

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
With \(\eta = (V_0/V)^{2/3}\) and \(x = (V/V_0)^{1/3}\):

\[ E_\text{BM} = E_0 + \frac{9 V_0 B_0}{16}\left[(\eta - 1)^3 B_0' + (\eta - 1)^2 (6 - 4\eta)\right], \] \[ E_\text{Vinet} = E_0 + \frac{2 B_0 V_0}{(B_0' - 1)^2}\left[2 - \left(5 + 3B_0'(x - 1) - 3x\right) e^{-\frac{3}{2}(B_0' - 1)(x - 1)}\right], \] \[ E_\text{Murnaghan} = E_0 + \frac{B_0 V}{B_0'}\left[\frac{(V_0/V)^{B_0'}}{B_0' - 1} + 1\right] - \frac{V_0 B_0}{B_0' - 1}. \]

The third-order Birch–Murnaghan energy is a cubic in \(V^{-2/3}\), whose least squares are linear; it also gives the first guess of the other forms, which fit_curve then fits.

Please cite

Birch (1947) for the Birch–Murnaghan form, Vinet et al. (1987) for the Vinet form and Murnaghan (1944) for the Murnaghan form.

docs.title: Interpolation
docs.text:
mdapy.fitting.Spline draws a cubic spline through values at points on a line, and GridSpline one through values on a rectangular grid: a curve or a surface through every value, with continuous first and second derivatives, for values between the points, slopes, curvatures and integrals.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.fitting import Spline

# the energy per atom of copper at eight lattice constants
potential = EAM.zhou(["Cu"])
a = np.linspace(3.45, 3.80, 8)
energy = np.array(
    [
        potential.compute(build_crystal("fcc", s, elements="Cu"), ("energy",)).energy
        / 4
        for s in a
    ]
)

curve = Spline(a, energy)
fine = np.linspace(3.45, 3.80, 3501)
best = fine[np.argmin(curve(fine))]  # Å, 3.615
curve(best)  # eV, -3.540
curve(best, 2)  # eV/Å², 7.09: the curvature at the minimum
curve.integral(3.5, 3.7)  # eV Å
curve(3.9)  # NaN: no values beyond the points

A Spline takes several curves through the same points at once, as the columns of y; its values then have one more axis.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Spline(x, y, *, boundary="not-a-knot", slopes=None, extrapolate=False):

Name Type Default Meaning x (n,) float64 the points, strictly increasing, two or more y (n,) or (n, m) float64 the values at the points, or those of m curves boundary str "not-a-knot" at the two ends, one of BOUNDARIES: "not-a-knot", the third derivative continuous at the second and the second-last point; "natural", second derivatives zero; "clamped", first derivatives given by slopes; "periodic", a periodic curve whose first and last values are equal slopes (2,) or (2, m) float64 None the first derivatives at the two ends, for "clamped" extrapolate bool False continue the end cubics beyond the points; otherwise values there are NaN, or repeat with the period for "periodic"

GridSpline(x, y, z, *, boundary="not-a-knot", extrapolate=False):

Name Type Default Meaning x, y (nx,) and (ny,) float64 the points along the two axes, each strictly increasing, two or more z (nx, ny) float64 the values on the grid boundary str or (str, str) "not-a-knot" the condition along each axis, as for Spline, except "clamped"; "periodic" for a surface that repeats with the grid extrapolate bool False as for Spline

Three or four points make one cubic or parabola with "not-a-knot", and two make a straight line.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Method or attribute Returns Spline(at, derivative=0) float64 values, or a derivative of order 1 to 3, at points of any shape, followed by (m,) for m curves Spline.integral(start, end) float64, or (m,) float64, the integral from start to end GridSpline(x, y, *, dx=0, dy=0) float64 values or derivatives at points, x and y broadcast together x, y, boundary the points, the values and the conditions given

A surface of energies over the shifts of a lattice repeats with the cell of the lattice; a coarse periodic grid of such values gives the whole surface:

from mdapy.fitting import GridSpline
from mdapy.visualization import plot

# an energy on the shifts of a square cell: a 9 by 9 grid, its last row and
# column equal to its first
x = y = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 9)
z = np.cos(2 * np.pi * x)[:, None] ** 2 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * y)[None, :] ** 2
surface = GridSpline(x, y, z, boundary="periodic")
fine = np.linspace(0.0, 2.0, 201)  # two cells
fx, fy = np.meshgrid(fine, fine, indexing="ij")
with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure("double", 70, ncols=2)
    left.pcolormesh(x, y, z.T, shading="nearest")
    left.set_title("9 × 9 values")
    right.pcolormesh(fine, fine, surface(fx, fy).T, shading="gouraud")
    right.set_title("the periodic spline, two cells")
    for ax in (left, right):
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.set_xlabel("shift along x")
    left.set_ylabel("shift along y")
    plot.save(fig, "images/interpolation", formats=("png",))

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: InvalidParameter for points that are not strictly increasing or not finite, values of another shape, an unknown boundary, slopes missing or of the wrong shape, periodic values whose ends differ, a derivative out of range, and the limits of an integral beyond the points of a spline that does not extrapolate.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: On each interval between neighboring points the spline is a cubic. The cubics meet with equal values, first and second derivatives at every point, which leaves two conditions to choose, set by boundary. A GridSpline is the spline along x of the splines along y: at every point of the grid it takes the values given, and along any line of the grid it is the Spline through them.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Curve fitting, which passes near noisy values rather than through them.

docs.title: ASE calculators
docs.text:
mdapy.interop.to_ase_calculator makes any MDAPY calculator, such as EAM or NEP, an ASE calculator, for the optimizers, filters and molecular dynamics of ASE; from_ase_calculator makes any ASE calculator, such as the calculator of a machine-learned potential, an MDAPY calculator, for minimize, defect energies and elastic constants.

from ase.build import bulk
from ase.calculators.emt import EMT
from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
from ase.optimize import BFGS
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.interop import from_ase_calculator, to_ase_calculator
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

# an mdapy potential in ASE
atoms = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=3.5, cubic=True)
atoms.calc = to_ase_calculator(EAM.zhou(["Cu"]))
BFGS(FrechetCellFilter(atoms), logfile=None).run(fmax=1e-4)
atoms.cell.lengths()  # [3.615, 3.615, 3.615]

# an ASE calculator in mdapy
copper = build_crystal("fcc", 3.5, elements="Cu", repeat=(2, 2, 2))
relaxed = minimize(copper, from_ase_calculator(EMT()), cell="isotropic")
relaxed.system.box.lengths / 2  # [3.590, 3.590, 3.590], the lattice of EMT

Any ASE calculator serves, for example the NEP calculator of torchnep:

from torchnep.ase_calculator import NEP

potential = from_ase_calculator(NEP("nep.txt"))
potential.compute(system, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))

Both need ASE (pip install "mdapy[ase]").

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Argument Returns to_ase_calculator(calculator) any MDAPY Calculator an ASE calculator from_ase_calculator(calculator) any ASE calculator an MDAPY Calculator

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The properties of each side and those of the other they come from:

ASE property Unit MDAPY property Unit energy, free_energy eV energy eV energies eV atomic_energies eV forces eV/Å forces eV/Å stress eV/Å³ virial, \(W = -\sigma V\) eV stresses eV/Å³ atomic_virials, \(-\sigma_i V\) eV

ASE gives stresses in the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, positive under tension. Each side offers the properties that the other computes. An MDAPY calculator in ASE gives its energy as both energy and free_energy; an ASE calculator in MDAPY gives free_energy as the energy where it computes one, since the forces derive from it.

Each calculation converts the atoms with from_ase or to_ase. An ASE calculator in MDAPY has a cutoff of 0: it searches its own neighbors and takes no neighbor list of MDAPY.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: ASE raises its PropertyNotImplementedError for a property that the MDAPY calculator does not compute; an ASE calculator in MDAPY raises InvalidParameter for one that the ASE calculator does not compute.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• The calculator interface.
  • ASE calculators.

docs.title: ASE
docs.text:
mdapy.interop.to_ase and from_ase convert a System to an ase.Atoms and back, with velocities, charges, constraints and the results of a calculation.

from ase.build import bulk
from ase.constraints import FixAtoms
from mdapy.interop import from_ase, to_ase

atoms = bulk("Cu", "fcc", a=3.615, cubic=True).repeat(2)
atoms.set_constraint(FixAtoms(indices=[0, 1]))
system = from_ase(atoms)  # 32 atoms in a 7.23 Å box
system.table["movable"]  # False for the first two atoms
back = to_ase(system)
back.constraints  # [FixAtoms(indices=[0, 1])]

Both need ASE (pip install "mdapy[ase]"). Calculators go between ASE and MDAPY too; see ASE calculators.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Function Argument Returns to_ase(system) a System a new ase.Atoms from_ase(atoms) an ase.Atoms a new System

The result shares no memory with its source.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
System ase.Atoms positions positions box.matrix, box.pbc cell, pbc box.origin cell displacement (celldisp) element chemical symbols; X without an element column mass masses, when set on the atoms velocities (Å/ps) momenta, in ASE's unit of time, Å·(amu/eV)1/2 charge initial charges movable FixAtoms for atoms that cannot move, FixCartesian for atoms fixed along some axes other numeric columns arrays of the same name info info info["energy"], forces, info["stress"] (GPa) or info["virial"] (eV) a single-point calculator with the energy, forces and stress (eV/Å³)

Columns of strings, such as type_label, are not converted. ASE gives the stress in eV/Å³ in the order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy; MDAPY keeps it as a (3, 3) array in GPa. Both are positive under tension.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: from_ase raises InvalidParameter for constraints other than FixAtoms and FixCartesian.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • The ase.Atoms object.

docs.title: freud
docs.text:
mdapy.interop.to_freud gives the box and the points that the analyses of freud take, and from_freud makes a System of them.

import freud
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.interop import from_freud, to_freud

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(6, 6, 6))
box, points = to_freud(crystal)
rdf = freud.density.RDF(bins=100, r_max=6.0).compute((box, points))
rdf.bin_centers[rdf.rdf.argmax()]  # 2.55 Å, the nearest neighbors
q6 = freud.order.Steinhardt(6).compute((box, points), {"num_neighbors": 12})
q6.particle_order[0]  # 0.575, the q6 of fcc
back = from_freud(box, points)

Both need freud (pip install freud-analysis).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Argument Returns to_freud(system) a System in a right-handed box periodic in every direction a freud.box.Box and (N, 3) float32 points from_freud(box, points) a three-dimensional freud.box.Box and (N, 3) points a new System

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
freud keeps a box with its first vector along x and its second in the xy plane, centered on the origin, and points in single precision. to_freud gives that box, of the same shape as the box of the system, and the atoms in it: their fractional coordinates are the same, moved into the box. The box and the atoms of a system in another orientation are turned together, so distances and angles do not change.

from_freud gives a box with freud's vectors, its origin at the corner of the box centered on the origin, and the periodicity of the freud box.

freud and OVITO in one process

With freud 3.6.1 and OVITO 3.17.1 in one process, the Voronoi tessellation of whichever was imported second crashes the process; both use the Voronoi library voro++. Run them in separate processes, or import the one whose Voronoi tessellation you need first.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: to_freud raises InvalidParameter for a box not periodic in every direction, as freud finds neighbors only in such boxes, and for a left-handed box; from_freud raises it for a two-dimensional box.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• freud boxes.
  • MDAPY, OVITO and freud: timings of the analyses they share.

docs.title: GPUMD
docs.text:
MDAPY writes the model.xyz that GPUMD starts from, reads the extended XYZ files GPUMD writes, computes with the NEP potentials GPUMD trains, and builds their training sets.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.io import write

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(10, 10, 10))
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
upper = crystal["positions"][:, 2] > crystal.box.matrix[2, 2] / 2
crystal = crystal.with_columns(
    velocities=rng.normal(0.0, 2.0, (len(crystal), 3)),  # Å/ps
    group=upper.astype(np.int64),  # one grouping method: lower 0, upper 1
)
write("model.xyz", crystal)
# Properties=species:S:1:pos:R:3:vel:R:3:group:I:1, velocities in Å/fs

Then, after the run:

from mdapy.calculators import NEP
from mdapy.io import read_trajectory

with read_trajectory("dump.xyz") as frames:  # from dump_exyz
    last = frames[-1]
potential = NEP("nep.txt")
potential.compute(last, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))

docs.title: What goes between them
docs.text:
GPUMD MDAPY Page model.xyz: species, pos, mass, charge, vel (Å/fs), group mdapy.io.write of extended XYZ: element, positions, mass, charge, velocities (Å/ps), group Extended XYZ dump_exyz, train.xyz, test.xyz mdapy.io.read_trajectory Extended XYZ NEP potentials, nep.txt the calculator NEP NEP training sets OUTCARs to extended XYZ, choosing frames, perturbed structures Training sets from VASP

GPUMD needs at least two atoms and a Lattice, which MDAPY always writes. A group column of integers, or of k integers per atom for k grouping methods, is written as group:I:k. GPUMD has no origin of the box and ignores the Origin that MDAPY writes for a box with one.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • GPUMD documentation.

docs.title: LAMMPS
docs.text:
MDAPY reads and writes the data and dump files of LAMMPS, and computes energies and forces with any interaction of LAMMPS through its Python module.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.io import read, write

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(4, 4, 4))
write("copper.data", crystal)  # atom_style atomic, Cu as type 1
read("copper.data").table["element"]  # Cu, from the comment after its mass

A LAMMPS input then starts from the file, and its dumps come back as a trajectory:

units           metal
read_data       copper.data
pair_style      eam/alloy
pair_coeff      * * Cu.eam.alloy Cu
dump            1 all custom 100 dump.lammpstrj id type x y z vx vy vz

from mdapy.io import read_trajectory

with read_trajectory("dump.lammpstrj", elements=["Cu"]) as frames:
    last = frames[-1]  # velocities in Å/ps

docs.title: What goes between them
docs.text:
LAMMPS MDAPY Page data files (read_data, write_data) mdapy.io.read, mdapy.io.write: atom styles, velocities, topology, type labels, coefficients LAMMPS data text dumps (dump atom, dump custom) mdapy.io.read_trajectory, mdapy.io.write LAMMPS dump the box: bounds, tilt factors, general triclinic boxes Box.from_lammps, Box.to_lammps Simulation box any pair_style the calculator LAMMPS LAMMPS calculator potentials in the eam/alloy format EAM reads and writes them EAM replicate mdapy.transform.replicate Periodic copies and images

MDAPY works in LAMMPS metal units; the data and dump files of real units are converted when read and written.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • LAMMPS documentation.

docs.title: OVITO
docs.text:
mdapy.interop.to_ovito and from_ovito convert a System to an OVITO data collection and back, so that a system goes through the modifiers of an OVITO pipeline and their results come back as columns.

from ovito.modifiers import CommonNeighborAnalysisModifier
from ovito.pipeline import Pipeline, StaticSource
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.interop import from_ovito, to_ovito

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(5, 5, 5))
pipeline = Pipeline(source=StaticSource(data=to_ovito(crystal)))
pipeline.modifiers.append(CommonNeighborAnalysisModifier())
analyzed = from_ovito(pipeline.compute())
analyzed.table["structure"]  # 1, fcc, for every atom
analyzed.info["CommonNeighborAnalysis.counts.FCC"]  # 500

Any file OVITO reads becomes a System the same way:

from ovito.io import import_file

system = from_ovito(import_file("run.dump").compute(10))  # frame 10

Both need OVITO (pip install ovito).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Argument Returns to_ovito(system) a System a new ovito.data.DataCollection from_ovito(data) an ovito.data.DataCollection, such as pipeline.compute() a new System

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
System OVITO box simulation cell, its vectors as columns and the origin as the fourth box.pbc periodic boundary conditions of the cell positions Position type, element, type_label Particle Type: the type column, or types numbered from 1 by first appearance of the elements; elements, or type labels, are the names of the types velocities, forces, mass, charge Velocity, Force, Mass, Charge id, molecule, image Particle Identifier, Molecule Identifier, Periodic Image atomic_energies Potential Energy the one column of structure types, such as cna_structure; several keep their names Structure Type csp, coordination, cluster Centrosymmetry, Coordination, Cluster ptm_rmsd, ptm_interatomic_distance, ptm_orientation RMSD, Interatomic Distance, Orientation shear_strain, volumetric_strain, d2min Shear Strain, Volumetric Strain, Nonaffine Squared Displacement voronoi_volume Atomic Volume other numeric columns properties of the same name; movable as 0 and 1 topology bonds, angles, dihedrals and impropers, with their types and type labels; each bond with the periodic image of its second atom that is nearest to the first info global attributes

from_ovito always gives a type column, with element where the type names are chemical symbols and type_label where they are other names. Other properties become columns of their names in lowercase with underscores, such as selection for Selection; properties of strings are left out. Values keep MDAPY's units both ways; OVITO itself assumes none.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• OVITO's Python module.
  • MDAPY, OVITO and freud: timings of the analyses they share.

docs.title: pymatgen
docs.text:
mdapy.interop.to_pymatgen and from_pymatgen convert a System to a pymatgen Structure and back, for the symmetry analysis, structure matching and materials databases of pymatgen.

from pymatgen.core import Lattice, Structure
from mdapy.interop import from_pymatgen, to_pymatgen

nacl = Structure.from_spacegroup(
    "Fm-3m", Lattice.cubic(5.64), ["Na", "Cl"], [[0, 0, 0], [0.5, 0.5, 0.5]]
)
system = from_pymatgen(nacl)  # 8 atoms
structure = to_pymatgen(system)
structure.get_space_group_info()  # ('Fm-3m', 225)

Both need pymatgen (pip install pymatgen, or pymatgen-core for the structures alone).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Argument Returns to_pymatgen(system) a System with an element column a new Structure from_pymatgen(structure) a Structure or a Molecule a new System

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
System pymatgen box.matrix, box.pbc lattice and its periodicity positions Cartesian coordinates, from the origin of the box element species velocities (Å/ps) site property velocities (Å/fs, as in POSCAR files) movable site property selective_dynamics other numeric columns site properties of the same name info properties

pymatgen has no origin of the lattice: to_pymatgen moves the atoms by minus the origin, and from_pymatgen gives a box at the origin. A Molecule gets a box that encloses it, not periodic. Columns of strings and the topology are not converted.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: to_pymatgen raises MissingProperty without an element column; from_pymatgen raises InvalidParameter for a disordered site, with more than one element.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • pymatgen Structure.

docs.title: VASP
docs.text:
MDAPY writes the POSCAR of a calculation and reads its CONTCAR and OUTCAR, runs VASP as a calculator and turns its results into training sets of machine-learned potentials.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import add_vacuum, build_crystal
from mdapy.io import read, write

slab = add_vacuum(build_crystal("fcc", 3.52, elements="Ni", repeat=(2, 2, 4)), 10.0)
bottom = slab["positions"][:, 2] < 2.0
movable = np.repeat(~bottom[:, None], 3, axis=1)  # the bottom layers fixed
write("POSCAR", slab.with_columns(movable=movable))  # selective dynamics
read("POSCAR").table["movable"]  # back as written

After the run:

from mdapy.io import read_trajectory

relaxed = read("CONTCAR")
steps = read_trajectory("OUTCAR")  # every ionic step, with energies, forces, virials

docs.title: What goes between them
docs.text: VASP MDAPY Page POSCAR, CONTCAR: selective dynamics, velocities mdapy.io.read, mdapy.io.write; the columns movable and velocities VASP POSCAR OUTCAR: ionic steps, free energies TOTEN, forces, virials, convergence mdapy.io.read, mdapy.io.read_trajectory VASP OUTCAR, Training sets from VASP single points run by a command, as in a job script the calculator VASP VASP calculator

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • VASP wiki.

docs.title: Checking frames
docs.text:
A training set gathered from many calculations often holds a few frames that would spoil a model: atoms that overlap, as after a wrong wrap or a failed relaxation; forces that do not sum to zero, as of a calculation that did not converge; and labels left out. check_frames finds them before training, frame by frame.

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.io import read, write
from mdapy.mlip import check_frames
from mdapy.visualization import plot

# forty frames of the CrCoNi alloy, shaken and labeled by an EAM
eam = EAM.zhou(["Cr", "Co", "Ni"])
sqs = read("SQS.xyz")  # 108 atoms
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
frames = []
for k in range(40):
    x = sqs["positions"] + rng.normal(0, 0.1, (len(sqs), 3))
    if k == 12:
        x[0] = x[1] + [0.6, 0, 0]  # an atom on top of another
    shaken = sqs.with_columns(positions=x)
    label = eam.compute(shaken, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
    forces = label.forces + ([0.05, 0, 0] if k == 27 else 0)  # not converged
    virial = None if k == 33 else label.virial  # left out
    frames.append(
        shaken.with_columns(forces=forces).with_info(energy=label.energy, virial=virial)
    )

table = check_frames(frames)  # close=0.5 of the sum of the covalent radii
bad = table.filter(
    pl.col("too_close")
    | (pl.col("net_force") > 1e-3)
    | ~(pl.col("has_energy") & pl.col("has_forces") & pl.col("has_virial"))
)
bad["frame"].to_list()  # [12, 27, 33]
write("clean.xyz", [f for k, f in enumerate(frames) if k not in bad["frame"]])

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure("double", ncols=2)
    near = table["closest"].to_numpy()  # infinite when no pair is close
    left.bar(table["frame"], np.where(np.isfinite(near), near, 0))
    left.axhline(0.5, color="0.5", ls="--", lw=0.8)
    left.set_ylim(0, 0.6)
    left.set_xlabel("frame")
    left.set_ylabel("closest pair / sum of covalent radii")
    right.semilogy(table["frame"], table["net_force"], "o")
    right.set_xlabel("frame")
    right.set_ylabel("net force (eV/Å)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/checks", formats=("png",))

Left: the one frame with two atoms nearer than half the sum of their covalent radii; the others have no pair that near. Right: the net force of each frame, near the rounding of the forces in all but the one whose forces were shifted by 0.05 eV/Å along x, 5.4 eV/Å over its 108 atoms.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Default Meaning frames sequence of System the frames, with an element column; their labels the info energy and virial and the column forces, as extended XYZ training sets hold them close float64 0.5 two atoms closer than this fraction of the sum of their covalent radii are too close

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A polars DataFrame of one row per frame:

Column Type Unit Meaning frame int64 the index of the frame atoms int64 its number of atoms closest float64 the smallest distance of two atoms over the sum of their covalent radii, where it is below close; inf otherwise too_close bool whether closest is below close net_force float64 eV/Å the length of the sum of the forces; NaN without forces has_energy, has_forces, has_virial bool whether the frame has these labels

The covalent radii are those of Cordero et al. (2008). The net force of a crystal or a cluster in vacuum is zero: a frame whose net force is far above the rounding of its forces holds forces of a calculation that did not converge, or of another frame.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
check_frames raises InvalidParameter for a close that is not positive, and MissingProperty for frames without an element column.

The closest pairs of many frames are found at a time, a frame on each of the threads of set_num_threads, the same whatever the threads.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Errors of a model.
  • Uncertainty and novelty.

docs.title: Errors of a model
docs.text:
predict compares the energies, forces and virials a model predicts with the labels of frames, such as those of a training set from DFT: the root mean square errors, a table of the errors of each frame and the frames that err most, to look at first. Any MDAPY calculator is a model, as a NEP or an EAM, and so is any ASE calculator through from_ase_calculator. read_gpumd reads the same from the files GPUMD writes when it trains a NEP model, and torchnep when it trains or predicts, without computing anything.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.calculators import EAM, NEP
from mdapy.io import read, write
from mdapy.mlip import predict
from mdapy.visualization import plot

# thirty frames of the CrCoNi alloy, shaken more and more, labeled by the
# EAM of Zhou as a training set would be by DFT
eam = EAM.zhou(["Cr", "Co", "Ni"])
sqs = read("SQS.xyz")  # 108 atoms
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
shaking = np.linspace(0.02, 0.2, 30)
frames = []
for amplitude in shaking:
    shaken = sqs.with_columns(
        positions=sqs["positions"] + rng.normal(0, amplitude, (len(sqs), 3))
    )
    label = eam.compute(shaken, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
    frames.append(
        shaken.with_columns(forces=label.forces).with_info(
            energy=label.energy, virial=label.virial
        )
    )

# a NEP model of CrCoNi, trained on DFT, against those labels
result = predict(frames, NEP("nep.txt"))
result.rmse()  # {"energy": eV/atom, "forces": eV/Å, "virial": eV/atom}
table = result.table()  # the errors of each frame
worst = result.worst(5)  # the five frames of the largest force errors
write("worst.xyz", [frames[k] for k in worst])

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure("double", ncols=2)
    plot.parity(
        result.forces[:, 0].ravel(),
        result.forces[:, 1].ravel(),
        ax=left,
        label="forces",
        unit="eV/Å",
    )
    right.plot(shaking, table["force_rmse"], "o")
    right.set_xlabel("shaking (Å)")
    right.set_ylabel("force error of the frame (eV/Å)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/errors", formats=("png",))

Left: each force component of the NEP model against the label of the EAM, over all atoms of the thirty frames. Right: the root mean square force error of each frame grows with how far its atoms are shaken, as the two potentials part further from the crystal; worst picks the frames at the right end.

The files of a NEP model of GPUMD trained on train.xyz, in the folder it ran in, or of the predictions of torchnep, whose frames may lie elsewhere:

from mdapy.mlip import read_gpumd

result = read_gpumd("nep_folder")  # energy_train.out, force_train.out, ...
result.rmse()
test = read_gpumd("nep_folder", "test")  # with test.xyz

# torchnep: predict_dataset("nep.txt", "data/all.xyz", "predicted")
other = read_gpumd("predicted", xyz="data/all.xyz")

A NEP model computes many frames at a time, a frame on each of the threads of set_num_threads, each as it would be alone, in predict and committee; other models frame by frame.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Parameters predict(frames, calculator) the frames, their labels the info energy and virial (eV) and the column forces (eV/Å) as extended XYZ training sets hold them; and the model read_gpumd(directory, kind="train", *, xyz=None) the directory of energy_train.out, force_train.out and virial_train.out, as GPUMD writes them when it trains a NEP model and torchnep when it trains or predicts; kind="test" for those of the test set; and the extended XYZ file of the frames, for their numbers of atoms, by default train.xyz (or test.xyz) in the directory Predictions.worst(count, *, by="force_rmse") how many frames, and the column of table() to rank them by: energy_error (by its size), force_rmse, force_max_error or virial_rmse

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A Predictions:

Attribute Type Unit Meaning atoms (F,) int64 the number of atoms of each frame energy (F, 2) float64 eV/atom the label and the prediction of each frame; NaN for a frame without a label forces (A, 2, 3) float64 eV/Å the label and the prediction of the force on each atom of all frames one after the other virial (F, 2, 3, 3) float64 eV/atom the label and the prediction of the virial of each frame, NaN where either is missing, as for a model that does not compute virials frame_of_atom (A,) int64 the frame of each atom of forces

rmse() gives the root mean square errors over the frames with labels: energy in eV/atom, forces in eV/Å over the force components, virial in eV/atom over its components. table() gives a polars DataFrame of one row per frame: frame, atoms, energy (the label per atom), energy_error, force_rmse, force_max_error (of a component) and virial_rmse. The energies of two potentials, or of DFT codes with other references, differ by a constant per atom of each element; the errors of the forces and the spread of the energy errors are what compare them.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: predict raises InvalidParameter for no frames, and what the model raises for frames it cannot compute; read_gpumd raises it for files it cannot read, files of other numbers of columns, and files that do not hold the frames of the XYZ file; worst raises it for another column.

docs.title: Perturbed structures
docs.text:
perturb makes copies of a system with its atoms displaced and its box strained at random: the first frames of a training set, to be computed by DFT, around a crystal or any other structure.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.io import write
from mdapy.mlip import perturb

crystal = build_crystal("bcc", 3.165, elements="W", repeat=(3, 3, 3))
copies = perturb(crystal, 20, displacement=0.1, strain=0.03, seed=1)
write("perturbed.xyz", copies)

# displacements of exactly 0.05 Å, without strain
small = perturb(crystal, 5, displacement=0.05, strain=0.0, style="const", seed=2)

The lengths of the displacements of the three styles, without strain:

import numpy as np
from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    for style in ("normal", "uniform", "const"):
        frames = perturb(crystal, 20, displacement=0.1, strain=0.0, style=style, seed=3)
        moved = np.concatenate([f["positions"] - crystal["positions"] for f in frames])
        length = np.linalg.norm(moved, axis=1)
        ax.hist(length, bins=50, range=(0, 0.3), histtype="step", label=style)
    ax.set_xlabel("Displacement (Å)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Atoms")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/perturbation", formats=("png",))

displacement=0.1: Gaussian displacements of root mean square length 0.1 Å, with a tail beyond it; uniform ones in a ball of radius 0.1 Å, most near its surface; and all exactly 0.1 Å long.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the structure perturbed count int32 number of copies displacement float64 0.05 Å size of the displacement of each atom strain float64 0.03 largest component of the strain of the box style str "normal" "normal": Gaussian, displacement the root mean square length; "uniform": uniform in a ball of radius displacement; "const": exactly displacement long, in a random direction seed int64 or numpy.random.Generator None seed of the random numbers

docs.title: Results
docs.text: A list of count systems. Each box is deformed by \(\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{I} + (\mathbf{e} + \mathbf{e}^\mathsf{T})/2\), the components of \(\mathbf{e}\) uniform in ±strain; the atoms move with the box and are then displaced. The copies keep every column and value of info except forces, velocities, energy, virial and stress, which belong to the system before the perturbation.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: perturb raises InvalidParameter for a negative or non-integer count, a negative displacement or strain, and an unknown style.

docs.title: Choosing frames
docs.text:
A training set grows best with frames unlike those it has. structure_descriptors gives each frame the mean of the descriptors of its atoms, of a NEP model or SOAP of any structures, farthest_point_sampling chooses the frames that cover the space of descriptors, and principal_components projects them onto a plane to look at.

from mdapy.calculators import NEP
from mdapy.io import read_trajectory, write
from mdapy.mlip import (
    farthest_point_sampling,
    principal_components,
    structure_descriptors,
)
from mdapy.visualization import plot

potential = NEP("nep.txt")
train = read_trajectory("train.xyz")
candidates = read_trajectory("md.xyz")

old = structure_descriptors(train, potential)  # (F, D)
new = structure_descriptors(candidates, potential)

# 50 candidates far from the training set and from each other
chosen = farthest_point_sampling(new, 50, start=None, selected=old)
write("add.xyz", [candidates[i] for i in chosen])

pca = principal_components(old, count=2)
pca.ratio  # fraction of the variance on each component
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure()
    ax.scatter(*pca.transform(new).T, s=4, color="0.75", label="candidates")
    ax.scatter(*pca.projection.T, s=4, label="train")
    ax.scatter(*pca.transform(new[chosen]).T, s=10, label="chosen")
    ax.set_xlabel("Principal component 1")
    ax.set_ylabel("Principal component 2")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/selection", formats=("png",))

Silicon with a NEP model of GPUMD: a training set of slightly perturbed diamond crystals (blue) and 200 candidates in four groups, their atoms displaced by 0.05 to 0.4 Å (grey, from the top down; the strains of the first group spread it sideways). Farthest point sampling takes most of the 50 from the group displaced most, farthest from the training set and from one another, and a few from each of the others.

The descriptors of a NEP model and SOAP are computed for many frames at a time, a frame on each of the threads of set_num_threads, each as it would be alone; those of other models frame by frame.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Function Parameters structure_descriptors(frames, calculator) the frames, and anything with descriptors(system), such as NEP or SOAP farthest_point_sampling(points, count, *, start=0, selected=None) (M, D) candidates, the number chosen, the first one chosen (None: the farthest from selected), and (K, D) points chosen before principal_components(points, count=2) (M, D) points, two or more, and the number of components kept, at most D

The points may be descriptors of frames or of atoms, or any other features.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
structure_descriptors returns an (F, D) array. farthest_point_sampling returns the int64 indices of the chosen points, in the order chosen. principal_components returns a PrincipalComponents:

Attribute Meaning projection (M, count) coordinates of the points along the components components (count, D) unit vectors by decreasing variance, each with its largest entry positive variance (count,) variance along each component ratio (count,) fraction of the total variance mean (D,) mean of the points transform(points) coordinates of other points along the same components

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: farthest_point_sampling raises InvalidParameter for points that are not (M, D), a count outside 0 to M, a start outside the points, and start=None without selected. principal_components raises it for fewer than two points and a count outside 1 to D.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Farthest point sampling chooses, after the first, the point whose distance to the nearest point already chosen (or in selected) is largest:

\[ i_{k+1} = \arg\max_i \min_{j \in S_k} \lVert \mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{x}_j \rVert , \]

so that the chosen points spread over the whole set. The principal components are the eigenvectors of the covariance of the points, \(\frac{1}{M-1} \sum_i (\mathbf{x}_i - \bar{\mathbf{x}})(\mathbf{x}_i - \bar{\mathbf{x}})^\mathsf{T}\), by decreasing eigenvalue, the variance along each.

docs.title: SOAP descriptors
docs.text:
SOAP gives the smooth overlap of atomic positions of each atom: a vector that describes its neighborhood, the same for rotated, moved or reordered copies of it, whatever potential the structures were made with. It is the default descriptor of MDAPY's tools for training sets: the choice of frames and the maps of their structures work with it as with the descriptors of a NEP model. The values are those of DScribe's SOAP with its default Gaussian radial functions.

import numpy as np
import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.mlip import SOAP, principal_components, structure_descriptors
from mdapy.visualization import plot

soap = SOAP(["Cu"], cutoff=5.0, n_max=8, l_max=6, sigma=0.5)
copper = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(3, 3, 3))
soap.descriptors(copper).shape  # (108, 252): one row per atom
soap.dimension  # 252

# twenty frames each of fcc, hcp and bcc copper, shaken and strained
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
cells = {
    "fcc": build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(3, 3, 3)),
    "hcp": build_crystal("hcp", 2.556, elements="Cu", repeat=(4, 3, 3)),
    "bcc": build_crystal("bcc", 2.87, elements="Cu", repeat=(4, 4, 4)),
}
frames, names = [], []
for name, cell in cells.items():
    for _ in range(20):
        box = mp.Box(cell.box.matrix @ (np.eye(3) + rng.normal(0, 0.01, (3, 3))))
        strained = cell.with_box(box, scale_positions=True)
        noise = rng.normal(0, rng.uniform(0.05, 0.1), (len(cell), 3))
        frames.append(strained.with_columns(positions=strained["positions"] + noise))
        names.append(name)

points = structure_descriptors(frames, soap)  # the mean of the atoms of each frame
# the length of SOAP grows with the density; unit vectors compare the shapes
points /= np.linalg.norm(points, axis=1, keepdims=True)
pca = principal_components(points, count=2)
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure()
    for name in cells:
        mine = np.array(names) == name
        ax.scatter(*pca.projection[mine].T, s=8, label=name)
    ax.set_xlabel("Principal component 1")
    ax.set_ylabel("Principal component 2")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/soap", formats=("png",))

Sixty frames of copper in three structures, each shaken by 0.05 to 0.1 Å and strained by about 1 %, by the first two principal components of the mean SOAP of their atoms as unit vectors: hcp lies apart, fcc and bcc side by side, each spread by its strains and shaking.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
SOAP(species, cutoff=5.0, *, n_max=8, l_max=6, sigma=0.5, crossover=True)

Name Type Default Unit Meaning species sequence of str the elements; every atom must be one of them, so that systems of other compositions share one layout cutoff float64 5.0 Å the cutoff of the radial functions, above 1 Å n_max int32 8 the number of radial functions l_max int32 6 the highest degree of the spherical harmonics, at most 20 sigma float64 0.5 Å the width of the Gaussian on each neighbor crossover bool True keep the products of the densities of two different elements; without them the descriptor grows with the number of elements, not its square

descriptors(system, *, neighbors=None, progress=None, cancel=None) takes a system with an element column of the species, and optionally a neighbor list reaching reach. The property reach is the reach of the neighbors: cutoff and the distance over which the Gaussian of a neighbor decays to a thousandth, 3.72 sigma. dimension is the number of values per atom.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A (N, dimension) float64 array: for each atom, for each pair of species (in the order of their atomic numbers, each pair once), for each degree l, for each pair of radial functions (within one species the second from the first on), the power spectrum. A neighborhood of one element has (n_max (n_max + 1) / 2) (l_max + 1) values; S elements have (S n_max)(S n_max + 1) / 2 (l_max + 1), or S times the first without crossover. These are the values and the order of DScribe's SOAP with the same species, n_max, l_max and sigma and r_cut the cutoff, with compression={"mode": "crossover"} for crossover=False.

The values grow with the number of neighbors within the cutoff, so that a denser or strained structure has a longer vector; divided by their lengths, as above, the vectors compare the shapes of the neighborhoods, and their dot product is the usual SOAP kernel of two atoms or frames.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: SOAP raises InvalidParameter for no species, an unknown or repeated element, cutoff not above 1 Å, n_max below 1, l_max not from 0 to 20, sigma not positive, and radial functions so many in so short a cutoff that they are linearly dependent. descriptors raises MissingProperty without an element column and InvalidParameter for an atom of an element not among the species.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The density of the neighbors of element Z about atom i is a Gaussian of width σ on each, the atom itself included:

\[ \rho^Z_i(\mathbf r) = \sum_{j \in Z,\; r_{ij} < r_\text{cut} + 3.72\sigma} e^{-|\mathbf r - \mathbf r_{ij}|^2 / 2\sigma^2}. \]

Its coefficients in radial functions \(g_{nl}\) and real spherical harmonics \(Y_{lm}\) are \(c^Z_{nlm} = \int g_{nl}(r)\, Y_{lm}(\hat{\mathbf r})\, \rho^Z_i(\mathbf r)\, d\mathbf r\), and the power spectrum is

\[ p^{Z_1 Z_2}_{n n' l} = \pi \sqrt{\frac{8}{2l + 1}} \sum_{m=-l}^{l} c^{Z_1}_{nlm}\, c^{Z_2}_{n'lm}. \]

The radial functions of each l are Gaussians \(r^l e^{-\alpha_k r^2}\) that decay to a thousandth at n_max lengths from 1 Å to cutoff, made orthonormal by Löwdin's symmetric orthonormalization; with them the integrals over r have a closed form, so that no integral is approximated.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Choosing frames, with structure_descriptors, farthest_point_sampling and principal_components.
  • NEP, whose descriptors work the same way.

Please cite

Bartók, Kondor and Csányi (2013); for these conventions, Himanen et al. (2020).

docs.title: Uncertainty and novelty
docs.text:
A model is unsure where it has not been trained. Two measures find such frames without labels, to choose the ones worth a DFT calculation: committee gives how much the predictions of several models differ, such as NEP models trained with other seeds, or models of other kinds; and novelty how far a frame lies from all frames of the training set in the space of descriptors, such as SOAP. Neither depends on the kind of model.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.calculators import EAM, NEP
from mdapy.io import read
from mdapy.mlip import SOAP, committee, novelty, structure_descriptors
from mdapy.visualization import plot

sqs = read("SQS.xyz")  # 108 atoms of CrCoNi
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)


def shaken(amplitude, missing=0):
    """The alloy with its atoms shaken, and some atoms taken away."""
    moved = sqs.with_columns(
        positions=sqs["positions"] + rng.normal(0, amplitude, (len(sqs), 3))
    )
    keep = np.ones(len(sqs), dtype=bool)
    keep[rng.choice(len(sqs), missing, replace=False)] = False
    return moved.filter(keep)


train = [shaken(a) for a in np.linspace(0.02, 0.08, 20)]
candidates = {
    "shaken as the training set": [shaken(0.05) for _ in range(10)],
    "shaken more": [shaken(a) for a in np.linspace(0.12, 0.2, 10)],
    "with vacancies": [shaken(0.05, missing=4) for _ in range(10)],
}

soap = SOAP(["Cr", "Co", "Ni"], cutoff=5.0, n_max=6, l_max=4)
known = structure_descriptors(train, soap)
models = [NEP("nep.txt"), EAM.zhou(["Cr", "Co", "Ni"])]
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure()
    for name, frames in candidates.items():
        distance = novelty(structure_descriptors(frames, soap), known)
        spread = committee(frames, models).max_force  # eV/Å, the largest of each frame
        ax.scatter(distance, spread, s=10, label=name)
    ax.set_xlabel("distance from the training set (SOAP)")
    ax.set_ylabel("largest spread of the forces (eV/Å)")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/uncertainty", formats=("png",))

Thirty candidate frames of CrCoNi against a training set of the alloy shaken by 0.02 to 0.08 Å, with a committee of two models, a NEP and an EAM. Frames like the training set lie close to it, and the models agree on them; frames shaken more lie farther, and the models differ the more the farther they lie; frames with vacancies lie far from it, yet the models agree on them. Each measure finds frames the other misses.

With the descriptors of the training set and of the candidates, farthest point sampling then chooses among the frames far from it.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Function Parameters committee(frames, calculators) the frames, and two or more models, any MDAPY calculators novelty(points, reference=None) (M, D) points, such as the descriptors of frames, and (K, D) points to measure from, such as those of a training set; without them, each point is measured from the other points, and repeated frames are those at zero; computed on get_num_threads() threads

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
committee gives a CommitteeResult:

Attribute Type Unit Meaning atoms (F,) int64 the number of atoms of each frame energy (F,) float64 eV/atom the standard deviation of the energy per atom over the models forces (A,) float64 eV/Å of each atom of all frames one after the other, the root mean square over the models of the distance of its force from their mean force max_force (F,) float64 eV/Å the largest of forces in each frame, the model deviation of DP-GEN

novelty gives a (M,) float64 array: the Euclidean distance of each point from the nearest point of the reference.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: committee raises InvalidParameter for fewer than two models or no frames; novelty raises it for arrays that are not (M, D) and (K, D) of one D, and for no point to measure from.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Errors of a model, where labels exist.
  • Choosing frames.

docs.title: Training sets from VASP
docs.text:
The ionic steps of VASP calculations, read from their OUTCAR files with their energies, forces and virials, become the extended XYZ training set of NEP, GPUMD and other machine-learned potentials in a few lines:

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from mdapy.io import read_trajectory, write

frames = [
    frame.with_info(converged=None)
    for outcar in sorted(Path("calculations").glob("*/OUTCAR"))
    for frame in read_trajectory(outcar)
    # the converged steps, without those of huge forces
    if frame.info["converged"] and np.abs(frame["forces"]).max() <= 30.0
]
write("train.xyz", frames)  # energy, virial and forces of each frame

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
Each OUTCAR is read as a trajectory of one frame per ionic step, of a single point, a relaxation or molecular dynamics, in the format outcar:

Where Name Meaning column forces (N, 3) eV/Å, TOTAL-FORCE info energy eV, the free energy TOTEN info virial (3, 3) eV, from FORCE on cell =-STRESS; only when VASP computed the stress (ISIF ≥ 1) info converged whether the electronic loop reached EDIFF

docs.title: Writing
docs.text: Extended XYZ files keep the energy and virial of each frame in its comment line and the forces as a column, as NEP and GPUMD read them. converged is set to None above so that the file leaves it out.

docs.title: Calculators
docs.text:
A calculator computes the energy, forces and virial of a system. MDAPY defines one interface, mdapy.calculators.Calculator, which its own potentials implement and which other packages can implement to work with everything in MDAPY that needs energies and forces.

from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.io import read

potential = EAM("CuNi.eam.alloy")
system = read("alloy.xyz")
result = potential.compute(system, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
result.energy  # eV
result.forces  # (N, 3) eV/Å
result.stress  # (3, 3) GPa
system = result.attach(system)  # forces as a column, energy and virial in info

MDAPY's calculators are EAM, NEP, LAMMPS, which makes any interaction of LAMMPS a calculator, and VASP, which runs VASP for each calculation. Any calculator serves energy minimization and elastic constants.

docs.title: The calculator interface
docs.text:
Every calculator has these members:

Name Type Meaning cutoff float64 interaction cutoff in Å elements tuple of str or None the elements the calculator handles, None for any implemented frozenset of str the properties compute can return compute(system, properties=("energy", "forces"), *, neighbors=None) CalculatorResult at least the requested properties

properties is any of "energy", "atomic_energies", "forces", "virial" and "atomic_virials" (mdapy.calculators.PROPERTIES); a calculator may compute more than requested. neighbors is a NeighborList of the same system built with a cutoff of at least calculator.cutoff, so that several calculators and analyses share one search; it is built when not given.

compute raises InvalidParameter for an unknown or unimplemented property, and for a neighbor list built for other positions or another box, with a smaller cutoff, or of nearest neighbors; MissingProperty when the system lacks a column the calculator needs.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A CalculatorResult holds:

Attribute Type Unit Meaning energy float64 eV total energy atomic_energies (N,) float64 eV they sum to energy forces (N, 3) float64 eV/Å virial (3, 3) float64 eV positive under compression atomic_virials (N, 3, 3) float64 eV they sum to virial volume float64 Å³ of the box stress (3, 3) float64 GPa \(\sigma = -W/V\), positive under tension; InvalidParameter without a virial or a volume

Values that were not computed are None; the arrays are read-only.

Method Returns attach(system) the system with forces, atomic_energies and atomic_virials as columns and energy and virial in info

The virial is the response of the energy to a homogeneous strain \(\varepsilon\) of the box and the positions,

\[ W_{ab} = -\frac{\partial E}{\partial \varepsilon_{ab}} = \sum_i x_{i,a} F_{i,b}, \]

the second form holding for systems without periodic directions.

docs.title: Writing a calculator
docs.text:
A calculator subclasses Calculator, sets cutoff, elements and implemented, and defines compute, which must accept neighbors=.

mdapy.calculators.testing.check_calculator(calculator, system) checks an implementation on a small system and raises AssertionError naming the first failed check and its largest deviation. It checks that atomic energies and atomic virials sum to the energy and the virial; that forces and the virial agree with finite differences of the energy; that translation, rotation and reordering of the atoms change nothing beyond rotating and reordering vectors; that a cell doubled along a has twice the energy; and that a neighbor list given with a larger cutoff changes nothing.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning calculator Calculator the calculator to check system System a few dozen atoms the calculator handles displacement float64 1e-4 Å step of the finite differences, also used as strain rtol, atol float64 1e-6 relative and absolute tolerances of the comparisons num_atoms int32 3 number of atoms whose forces are checked by finite differences seed int32 0 seed of the random rotation, translation and choice of atoms

docs.title: Defect energies
docs.text:
vacancy_formation_energy, surface_energy and stacking_fault_energy relax the configurations of the structure builder with a calculator and give the energies of their defects.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.simulation import (
    stacking_fault_energy,
    surface_energy,
    vacancy_formation_energy,
)

copper = EAM.zhou(["Cu"])
a = 3.615
crystal = build_crystal("fcc", a, elements="Cu", repeat=(4, 4, 4))
vacancy_formation_energy(crystal, copper).energy  # eV, about 1.28

layers = build_crystal(
    "fcc",
    a,
    elements="Cu",
    orientation=[(1, 1, -2), (-1, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1)],
    repeat=(2, 3, 4),
)
surface_energy(layers, copper).energy  # J/m², the (111) surface

# the generalized stacking fault energy along [11-2] on (111)
curve = stacking_fault_energy(layers, copper, [a * np.sqrt(6) / 2, 0, 0], points=13)
curve.energy[4]  # J/m², the intrinsic stacking fault at 1/6 [11-2]

The curve, with plot.stacking_fault:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    plot.stacking_fault(curve, ax=ax)
    plot.save(fig, "images/stacking-fault-energy", formats=("png",))

The energy of copper slipped along [11-2] on (111), over a full lattice vector: the unstable stacking fault at the first maximum, the intrinsic stacking fault at the local minimum a third of the way along, and at two thirds the highest energy, with the atoms of the two halves on top of each other.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Function Parameters vacancy_formation_energy(crystal, calculator, *, atom=0, cell=None, max_force=1e-4, max_steps=10000) the perfect crystal, the atom removed, and how the box relaxes (cell of minimize) surface_energy(crystal, calculator, *, axis=2, vacuum=15.0, max_force=1e-4, max_steps=10000) the periodic crystal, the box vector axis across the slab, and the vacuum in Å added along it stacking_fault_energy(crystal, calculator, direction, *, points=21, height=None, axis=2, relax=True, max_force=1e-4, max_steps=10000) the crystal with the plane of the fault normal to the Cartesian axis, the slip vector direction in Å, the number of points from 0 to the whole vector, the fractional height of the fault (default 0.5) and whether the atoms relax along the normal

max_force (eV/Å) and max_steps are those of each minimization, with FIRE; a minimization that does not converge raises an error. The crystal must be large enough that a defect does not meet its periodic images, and the slab thick enough that its surfaces do not feel each other. With a crystal periodic along the normal of the fault, the box moves with the upper half, so that the box holds a single fault (see slip); without it, the fault lies between two free surfaces, whose energy cancels in the difference.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Result Attributes VacancyResult energy (eV), perfect and defect energies (eV), the relaxed system SurfaceResult energy (J/m²), bulk and slab energies (eV), the area of one surface (Å²), the relaxed system StackingFaultResult fraction of the slip vector, displacement (P, 3) in Å, energy (P,) in J/m² relative to no slip, the area of the fault (Å²)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: They raise InvalidParameter for a crystal of fewer than two atoms, a crystal that is not periodic for a surface, a vacuum that is not positive, fewer than two points, a plane of fault not normal to the axis, an unknown axis, and a minimization that does not converge.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
With \(E_N\) the energy of the perfect crystal of \(N\) atoms and \(E_{N-1}\) that of the crystal with a vacancy, both relaxed,

\[ E_v = E_{N-1} - \frac{N-1}{N} E_N . \]

With \(E_\text{slab}\) the energy of the crystal opened by the vacuum, relaxed, and \(A\) the area of each of its two surfaces,

\[ \gamma_s = \frac{E_\text{slab} - E_\text{bulk}}{2A} . \]

The generalized stacking fault energy at the slip \(f\,\mathbf d\) is

\[ \gamma(f) = \frac{E(f\,\mathbf d) - E(0)}{A}, \]

each configuration relaxed along the normal of the fault only: a movable column keeps the atoms still along the plane, as LAMMPS fix setforce 0 0 NULL does. In fcc along \([11\bar2]\) the curve has the unstable stacking fault energy as its first maximum and the intrinsic stacking fault energy at \(\tfrac16[11\bar2]\).

docs.title: Molecular dynamics
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.MolecularDynamics(system, potential, *, timestep=0.001) runs molecular dynamics of a system in LAMMPS, with the interaction of a LAMMPS calculator, and gives back the thermodynamic state, the atoms along the way and the system at the end. Molecular dynamics through LAMMPS shows it at work, says what it is not made for, and how to run it on several threads or a GPU.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import MolecularDynamics

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(8, 8, 8))

with MolecularDynamics(crystal, potential, timestep=0.002) as md:
    md.velocities(600, seed=1)
    md.run(10000, ensemble="npt", temperature=300, pressure=0.0, thermo=100)
    md.run(5000, ensemble="nvt", temperature=300, save_every=500)
    md.thermo  # polars DataFrame: step, time, temperature, energies, ...
    md.frames  # the atoms every 500 steps of the second run
    hot = md.system  # the atoms at the end, with velocities and images

The thermodynamic state along the two runs:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

thermo = md.thermo
a = (thermo["volume"] / 512) ** (1 / 3)  # lattice parameter of the 8 x 8 x 8 cells
with plot.style():
    fig, (top, bottom) = plot.figure("single", 100, nrows=2, sharex=True)
    top.plot(thermo["time"], thermo["temperature"])
    top.set_ylabel("Temperature (K)")
    bottom.plot(thermo["time"], a)
    bottom.set_ylabel("Lattice parameter (Å)")
    bottom.set_xlabel("Time (ps)")
    for ax in (top, bottom):
        ax.axvline(20.0, color="0.5", linestyle="--")  # npt, then nvt
    plot.save(fig, "images/dynamics", formats=("png",))

Copper started at 600 K: half the kinetic energy goes into the potential energy at once, and the thermostat holds the rest at 300 K. The barostat expands the box from the lattice parameter of 0 K to that of 300 K at zero pressure; after the dashed line the box is fixed (nvt).

LAMMPS runs in metal units, those of MDAPY, through its Python module, installed as the LAMMPS documentation describes; potential gives the commands of the interaction, the element of each atom type and the command-line arguments of LAMMPS, such as those of Kokkos. The box may have any orientation and need not be periodic: LAMMPS gets it rotated into its own form, its non-periodic directions shrink-wrapped but never smaller than the box of system, and everything comes back in the orientation of system. The velocities of system, if it has them, are where the dynamics starts.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the atoms, with an element column, and velocities in Å/ps when it has them potential LAMMPS the interaction, as a LAMMPS calculator timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step
