docs.title: EAM
docs.text:
from mdapy.calculators import EAM

potential = EAM.zhou(["Cu", "Ni"])  # or EAM("CuNi.eam.alloy")
potential.elements, potential.cutoff
potential.write("CuNi.eam.alloy")

The energy per atom of fcc copper and nickel against the lattice parameter, from the potential:

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.visualization import plot

lattice = np.linspace(3.2, 4.4, 61)
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    for element in potential.elements:
        cells = [build_crystal("fcc", a, elements=element) for a in lattice]
        energy = [potential.compute(cell, ("energy",)).energy / 4 for cell in cells]
        ax.plot(lattice, energy, label=element)
    ax.set_xlabel("Lattice parameter (Å)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Energy (eV/atom)")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/eam", formats=("png",))

The minima are the lattice parameters and cohesive energies of the potential, near the measured 3.615 Å and 3.52 Å; the curvature at the minimum gives the bulk modulus.

EAM(path) reads an embedded atom method potential in the eam/alloy (setfl) format of LAMMPS and computes every property.

Attribute Type Meaning path str or None the potential file, None for a built potential elements tuple of str or None the elements of the potential, in the order of the file; None for an average-atom potential masses (n,) float64 their masses in amu; the mass of the average atom for an average-atom potential cutoff float64 cutoff radius in Å Method Returns compute(system, properties, *, neighbors=None, progress=None, cancel=None) as every calculator, with the progress= and cancel= of Parallelism write(path) writes the potential as an eam/alloy file, which LAMMPS reads and which reads back to the same tables EAM.zhou(elements, *, nr=2000, nrho=2000) the potential of Zhou, Johnson and Wadley for the elements average(fractions) the average-atom potential of an alloy of the elements

The atoms need an element column; elements the potential does not have raise InvalidParameter, and a malformed file raises FileFormatError with its line. A file may name species that are not elements, such as the A of an average atom; they are kept when the potential is written, but no atom of a system is one of them.

The energy of atom \(i\) is

\[ E_i = F_{s_i}\Big(\sum_j \rho_{s_j}(r_{ij})\Big) + \frac{1}{2}\sum_j \phi_{s_i s_j}(r_{ij}), \]

with the embedding energy \(F\), the electron density \(\rho\) and the pair potential \(\phi\) of the species \(s\) of the atoms, interpolated from the tables of the file as LAMMPS pair_style eam/alloy does. Each pair's virial is shared equally by its two atoms.

Please cite

Daw and Baskes (1984), and the paper of the potential.

docs.title: Potentials of Zhou, Johnson and Wadley
docs.text:
potential = EAM.zhou(["Cu", "Ni", "Al"])
potential.write("CuNiAl.eam.alloy")

EAM.zhou builds the potential for any of Cu, Ag, Au, Ni, Pd, Pt, Al, Pb, Fe, Mo, Ta, W, Mg, Co, Ti, Zr and Cr, with the tables that the database tool of LAMMPS (tools/eam_database) writes for them: the parameters of Zhou et al. (2004), those of Lin et al. (2008) for Cr, and their rule for the pair potential between two elements,

\[ \phi_{ab}(r) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\rho_b(r)}{\rho_a(r)}\phi_{aa}(r) + \frac{\rho_a(r)}{\rho_b(r)}\phi_{bb}(r)\right). \] Name Type Default Unit Meaning elements sequence of str the elements, in the order of the file nr int32 2000 points of the tables in distance, up to the cutoff \(\sqrt{10}/2\) times the largest fcc lattice constant \(\sqrt 2\, r_e\) nrho int32 2000 points of the embedding tables in density

The parameters are fitted to the pure metals; the pair potentials between elements come from the rule above, not from a fit to alloys. An unknown or repeated element raises InvalidParameter.

A cutoff on a shell of neighbors

The cutoff, \(\sqrt{10}/2\) times the fcc lattice constant, is the distance of the fifth neighbors in fcc. In a relaxed fcc crystal of one element they lie less than \(10^{-4}\) Å beyond it, and a strain above about \(10^{-5}\) brings some of them inside: the stress jumps, and what comes from small strains depends on their size. The elastic constant \(C_{11}\) of relaxed copper from elastic_constants is 168.6 GPa with the default strain=1e-3, 158.8 GPa with 1e-4, and 169.7 GPa with 1e-6, which leaves the fifth neighbors where they are. LAMMPS, with the same tables, does the same. Potentials that reach zero smoothly at their cutoff, such as NEP, do not.

Please cite

Zhou et al. (2004); with Cr, also Lin et al. (2008).

docs.title: Average atom
docs.text:
average = potential.average({"Cu": 0.4, "Ni": 0.4, "Al": 0.2})
average.compute(system)  # every atom is the average atom
average.write("CuNiAl.average.eam.alloy")  # Cu, Ni, Al and the average atom A

average(fractions) returns the average-atom potential of Varvenne et al. (2016) for a random alloy with the fractions \(c_a\) of the elements:

\[ F_A = \sum_a c_a F_a, \qquad \rho_A = \sum_a c_a \rho_a, \qquad \phi_{Ab} = \sum_a c_a \phi_{ab}, \qquad \phi_{AA} = \sum_{a,b} c_a c_b \phi_{ab}. \]

fractions is a mapping from element to fraction, or the fractions in the order of elements; elements left out have none, and the fractions sum to 1. In MDAPY every atom of a system is the average atom, whatever its element. The written file holds the elements of the potential and the average atom, named A, last, so that LAMMPS can mix them, for example with pair_coeff * * CuNiAl.average.eam.alloy A Cu for a Cu solute in the average alloy. Invalid fractions raise InvalidParameter.

Please cite

Varvenne et al. (2016), and the paper of the potential averaged.

docs.title: Elastic constants
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.elastic_constants(system, calculator, *, strain=1e-3, relax=True, max_force=1e-4, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None) gives the elastic constants of a periodic crystal from its stress under small strains.

from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import elastic_constants
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

relaxed = minimize(crystal, potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-4).system
result = elastic_constants(relaxed, potential)
result.constants  # (6, 6) GPa
result.bulk_modulus(), result.shear_modulus("voigt")

Relax the box first

The constants are those of the box as it is given. Relax it to zero stress first, as above, or the constants belong to a crystal under stress.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the crystal, periodic in every direction, or a sheet, with a mass or an element column when its positions relax calculator Calculator computes the virial, and energies and forces when the positions relax strain float64 1e-3 the magnitude \(\delta\) of the strains relax bool True whether the positions relax in each strained box (relaxed-ion constants) or stay put (clamped-ion constants) max_force float64 1e-4 eV/Å convergence of each relaxation, as in minimize max_steps int32 5000 largest number of steps of each relaxation symmetry bool or None None take the stress under a strain that an operation makes from another as the image of its stress, with the symmetry operations of the crystal, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed

A cubic crystal takes 3 strains instead of 12: a stretch both ways and a shear.

The constants of a potential that does not reach zero smoothly at its cutoff can depend on strain, when neighbors lie at the cutoff: so do those of the Zhou potentials for fcc metals.

A box periodic along two vectors in the x-y plane only makes the system a sheet, whose constants are in N/m.

docs.title: Along directions
docs.text:
A crystal is stiffer along some directions than along others. The result gives its Young's modulus and its linear compressibility along any direction, or along each of many, its shear modulus on any plane along any direction, its Poisson ratio for any stretch and direction across it, and its anisotropy in one number, zero for an isotropic crystal. plot.elastic_surface draws a quantity along every direction, and plot.elastic_section along the directions of a plane; Elastic anisotropy of copper and titanium reads the results in detail:

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import elastic_constants
from mdapy.simulation import minimize
from mdapy.visualization import plot


def constants(structure, a, element, repeat, c=None):
    potential = EAM.zhou([element])
    crystal = build_crystal(structure, a, c=c, elements=element, repeat=repeat)
    relaxed = minimize(crystal, potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-4).system
    return elastic_constants(relaxed, potential)


copper = constants("fcc", 3.615, "Cu", (3, 3, 3))
titanium = constants("hcp", 2.95, "Ti", (4, 4, 3), c=4.68)  # c along z
print(copper.young_modulus([[1, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0], [1, 1, 1]]))  # GPa
print(copper.universal_anisotropy(), titanium.universal_anisotropy())
print(titanium.linear_compressibility([[1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]]))  # 1/GPa

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure(
        "double", nrows=1, ncols=2, subplot_kw={"projection": "3d"}
    )
    plot.elastic_surface(copper, ax=left)
    plot.elastic_surface(titanium, ax=right)
    plot.panel_label(left, "a")
    plot.panel_label(right, "b")
    fig.savefig("images/elastic-surfaces.png", dpi=200)

[ 66.63540948 130.30363359 191.19854312]
1.8275734112530406 0.3528895390792597
[0.00347453 0.00256451]

The Young's modulus along every direction, with the EAM potentials of Zhou et al. a: copper, cubic, stiffest along ⟨111⟩ and softest along ⟨100⟩. b: titanium, hexagonal, stiffest along its c axis and the same in every direction around it.

The directions are in the axes of the box: those of a crystal built with an orientation turn with it.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The box and the atoms are strained by \(\pm\delta\) in each of the six components \(k\) of the strain in Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, the shear components as engineering strains (half on each off-diagonal entry), and the constants are central differences of the stress \(\sigma\) (positive under tension) in the same order:

\[ C_{jk} = rac{\sigma_j(+\delta\, \mathbf e_k) - \sigma_j(-\delta\, \mathbf e_k)}{2\delta}. \]

With \(S = C^{-1}\), the moduli of a polycrystal are the Voigt and Reuss bounds and their mean, the Hill average (Hill (1952)):

\[ egin{aligned} K_\mathrm V &= frac19\left[C_{11} + C_{22} + C_{33} + 2(C_{12} + C_{13} + C_{23}) ight], & K_\mathrm R &= \left[S_{11} + S_{22} + S_{33} + 2(S_{12} + S_{13} + S_{23}) ight]^{-1}, \ G_\mathrm V &= frac1{15}\left[C_{11} + C_{22} + C_{33} - (C_{12} + C_{13} + C_{23}) + 3(C_{44} + C_{55} + C_{66}) ight], & G_\mathrm R &= 15\left[4(S_{11} + S_{22} + S_{33}) - 4(S_{12} + S_{13} + S_{23}) + 3(S_{44} + S_{55} + S_{66}) ight]^{-1}, \ K_\mathrm H &= frac12 (K_\mathrm V + K_\mathrm R), & G_\mathrm H &= frac12 (G_\mathrm V + G_\mathrm R). \end{aligned} \]

Along a unit vector \(\mathbf n\), the Young's modulus \(E\), the stress over the strain of a stretch along \(\mathbf n\) with no stress across it, and the linear compressibility \( eta\), the relative shortening along \(\mathbf n\) per unit of hydrostatic pressure, are

\[ E(\mathbf n) = \left(s_{ijkl}\, n_i n_j n_k n_l ight)^{-1}, \qquad eta(\mathbf n) = s_{ijkk}\, n_i n_j, \]

summed over repeated indices, with the compliance tensor \(s_{ijkl}\) the entry of \(S\) in the Voigt order of the pairs \(ij\) and \(kl\), halved for each of the two that is a shear (Nye (1985)). The universal anisotropy index (Ranganathan and Ostoja-Starzewski (2008))

\[ A^\mathrm U = 5\, rac{G_\mathrm V}{G_\mathrm R} + rac{K_\mathrm V}{K_\mathrm R} - 6 \]

is zero for an isotropic crystal and positive for any other. On the plane normal to \(\mathbf n\) along \(\mathbf m\), perpendicular to it, the shear modulus \(G\), and for a stretch along \(\mathbf n\) the Poisson ratio \( u\), the contraction along \(\mathbf m\) over the stretch, are

\[ G(\mathbf n, \mathbf m) = \left(4\, s_{ijkl}\, n_i m_j n_k m_l ight)^{-1}, \qquad u(\mathbf n, \mathbf m) = - rac{s_{ijkl}\, n_i n_j m_k m_l}{s_{ijkl}\, n_i n_j n_k n_l}. \]

A polycrystal of grains in every orientation is isotropic, with the bulk modulus \(K\) and the shear modulus \(G\) of an average, and

\[ E = rac{9KG}{3K + G}, \qquad u = rac{3K - 2G}{2(3K + G)}. \]

docs.text:
It returns an ElasticResult:

Attribute or method Type Meaning constants (6, 6) float64 elastic constants \(C\) in GPa, in Voigt order; read-only bulk_modulus(average="hill") float64 the bulk modulus in GPa: the "voigt", "reuss" or "hill" average shear_modulus(average="hill", *, normal=None, direction=None) float64 or (N,) float64 the shear modulus in GPa with the same averages; with normal and direction, that of the crystal sheared on the plane normal to normal along direction, perpendicular to it, for a pair (3,) float64 or each of pairs (N, 3) float64 young_modulus(direction=None, *, average="hill") float64 or (N,) float64 the Young's modulus in GPa along a direction (3,) float64, in the axes of the box and of any length, or along each of directions (N, 3) float64; without one, that of a polycrystal from the bulk and shear moduli of average poisson_ratio(direction=None, transverse=None, *, average="hill") float64 or (N,) float64 the Poisson ratio for a stretch along direction and the contraction along transverse, perpendicular to it, for a pair or each of pairs; without them, that of a polycrystal linear_compressibility(direction) float64 or (N,) float64 the linear compressibility in 1/GPa, along a direction or directions as for young_modulus universal_anisotropy() float64 the universal anisotropy index \(A^\mathrm U\) errors (6, 6) float64 or None standard errors in GPa, from molecular dynamics; None here

elastic_constants raises InvalidParameter for a box that is not periodic in every direction and is not that of a sheet, a non-positive strain, a calculator without the properties it needs, or a relaxation that does not converge within max_steps. The methods raise it for an unknown average, an average given with directions, one of a pair of directions without the other, directions of another shape, zero, not finite or, in a pair, not perpendicular or of different shapes, and for constants that cannot be inverted.

docs.title: Free energy
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.free_energy(system, potential, temperatures) gives the free energy of a solid or a liquid per atom from molecular dynamics in LAMMPS: at one temperature by switching to a system whose free energy is known, and from there to other temperatures by the enthalpy along a run.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import free_energy, minimize

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(11, 11, 11)),
    potential,
    cell="full",
    max_stress=1e-4,
).system

temperatures = np.arange(1000.0, 1601.0, 25.0)
options = dict(switching=100, scan=300, repeats=2)
solid = free_energy(crystal, potential, temperatures, **options)
liquid = free_energy(
    crystal, potential, temperatures[::-1], phase="liquid", equilibration=15, **options
)
solid.free_energy  # eV per atom at each temperature
melting = solid.crossing(liquid)
melting.temperature, melting.latent_heat  # 1328 K, 0.124 eV per atom

The two phases of copper meet at its melting point:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    difference = liquid.free_energy[::-1] - solid.free_energy
    ax.plot(solid.temperatures, 1e3 * difference)
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="0.75", lw=0.5, zorder=0)
    ax.axvline(melting.temperature, color="0.6", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (K)")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$G_\mathrm{liquid} - G_\mathrm{solid}$ (meV/atom)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/free-energy", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al., 5324 atoms: the liquid has the lower free energy above 1328 K. A millielectronvolt per atom is 11 K here.

These are the free energies of exactly these atoms in their periodic box, so they depend a little on the number of atoms, and so does where the phases meet: the same copper gives 1331 K with 2048 atoms and 1326 K with 16384, as does the two-phase method with 16000.

A smooth potential

The potential must be continuous at its cutoff, as those fitted for metals are; a Lennard-Jones potential needs pair_modify shift yes. A jump of the energy at the cutoff is in the energies the integrals read, but not in the forces that move the atoms, and it gave an error of 1.6 meV per atom at 60 K in a crystal of argon.

The atoms are classical, as in molecular dynamics: the free energy has no zero-point energy, and well below the Debye temperature the quasi-harmonic approximation is better. LAMMPS needs its packages EXTRA-FIX, for solids, and EXTRA-PAIR, for liquids.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the atoms, with an element column, in a box periodic in every direction: for a solid at their places in the crystal (relax them first), for a liquid anywhere, as it is melted first potential LAMMPS the interaction; a liquid needs one pair style, not a hybrid temperatures float64 or (T,) float64 K the free energy is calculated at the first and followed from there to the others, which lie on one side of it, in order phase str "solid" "solid" or "liquid" pressure float64 or None 0 GPa the pressure, for the Gibbs energy; None for the Helmholtz energy in the box of system timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step equilibration float64 10 ps the time of each equilibration switching float64 50 ps the time of each switching between two interactions scan float64 100 ps the time of each run between the first and the last temperature repeats int32 1 independent calculations at the first temperature, for error mixing bool False add the ideal entropy of mixing of a random solid solution, whose atoms do not exchange places in the dynamics; a liquid has it by itself melt_temperature float64 twice the first temperature K the temperature at which a liquid is melted barostat str "aniso", "iso" for a liquid how the box changes, as in run seed int32 1 the seed of the random numbers progress callable None called as progress(done, total) with the steps run cancel CancelToken None stops the calculation, which raises Cancelled

Solids start from the first temperature low, near where the crystal is stable, and go up; liquids start high and come down. A crystal heated too far melts, and a liquid cooled too far freezes: when the enthalpy of a scan shows this, the scan is run again short of there, and the temperatures beyond are left out with a warning. In a scan of 200 ps a crystal kept its structure up to about 1.2 times its melting point, for copper, aluminum and nickel.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
free_energy returns a FreeEnergyResult, all per atom; arrays are read-only.

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures pressure float64 or None GPa the pressure free_energy (T,) float64 eV the Gibbs energy, or the Helmholtz energy at constant volume enthalpy (T,) float64 eV the enthalpy, or the energy at constant volume, smoothed entropy (T,) float64 eV/K the entropy, \((H - G)/T\); classical, so negative at low temperatures volume (T,) float64 Å³ the volume phase str "solid" or "liquid" error float64 or None eV the standard error at the first temperature from the repeats; None for one dissipation (T,) float64 eV half the difference of the work there and back: near zero when the switching and the scan are slow enough and the phase stays as it is system System the atoms in the box of the first temperature

crossing(other) gives where this phase and another at the same pressure have the same free energy, as a PhaseCoexistence:

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperature float64 K the temperature latent_heat float64 eV the change of enthalpy to the other phase entropy float64 eV/K the change of entropy volume float64 Å³ the change of volume

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
A solid at volume \(V\) is switched to independent harmonic springs of spring constants \(k_i\) at the places of its atoms, chosen to give each element the mean square displacement it has in the crystal, and back (Frenkel and Ladd (1984); Freitas et al. (2016)):

\[ F = F_\mathrm{springs} + F_\mathrm{cm} + \frac{1}{2N} \left[ \int_0^1 (U - U_\mathrm{springs})\, d\lambda - \int_1^0 (U - U_\mathrm{springs})\, d\lambda \right], \]

with the forces \((1-\lambda)\) of the crystal and \(\lambda\) of the springs, and

\[ F_\mathrm{springs} = \frac{3 k_B T}{N} \sum_i \ln\frac{\hbar\omega_i}{k_B T}, \qquad F_\mathrm{cm} = \frac{k_B T}{N} \ln\left[ \frac{N}{V} \left( 2\pi \sum_i \frac{m_i^2}{M^2} \frac{k_B T}{k_i} \right)^{3/2} \right] \]

for the center of mass, held fixed. Half the difference of the two ways removes the heat lost on the way.

A liquid at volume \(V\) is switched in the same way to the Uhlenbeck-Ford model \(U_\mathrm{UF} = -p\,k_B T \ln(1 - e^{-r^2/\sigma^2})\), with \(p = 50\) and \(\sigma = 1.5\) Å (Paula Leite et al. (2016)), which is switched in turn from nothing, the ideal gas:

\[ F = F_\mathrm{gas} + \frac{1}{N} \int_0^1 \langle U_\mathrm{UF} \rangle_\lambda\, d\lambda + \frac{1}{N} \int_0^1 \langle U - U_\mathrm{UF} \rangle_\lambda\, d\lambda. \]

Between temperatures the free energy follows the enthalpy \(H\) along runs with the temperature changing there and back, of which the mean is taken:

\[ \frac{G(T)}{T} = \frac{G(T_0)}{T_0} - \int_{T_0}^{T} \frac{H(T')}{T'^2}\, dT'. \]

The Gibbs energy at pressure \(P\) is \(G = F + PV\), with \(V\) the mean volume at the first temperature and \(P\).

docs.text:
free_energy raises InvalidParameter for invalid options, a box not periodic in every direction, a hybrid pair style for a liquid, a liquid whose atoms do not move from their neighbors, a phase that changes in every scan, or if LAMMPS fails; MissingProperty for a system without an element column; Cancelled when cancelled. crossing raises InvalidParameter for other pressures, temperatures that do not overlap, or free energies that do not cross between them.

Please cite

Frenkel and Ladd (1984) and Freitas et al. (2016) for solids; Paula Leite et al. (2016) for liquids.

docs.title: LAMMPS
docs.text:
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS

calculator = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * CuNi.eam.alloy Cu Ni",
    elements=["Cu", "Ni"],
)
calculator.compute(system, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
calculator.close()

LAMMPS(pair, elements, *, commands="", cmdargs=(), cutoff=None) makes any interaction that LAMMPS computes a calculator, through the LAMMPS Python module, installed as the LAMMPS documentation describes.

Metal units only

LAMMPS runs in metal units, those of MDAPY: Å, eV, ps and amu. The commands in pair must define the interaction for metal units; potentials written for other units, such as real or si, give wrong results.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning pair str the LAMMPS commands of the interaction, such as pair_style and pair_coeff, for metal units elements sequence of str the element of each LAMMPS atom type, from type 1 commands str "" LAMMPS commands run before pair, such as newton on cmdargs sequence of str () command-line arguments of LAMMPS, such as ["-k", "on", "t", "4", "-sf", "kk"] for Kokkos with four threads cutoff float64 None Å the largest cutoff of the interaction; asked from LAMMPS when not given, which LAMMPS older than 30 Sep 2026 cannot tell Attribute or method Meaning elements the element of each atom type cutoff the largest cutoff of the interaction in Å compute(system, properties, *, neighbors=None) every property; LAMMPS searches its own neighbors, so neighbors is not used close() closes the LAMMPS instance; the next computation starts a new one

The calculator keeps one LAMMPS instance while the atoms and their elements stay the same, as during minimize, also when the box changes but not its periodic directions; it starts a new one for other atoms, elements or periodic directions. Any box works: LAMMPS receives it rotated to its restricted triclinic form, and forces and virials are rotated back. Along non-periodic directions LAMMPS has fixed boundaries around the atoms. With Kokkos, LAMMPS is shut down when Python exits.

The constructor raises InvalidParameter when LAMMPS rejects the commands, with the message of LAMMPS, or cannot tell the cutoff that is not given, and ImportError without the LAMMPS Python module; compute raises InvalidParameter for atoms of an element that no atom type has.

Please cite

Thompson et al. (2022), and the paper of the potential.

docs.title: Elastic constants from molecular dynamics
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.md_elastic_constants(system, potential, temperature, *, pressure=0.0, strain=0.01, timestep=0.001, equilibration=10000, production=20000, every=10, blocks=5, barostat="tri", seed=1) gives the isothermal elastic constants of a crystal at a temperature from the mean stress of molecular dynamics in LAMMPS under small strains, with their standard errors. It takes in the anharmonic vibrations that the quasi-harmonic approximation leaves out, at the cost of thirteen runs.

from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import md_elastic_constants
from mdapy.transform import replicate

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = replicate(cell, (6, 6, 6))  # large enough for small fluctuations
result = md_elastic_constants(crystal, potential, 600.0, timestep=0.002)
result.constants[0, 0], result.errors[0, 0]  # C11 and its standard error, GPa
result.bulk_modulus(), result.shear_modulus()

The crystal first runs at the temperature and pressure (Nosé–Hoover, fix npt): equilibration steps, then production steps over which its box is averaged every every steps. Its last atoms, put in the mean box, are the reference. For each of the six components of the strain in Voigt order, strains of \(+\delta\) and \(-\delta\) of the reference (shears as engineering strains, half on each off-diagonal entry, the atoms and their velocities moved with the box) each run equilibration steps at constant volume and temperature (fix nvt), then production steps over which the stress is averaged:

\[ C_{jk} = \frac{\bar\sigma_j(+\delta\,\mathbf e_k) - \bar\sigma_j(-\delta\,\mathbf e_k)}{2\delta}, \]

with \(\sigma\) positive under tension. The standard error of each mean comes from the means of blocks blocks of the run, and the two errors of a column add in quadrature. The constants are those at constant temperature; under a pressure, the stress–strain coefficients.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the crystal, periodic in every direction, with an element column potential LAMMPS the interaction, as a LAMMPS calculator temperature float64 K the temperature, positive pressure float64 0 GPa the pressure strain float64 0.01 the magnitude \(\delta\) of the strains timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step equilibration int32 10000 steps before each average production int32 20000 steps of each average every int32 10 steps between the values averaged blocks int32 5 blocks of each average for its standard error barostat str "tri" how the box finds its mean shape: "iso", "aniso" or "tri" seed int32 1 seed of the starting velocities

docs.title: Results
docs.text: An ElasticResult, as of elastic_constants, with errors, the (6, 6) standard errors in GPa.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: md_elastic_constants raises InvalidParameter for a box that is not periodic, a temperature, strain or numbers of steps that are not positive, fewer than two blocks or fewer samples than blocks, and the errors of MolecularDynamics.

docs.title: Melting point
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.melting_point(crystal, potential, temperature) gives the melting point of a crystal from a first guess, by the two-phase method in LAMMPS: a solid and a liquid share a box at constant enthalpy and pressure, where the interface between them moves until they reach their common temperature. A run in which one phase takes over gives a new guess, until both last.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import melting_point, minimize

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu"), potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-4
).system

result = melting_point(crystal, potential, 1000.0)
result.temperature, result.error  # 1323 K, 0.7 K
result.attempts  # how the search went

The last run, whose temperature and fraction of solid atoms no longer drift:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, (top, bottom) = plot.figure("single", 100, nrows=2, sharex=True)
    top.plot(result.time, result.temperatures)
    top.axhline(result.temperature, color="0.6", lw=0.8)
    top.set_ylabel("Temperature (K)")
    bottom.plot(result.fraction_time, result.fractions)
    bottom.set_ylabel("Solid fraction")
    bottom.set_xlabel("Time (ps)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/melting-point", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al., 16456 atoms, from a guess of 1000 K. The runs from 1000 and 1150 K froze, and the one from 1322 K kept both phases; its fifth stretch agreed with the fourth and gave 1323 K. Here is its last stretch.

The crystal is repeated to about num_atoms atoms in a box three times as long along its third vector as along the others; the interface lies across that vector. Each run:

  1. brings the crystal to the temperature and the pressure and takes its mean box;
  2. holds one half still and melts the other at constant volume, at twice the temperature, hotter until its atoms have moved by about the distance between them;
  3. cools the melted half to the temperature and lets it settle;
  4. releases the crystal, relaxes the pressure of the box for a moment at this temperature, and runs both at constant enthalpy, in stretches of coexistence, two or more and up to five, until the temperature no longer drifts: neither within the last stretch nor from the one before.

A run that melts started too hot and one that freezes too cold, whatever its temperature became; the next guess is 15 % away, or halfway between two such bounds. A run that keeps both phases but ends with less than a fifth of one, or with a temperature that still drifts, starts again from where its temperature was going.

Solid atoms are told from liquid ones by the order their bonds share, with as many neighbors as the first shell of the crystal has: 12 in fcc and hcp, 14 in bcc, 4 in diamond.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning crystal System the crystal, relaxed, with an element column, periodic in every direction; the interface is across its third vector potential LAMMPS the interaction temperature float64 K the first guess pressure float64 0 GPa the pressure num_atoms int32 16000 about how many atoms the box holds; fewer for a slow potential repeat (3,) int32 repeats of crystal along its vectors, instead of num_atoms; the third is made even timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step equilibration float64 10 ps the time of each stage before the phases meet coexistence float64 500 ps the time of each stretch of the two phases; a larger box needs longer tolerance float64 3 K how much the temperature may still drift, from the third quarter of a stretch to the last and from the stretch before to this one, for it to be the answer; twice its statistical error, if that is larger max_runs int32 8 the largest number of runs barostat_damping float64 1000 time steps ps the damping time of the barostat seed int32 1 the seed of the random numbers progress callable None called as progress(done, total) with the steps run, of a total that takes every run to be the last cancel CancelToken None stops the calculation, which raises Cancelled

The size and the time matter. In a small box the temperature and the interface fluctuate too much, and in a large one heat needs longer to cross it. A slow potential may need less than the default, through num_atoms, repeat and coexistence, at the price of a larger spread. For the copper above, from guesses of 1000, 1327 and 1700 K:

Atoms coexistence (ps) Melting point (K) 4000 100 1328, 1333, 1326 4000 500 1321, 1322, 1321 16000 100 1321, 1322, 1320 16000 500 1325, 1323, 1325

where the free energies of 16384 atoms cross at 1326 K. error is the statistical error of one run and smaller than this spread, so repeating a run with another seed says more about the error than error does.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
It returns a MeltingPointResult; arrays are read-only.

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperature float64 K the melting point: the mean temperature over the second half of the last stretch error float64 K the standard error of that mean, from blocks of the stretch: the statistical error of one run, smaller than the spread of runs from other guesses or seeds pressure float64 GPa the pressure attempts tuple of MeltingAttempt each stretch of each run, in order time (S,) float64 ps the time along the last stretch temperatures (S,) float64 K the temperature along the last stretch pressures (S,) float64 GPa the pressure along the last stretch fractions (F,) float64 the fraction of solid atoms along the last stretch fraction_time (F,) float64 ps the time of the fractions system System the atoms at the end, with a boolean column solid

A MeltingAttempt has start, the temperature in K at which its run started; outcome, "melted", "frozen" or "coexisting"; temperature, its mean temperature in K over its second half; fraction, the fraction of solid atoms at its end; and drift, how much in K its mean temperature changed from its third quarter to its last.

free_energy gives the melting point another way, by where the free energies of the two phases cross.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
melting_point raises InvalidParameter for invalid options, a box not periodic in every direction, half a crystal that does not melt, no run with two phases within max_runs, or if LAMMPS fails; MissingProperty for a crystal without an element column; Cancelled when cancelled.

Please cite

Morris et al. (1994) for the method.

docs.title: Energy minimization
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.minimize(system, calculator, *, max_force=1e-3, max_steps=1000, max_step=0.1, timestep=0.001, cell=None, pressure=0.0, max_stress=1e-2, save_every=None, callback=None) minimizes the energy over the positions, and optionally the box, with FIRE 2.0 (Guénolé et al. (2020)), the fast inertial relaxation engine of Bitzek et al. (2006), as LAMMPS min_style fire does with its default settings.

from mdapy.simulation import minimize

result = minimize(system, potential)  # the positions in a fixed box
result = minimize(system, potential, cell="full")  # and the box
result.system.box, result.stress  # the relaxed box and its stress in GPa
result = minimize(system, potential, cell="isotropic", pressure=10.0)
Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the starting configuration, with a mass or an element column; a movable column, (N, 3) bool as VASP's selective dynamics, keeps each atom still where it is False calculator Calculator computes energies and forces, and the virial when the box relaxes max_force float64 1e-3 eV/Å converged when every force is below it max_steps int32 1000 largest number of steps max_step float64 0.1 Å an atom moving at its current velocity goes at most this far along x, y or z in one step (LAMMPS dmax) timestep float64 0.001 ps first time step of the dynamics (the LAMMPS timestep in metal units) cell str None how the box may change, in the table below pressure float64 0.0 GPa external hydrostatic pressure when the box relaxes max_stress float64 1e-2 GPa when the box relaxes, converged when every relaxed component of the stress is this close to \(-p\) (−pressure on the diagonal, 0 off it) save_every int32 None keeps the configuration every this many steps, with the first and the last, in frames callback callable None called after each step as callback(step, system, energy, max_force); returning True stops the minimization

cell chooses how the box changes along its periodic directions; the atoms move with it, and the lattice vectors along directions that are not periodic stay as they are. At a pressure \(p\) the minimization minimizes the enthalpy \(E + pV\), so the stress of the relaxed box is \(-p\) on the diagonal.

cell The box Relaxed stress components None does not change none "isotropic" is scaled by one factor the mean of the diagonal "axes" is scaled along each Cartesian axis by its own factor the diagonal "full" takes any strain without rotation all

It returns a MinimizeResult:

Attribute Type Meaning system System the last configuration, with forces and atomic_energies columns and energy, virial (eV) and stress (GPa) in info converged bool whether every force fell below max_force and, when the box relaxes, every relaxed stress component came within max_stress of \(-p\) steps int32 number of steps taken energy float64 energy of the last configuration in eV max_force float64 largest force of the last configuration in eV/Å stress (3, 3) float64 or None stress of the last configuration in GPa, positive under tension; None when the calculator does not compute the virial frames tuple of System or None with save_every, the kept configurations, with the columns and info of system and the step as timestep in info; None otherwise

virial and stress are in info, and stress is set, whenever the calculator computes the virial, also when the box does not change.

The steps on the positions are those of LAMMPS: the same time step control, mixing and half step back after an uphill step, with masses from the mass column or, when there is none, the standard atomic weights of the elements. Masses change the path, not the minimum; LAMMPS takes them from the data file or, for EAM, from the potential file. A box relaxation reaches the minimum of LAMMPS fix box/relax (which LAMMPS runs with min_style cg, not FIRE) by another path; LAMMPS keeps its box in restricted triclinic form, so the two boxes agree up to a rotation.

The kept frames show the minimization on its way, with the box and the stress of each step, and can be written as a trajectory:

from mdapy.io import write

result = minimize(system, potential, cell="full", save_every=10)
write("relaxation.xyz", result.frames)

A callback follows the minimization step by step. Copper with every atom displaced at random by about 0.1 Å, relaxed to forces below 1e-4 eV/Å:

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.visualization import plot

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(4, 4, 4))
shake = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 0.1, (len(crystal), 3))
shaken = crystal.with_columns(positions=crystal["positions"] + shake)

steps = []  # step, energy and largest force after each step


def record(step, system, energy, max_force):
    steps.append((step, energy, max_force))


result = minimize(shaken, potential, max_force=1e-4, callback=record)
step, energy, force = np.array(steps).T

with plot.style():
    fig, (top, bottom) = plot.figure("single", 100, nrows=2, sharex=True)
    top.semilogy(step, energy - result.energy)
    top.set_ylabel("Energy above the minimum (eV)")
    bottom.semilogy(step, force)
    bottom.set_ylabel("Largest force (eV/Å)")
    bottom.set_xlabel("Step")
    plot.save(fig, "images/minimize", formats=("png",))

The energy and the largest force fall by orders of magnitude in 121 steps. Each kink is an uphill step: FIRE steps half a step back, stops the atoms and starts again with a shorter time step.

minimize raises InvalidParameter for a non-positive max_force, max_step, timestep, max_stress or save_every, a negative max_steps, an unknown cell, or a calculator that does not compute energies and forces, and the virial when the box relaxes, and MissingProperty for a system with neither masses nor elements.

Please cite

Guénolé et al. (2020) and Bitzek et al. (2006).

docs.title: NEP
docs.text:
NEP(path) reads a neuroevolution potential of version 4 in the nep.txt format of GPUMD, without (nep4) or with (nep4_zbl) a ZBL repulsion, and computes every property.

from mdapy.calculators import NEP

potential = NEP("nep.txt")
result = potential.compute(system, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
descriptors = potential.descriptors(system)  # (N, dim)
Attribute Type Meaning path str the potential file elements tuple of str the elements of the potential, in the order of the file cutoff float64 the largest radial or angular cutoff in Å Method Returns compute(system, properties, *, neighbors=None, progress=None, cancel=None) as every calculator, with the progress= and cancel= of Parallelism descriptors(system, *, neighbors=None, progress=None, cancel=None) (N, dim) descriptors of each atom, scaled as the network sees them: the radial ones, then the angular ones by \(l\) and \(n\), then the four-body and five-body ones by \(n\)

The atoms need an element column; elements the potential does not have raise InvalidParameter. Other models of GPUMD (NEP3, NEP5, charge, dipole and polarizability models) and malformed files raise FileFormatError.

The model is that of GPUMD (Fan et al. (2022)), version 4 (Song et al. (2024)): radial descriptors from Chebyshev functions of the distance, angular ones from real spherical harmonics up to \(l_\text{max}\), with optional four-body and five-body invariants, each scaled by its factor in the file and fed to one hidden layer of \(\tanh\) neurons per element, which gives the energy \(E_i\) of atom \(i\). The cutoff of a pair is the mean of the cutoffs of its two elements. With ZBL, each pair within the angular cutoff adds the screened Coulomb repulsion of Ziegler et al. (1985), \(V(r) = \frac{k_e Z_i Z_j}{r}\,\phi(r/a)\, f_s(r)\), half to each atom; the switch \(f_s\) is 1 below an inner cutoff and falls as a cosine to 0 at an outer cutoff, as the zbl line of the file chooses:

zbl line screening \(\phi\) inner cutoff outer cutoff zbl r1 r2 universal ZBL r1 r2 zbl r1 r2 f universal ZBL 0 the smaller of r2 and f times the sum of the two covalent radii GPUMD uses zbl 0 0 from a table at the end of the file, per pair of elements from the table from the table

As in GPUMD, the derivative of \(E_i\) by the vector to neighbor \(j\) adds to the atomic virial of atom \(j\), so atomic virials are those of GPUMD; EAM shares each pair's virial equally between its two atoms, as LAMMPS does. Both sum to the same virial.

Please cite

Fan et al. (2022) and Song et al. (2024); with ZBL, also Ziegler et al. (1985); and the paper of the potential.

docs.title: Phase diagrams of two elements
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.binary_phase_diagram(phases, temperatures) gives the phase diagram of two elements from the free energies of their phases: at each temperature the stable phases at each composition lie on the lower convex hull of the free energies.

import numpy as np

from mdapy.build import build_crystal, random_alloy
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import binary_phase_diagram, free_energy, minimize

potential = LAMMPS("pair_style nep\npair_coeff * * nep.txt Cu Ni", ["Cu", "Ni"])
temperatures = np.arange(900.0, 2101.0, 25.0)
solid, liquid = {}, {}
for x in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0):
    a = 3.63 * (1 - x) + 3.52 * x
    atoms = random_alloy(
        build_crystal("fcc", a, repeat=(8, 8, 8)), {"Cu": 1 - x, "Ni": x}, seed=7
    )
    atoms = minimize(atoms, potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-2).system
    options = dict(switching=50, scan=200, repeats=2)
    solid[x] = free_energy(atoms, potential, temperatures, mixing=0 < x < 1, **options)
    liquid[x] = free_energy(
        atoms,
        potential,
        temperatures[::-1],
        phase="liquid",
        equilibration=15,
        melt_temperature=2800,
        **options,
    )

diagram = binary_phase_diagram(
    {"fcc": solid, "liquid": liquid},
    np.arange(1100.0, 1701.0, 5.0),
    elements=("Cu", "Ni"),
    degree=3,
)
diagram.phases_at(1400.0, 0.5)  # the stable phases, one or two
diagram.tie_lines[0]  # which two phases, at which fractions

The diagram, with plot.phase_diagram, the region where two phases coexist shaded from its tie lines, and its widest tie line:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    plot.phase_diagram(diagram, ax=ax)
    ties = diagram.tie_lines
    ax.fill_betweenx(
        [t.temperature for t in ties],
        [t.first_fraction for t in ties],
        [t.second_fraction for t in ties],
        color="0.88",
        lw=0,
    )
    widest = max(ties, key=lambda t: t.second_fraction - t.first_fraction)
    ax.plot([widest.first_fraction, widest.second_fraction], [widest.temperature] * 2,
            color="0.4", lw=0.8)  # fmt: skip
    ax.annotate(
        "liquid + fcc",
        (widest.second_fraction, widest.temperature),
        (0.62, 1380),
        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", lw=0.6),
    )
    plot.save(fig, "images/phase-diagram", formats=("png",))

Copper and nickel with the UNEP16 model (Song et al. (2024); Wu et al. (2026)) through the LAMMPS interface of NEP, 2048 atoms at five compositions: a solid solution at all compositions below a lens, as in the experiments. The model melts its elements lower than the experiments do: copper at 1220 K against 1358 K, nickel at 1590 K against 1728 K.

The two lines are the liquidus, above which the alloy is all liquid, and the solidus, below which it is all crystal. Between them, inside the lens, the liquid and the crystal coexist: the free energy of the alloy is lowest as a mixture of a liquid of the fraction on the liquidus and crystals of the fraction on the solidus, the two ends of the tie line at that temperature, in amounts given by the lever rule. On the widest tie line, at 1435 K, an alloy of 40 % Ni is a liquid of 35.5 % Ni and crystals of 44.8 % Ni, half of each. This region has no counterpart in the phase diagram of one element against pressure and temperature, where two phases coexist only on a line: with two elements at one pressure the fraction is one more variable, and two phases coexist over a range of fractions at each temperature. Only a pure element melts at one temperature, where the lines meet.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning phases mapping for each phase, its free energies by the fraction of the second element: each a FreeEnergyResult, or a pair of (T,) temperatures in K and (T,) free energies in eV per atom temperatures array_like K the temperatures of the diagram elements 2 str ("A", "B") the elements, for the labels points int32 1001 the number of fractions from 0 to 1 degree int32 4 the largest degree of the polynomials

A phase of one fraction is a compound of that composition. A phase of more is a solution between its lowest and its highest fractions: at each temperature the free energy minus that of ideal mixing is a polynomial of the fraction, through the given points as closely as its degree allows. Beyond its temperatures a free energy goes on along a straight line; a phase there is usually one that has already lost to another, as a crystal above the temperature to which it stayed a crystal.

The free energies must include the entropy of mixing, which free_energy gives a liquid by itself and a random solid solution with mixing=True. Short-range order in a solid solution, which the dynamics cannot reach, is left out. All free energies must be at one pressure.

For a phase diagram at 0 K of any number of elements, from energies of formation, see the PhaseDiagram of pymatgen, to which a free energy at one temperature can be given as the energy of an entry.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
binary_phase_diagram returns a BinaryPhaseDiagram; arrays are read-only.

Attribute or method Type Meaning elements tuple of str the two elements; the fraction is that of the second phases tuple of str the names of the phases temperatures (T,) float64 the temperatures in K fractions (X,) float64 the fractions of the second element stable (T, X) int64 the index in phases of the one stable phase, or -1 where two coexist tie_lines tuple of TieLine each pair of phases in equilibrium phases_at(temperature, fraction) tuple of str the one or two stable phases at the nearest temperature of the diagram

A TieLine has temperature in K, first and second, the phases, the first at the lower fraction, and first_fraction and second_fraction.

plot.phase_diagram(result, *, ax=None, labels=True) draws where the tie lines end against the temperature, with the name of each phase in the middle of where it is the only one.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
With \(G_p(x, T)\) the free energy per atom of phase \(p\) at a fraction \(x\) of the second element, the stable phases at \(T\) are those on the lower convex hull of all \(G_p(x, T)\) against \(x\). A straight piece of the hull between two points is a tie line: two phases with the same chemical potentials of both elements. A solution has

\[ G(x, T) = \sum_k a_k(T) x^k + k_B T \left[ x \ln x + (1 - x) \ln (1 - x) \right]. \]

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: binary_phase_diagram raises InvalidParameter for no phases, a phase with no free energies, a fraction out of range, no phase at the fractions 0 or 1, free energies with another number of values than temperatures, or invalid temperatures, points, degree or elements. phases_at raises it for a fraction out of range.

docs.title: Phonons
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.phonons(system, calculator, *, supercell=None, displacement=0.01, symmetry=None) gives the harmonic vibrations of a crystal from the forces on atoms displaced in a supercell: frequencies and polarization vectors at any wave vector, band structures, densities of states and the thermodynamic properties of the vibrations.

from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import phonons, primitive_cell
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu"), potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-4
).system
cell = primitive_cell(crystal)  # one atom
result = phonons(cell, potential)

result.frequencies([0.5, 0.5, 0.5])  # THz at L
bands = result.band_structure("fcc")  # Γ–X–U|K–Γ–L–W–X
bands = result.band_structure("auto", connected=True)  # any crystal, with seekpath
dos = result.dos(20)  # states per THz per atom
thermal = result.thermal([100, 300, 600])  # F, E, S, C_V per atom

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure(
        "single", ncols=2, sharey=True, width_ratios=[3, 1]
    )
    plot.band_structure(bands, ax=left)
    plot.phonon_dos(dos, ax=right)
    plot.save(fig, "images/phonons", formats=("png",))

The phonon dispersion of copper along Γ–X–U|K–Γ–L–W–X with the EAM potential, and the density of states beside it.

Relax the crystal first

The force constants are those of the atoms where they are. Relax the positions and the box first, as above: forces left on the atoms, or a stress on the box, change the frequencies, and a crystal away from a minimum of the energy can have imaginary frequencies.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the cell of the crystal, periodic in every direction, or of a sheet, with an element or a mass column; best its primitive cell calculator Calculator computes the forces supercell int32, (3,) int32 or (3, 3) int32 repeats of the cell along its vectors, or the integer matrix whose rows times the vectors of the cell are the vectors of the supercell; by default the supercell nearest a cube that is at least twice the cutoff of the calculator thick in every direction displacement float64 0.01 Å the displacement \(h\) of the atoms symmetry bool or None None move only the atoms and along the axes that symmetry does not relate to others, with the symmetry operations of the crystal, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed

The calculator computes the forces on the supercell six times for each atom of the cell, so the primitive cell is the cheapest: one atom of fcc copper takes 6 computations, its cubic cell of four atoms 24. With the symmetry of the cell, through the operations that map the supercell onto itself, one atom of each set of equivalent atoms moves, along the fewest axes whose images under the operations that keep it in place span space, and by \(-h\) only where no such operation turns the axis around: fcc and bcc take one computation, cubic cell or primitive cell, hcp 2 and L12 3; the forces of the other displacements are images of these. The force constants are the same to rounding where the operations turn axes onto axes, as in cubic crystals; where they turn them by 60°, as in hcp, they differ by the error of the differences, of the order of \(h^2\). A crystal without symmetry, such as a special quasirandom structure, gains nothing. The default supercell is built from the cell whatever its shape: the primitive cell of fcc gives a cube of 4 × 4 × 4 cubic cells for a cutoff of 5.5 Å, the same supercell as the cubic cell gives. The force constants of a supercell reach half across it; the default supercell takes in the interactions within the cutoff, while many-body interactions such as EAM reach twice as far, so a larger supercell may change the frequencies a little.

primitive_cell(system, *, tolerance=1e-4) gives the smallest cell of a crystal: the atoms of one primitive cell, in a box of short lattice vectors of the crystal with the same origin. Atoms are alike when they have the same element, type and mass; tolerance is how far in Å an atom may be from the image of another. A box that is already primitive comes back as it is.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
phonons returns a Phonons. Wave vectors are in units of the reciprocal lattice vectors of the cell: \(\mathbf q = (h, k, l)\) is \(h\mathbf b_1 + k\mathbf b_2 + l\mathbf b_3\), with \(\mathbf a_i\cdot\mathbf b_j = 2\pi\delta_{ij}\).

Attribute or method Type Meaning cell System the crystal whose vibrations these are supercell (3, 3) int64 matrix of the supercell; read-only force_constants (n, nS, 3, 3) float64 force constants \(\Phi\) in eV/Å² between each atom of the cell and each atom of the supercell (S cells, the cell itself first); read-only frequencies(q) (3n,) or (K, 3n) float64 frequencies in THz at one or K wave vectors, ascending; imaginary ones negative modes(q) tuple of float64 and complex128 arrays the frequencies, and the (3n, n, 3) or (K, 3n, n, 3) complex polarization vector of each mode band_structure(path, *, points=51, connected=False) BandStructure the frequencies along a path dos(mesh=20, *, frequencies=None, sigma=None, projected=False) PhononDOS the density of states thermal(temperatures, *, mesh=20) ThermalProperties the thermodynamic properties of the vibrations

Band structures. path is one of:

  • "auto": the standard path of the crystal from its symmetry, any crystal in any orientation, by seekpath (Hinuma et al. (2017)), which must be installed (pip install seekpath); its special points are turned into wave vectors of the cell;
  • "sc", "fcc", "bcc" or "hexagonal": the standard path of that lattice, that of Setyawan and Curtarolo (2010) for sc, bcc and hexagonal and that of seekpath for fcc, without seekpath, for a cell with the axes of its conventional cell along x, y and z, or with a along x and c along z, as build_crystal makes them;
  • the sections of a path by hand, each a list of labeled wave vectors joined by straight lines, [[("Γ", (0, 0, 0)), ("X", (0.5, 0, 0.5))], ...].

points is the number of wave vectors on each line. The frequencies are ascending at each wave vector, so that two branches that cross swap columns there; with connected, each column follows one branch through crossings, by its polarization vector from one wave vector to the next. At points where several branches have the same frequency, as at the special points, their polarization vectors mix, so each branch is followed past them by the vector it had before; at the start of a section, branches of the same frequency are told apart by their order at the next wave vector.

Attribute Type Meaning q (P, 3) float64 the wave vectors distances (P,) float64 their distance along the path in 1/Å frequencies (P, 3n) float64 frequencies in THz, ascending, or a branch in each column when connected labels tuple of (float64, str) the distance and label of each special point; where the path breaks, the two labels join, as in "U\|K" write(path) writes the band structure as phonopy writes band.dat

BandStructure.write writes the format of phonopy's band.dat: the distances of the ends of the lines, then each branch line by line, the distances without the factor 2π as phonopy has them; files of MDAPY and of phonopy, from a calculation with VASP for example, plot the same way. read_band_structure(path) reads such a file into a BandStructure, its distances with the factor 2π, without the wave vectors, which the file does not hold. To draw a band structure of another calculation on one of MDAPY's along the same path, its distances can be moved line by line onto those of MDAPY, which differ as the lattice constants do:

import numpy as np
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import read_band_structure

dft = read_band_structure("band.dat")  # from phonopy
ends = [d for d, _ in dft.labels]
x = np.interp(dft.distances, ends, [d for d, _ in bands.labels])
ax = plot.band_structure(bands)
ax.plot(x, dft.frequencies, color="k", lw=0.8)

Densities of states. The modes on a mesh through Γ of mesh wave vectors along each reciprocal lattice vector give the density by the linear tetrahedron method, or with a Gaussian of width sigma THz for each mode. frequencies are where the density is given, by default 501 from 0 to a little above the highest. Imaginary frequencies, of a crystal that is not stable, show as negative ones, and the default frequencies then start a little below the lowest. With projected, each atom of the cell has its own part.

Attribute Type Meaning frequencies (F,) float64 frequencies in THz dos (F,) float64 states per THz per atom, integrating to 3 projected (F, n) float64 or None the density of each atom of the cell, each integrating to 3, whose mean is dos

Thermodynamic properties. Sums over the modes on the mesh, per atom; modes below 1e-3 THz, the translations of the crystal, are left out. A mode of imaginary frequency has no harmonic free energy: along it the energy falls, so the thermodynamic properties of a crystal with such modes do not exist.

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures free_energy (T,) float64 eV the Helmholtz free energy \(F\) of the vibrations, with the zero-point energy energy (T,) float64 eV their energy \(E\), with the zero-point energy entropy (T,) float64 eV/K their entropy \(S\) heat_capacity (T,) float64 eV/K their heat capacity at constant volume \(C_V\)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: phonons raises InvalidParameter for a box that is not periodic in every direction or has no atoms, an atom with neither element nor mass, a calculator that does not compute forces, a supercell that is not positive integers or a matrix of integers with a positive determinant, a displacement that is not positive, and symmetry=True without spglib; primitive_cell for a box that is not periodic. frequencies and modes raise it for wave vectors that are not three numbers each; band_structure for an unknown lattice, a cell that is not that lattice in the standard orientation, a section of fewer than two wave vectors, or fewer than two points, and ImportError for "auto" without seekpath; dos and thermal for a mesh or a sigma that is not positive, and thermal for a negative temperature and for imaginary frequencies below −0.01 THz on the mesh, which mean that the crystal is not stable or the supercell is too small.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The force constants are central differences of the forces \(\mathbf F\) on the atoms \(j\) of the supercell when atom \(a\) of the first cell moves by \(\pm h\) along \( eta\):

\[ \Phi_{a eta, j\gamma} = - rac{F_{j\gamma}(+h) - F_{j\gamma}(-h)}{2h}, \]

made symmetric, \(\Phi_{a eta,(b,\mathbf L)\gamma} = \Phi_{b\gamma,(a,-\mathbf L) eta}\), and summing to zero over \(j\), so that moving the whole crystal costs no energy. The dynamical matrix of the atoms \(a\) and \(b\) of the cell, of masses \(m_a\) and \(m_b\), is

\[ D_{a eta, b\gamma}(\mathbf q) = rac{1}{\sqrt{m_a m_b}} \sum_{j \in b} \Phi_{a eta, j\gamma}\, rac{1}{N_j} \sum_{\mathbf T} e^{i\mathbf q\cdot(\mathbf r_j + \mathbf T - \mathbf r_a)}, \]

where the sum runs over the atoms \(j\) of the supercell that are copies of \(b\), and \(\mathbf T\) over the \(N_j\) translations of the supercell that put \(j\) nearest to \(a\), all equally near (Born and Huang (1954)). Its eigenvalues are \(\omega^2\), the frequencies \( u = \omega/2\pi\), with the sign of the eigenvalue; its eigenvectors \(\mathbf e\) are the polarization vectors, so that atom \(b\) in the cell at \(\mathbf R\) moves as \(\mathbf e_b\, e^{i\mathbf q\cdot(\mathbf R + \mathbf r_b) - i\omega t}/\sqrt{m_b}\).

The density of states per atom of a cell of \(n\) atoms, over \(K\) wave vectors, is

\[ g( u) = rac{1}{Kn}\sum_{\mathbf q, s} \delta( u - u_{\mathbf q s}), \]

with each delta function spread over the tetrahedra of the mesh between the frequencies at their corners (Blöchl et al. (1994)), or a Gaussian. The projected density of atom \(a\) weighs each mode by \(|\mathbf e_a|^2\), over the corners of each tetrahedron.

With \(x = h u/k_B T\), each mode adds

\[ F = rac{h u}{2} + k_BT\ln(1 - e^{-x}),\quad E = h u\left( rac12 + rac{1}{e^x - 1} ight),\quad S = k_B\left[ rac{x}{e^x - 1} - \ln(1 - e^{-x}) ight],\quad C_V = k_B rac{x^2 e^x}{(e^x - 1)^2}, \]

and the sums over the \(3nK\) modes are divided by \(nK\).

docs.title: Pressure-temperature diagrams
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.pressure_temperature_diagram(phases) gives the phase diagram of one element against pressure and temperature, from the free energies of its phases at each pressure: at each temperature the phase with the lowest free energy is the stable one, and where this changes is a boundary.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import free_energy, minimize, pressure_temperature_diagram
from mdapy.visualization import plot

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(16, 16, 16)),
    potential,
    cell="full",
    max_stress=1e-4,
).system

# around where each pressure melts, not too far above it: a crystal must stay a crystal
windows = {0.0: (1100, 1600), 5.0: (1400, 1700), 10.0: (1600, 1900), 20.0: (1900, 2250)}
options = dict(switching=100, scan=300, repeats=2)
solid, liquid = [], []
for pressure, (low, high) in windows.items():
    temperatures = np.arange(low, high + 1.0, 25.0)
    solid.append(
        free_energy(crystal, potential, temperatures, pressure=pressure, **options)
    )
    liquid.append(
        free_energy(
            crystal,
            potential,
            temperatures[::-1],
            phase="liquid",
            pressure=pressure,
            equilibration=15,
            **options,
        )
    )

diagram = pressure_temperature_diagram({"fcc": solid, "liquid": liquid})
melting = diagram.boundaries[0]
melting.temperatures, melting.slope  # K, K/GPa
diagram.phase_at(10.0, 1650.0), diagram.phase_at(10.0, 1800.0)  # "fcc", "liquid"

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    plot.pressure_temperature(diagram, ax=ax)
    plot.save(fig, "images/pressure-temperature", formats=("png",))

The melting line of copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al., 16384 atoms: 1326 K at 0 GPa, 1526 K at 5 GPa, 1709 K at 10 GPa and 2040 K at 20 GPa, with slopes of 43, 38, 35 and 31 K/GPa. The two-phase method gives 1326, 1525, 1708 and 2035 K at these pressures, with 16456 atoms.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning phases mapping for each name of a phase, its free energies, one per pressure, each a FreeEnergyResult of a run at that pressure points int32 1001 the temperatures of the diagram, from the lowest of the free energies to the highest

Choose the temperatures of each pressure around its boundary. A crystal heated far above its melting point melts during the scan, and free_energy leaves those temperatures out with a warning. A boundary is found along the temperature at each pressure, so one that is nearly flat in temperature, as between two solids, needs pressures close together. One run of a liquid has an error of about 0.25 meV/atom at 2048 atoms, which is about 3 K here, so repeats matters more than a long scan.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
It returns a PressureTemperatureDiagram; arrays are read-only.

Attribute or method Type Unit Meaning phases tuple of str the names of the phases pressures (P,) float64 GPa the pressures temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures stable (P, T) int64 the index in phases of the phase with the lowest free energy of those known there, or -1 where none is boundaries tuple of PhaseBoundary each pair of phases in equilibrium phase_at(pressure, temperature) str or None the stable phase at the nearest pressure and temperature of the diagram

A PhaseBoundary:

Attribute Type Unit Meaning first, second str the phases, the first stable below the temperature of the boundary and the second above it pressures (B,) float64 GPa the pressures temperatures (B,) float64 K the temperature of the boundary at each pressure latent_heat (B,) float64 eV per atom the change of enthalpy from the first to the second volume (B,) float64 Å³ per atom the change of volume from the first to the second slope (B,) float64 K/GPa \(\mathrm{d}T/\mathrm{d}P\) by the Clausius-Clapeyron relation

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
At each pressure the stable phase has the lowest Gibbs free energy \(G(T, P)\), and two phases coexist where theirs are equal. Along such a boundary

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}T}{\mathrm{d}P} = \frac{T \Delta V}{\Delta H}, \]

the Clausius-Clapeyron relation, with \(\Delta V\) and \(\Delta H\) the changes of the volume and the enthalpy from one phase to the other.

plot.pressure_temperature(result, *, ax=None, labels=True) draws the boundaries, with the names of the phases where each is stable.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
pressure_temperature_diagram raises InvalidParameter for fewer than two phases, too few points, a free energy without a pressure, or two free energies of one phase at one pressure.

Please cite

Freitas et al. (2016) for the free energies.

docs.title: Quasi-harmonic approximation
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.quasi_harmonic(system, calculator, temperatures, *, volumes=None, pressures=None, pressure=0.0, supercell=None, mesh=20, displacement=0.01, max_force=1e-6, max_stress=1e-4, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None) gives the thermal expansion, bulk modulus, heat capacity and Gibbs energy of a crystal at finite temperature from its phonons at several volumes.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import primitive_cell, quasi_harmonic
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu"),
    potential,
    cell="full",
    max_stress=1e-4,
).system
result = quasi_harmonic(primitive_cell(crystal), potential, np.arange(0, 1001, 50))
result.volume  # Å³ per atom at each temperature
result.thermal_expansion / 3  # linear thermal expansion coefficient, 1/K
result.bulk_modulus  # GPa
result.heat_capacity  # C_P, eV/K per atom

The lattice parameter of copper, four atoms to its cubic cell, and the linear thermal expansion coefficient:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

t = result.temperatures
with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure("double", ncols=2)
    left.plot(t, (4 * result.volume) ** (1 / 3))
    left.set_xlabel("Temperature (K)")
    left.set_ylabel("Lattice parameter (Å)")
    right.plot(t, result.thermal_expansion / 3 * 1e6)
    right.set_xlabel("Temperature (K)")
    right.set_ylabel(r"Linear thermal expansion ($10^{-6}$/K)")
    plot.save(fig, "images/quasi-harmonic", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al.: at 0 K the zero-point vibrations already widen the lattice a little beyond its static 3.615 Å; it grows slowly at first, while the vibrations freeze out, then nearly linearly. The expansion coefficient rises from 0 and keeps growing slowly above the Debye temperature.

At each volume the box keeps its volume while its shape and the positions relax, so that a crystal whose shape changes with the volume, such as hcp with its c/a, takes its best shape at each; the phonons then give the free energy of the vibrations. The volumes must hold the equilibrium volume at every temperature: the default, from 0.97 to 1.09 times the volume of system, reaches the melting point of most metals. Instead of volumes, pressures relax the box and the positions under each pressure. The cells of the grid are kept, for elastic constants at finite temperature.

The quasi-harmonic approximation leaves out the anharmonic vibrations beyond the change of the frequencies with the volume, so it holds well below the melting point; near it, molecular dynamics is needed. The bulk modulus comes from the curvature of a fit through the volumes; with the default nine volumes it is good to about 1 %.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning system System the cell of the crystal, periodic in every direction, with an element or a mass column; best relaxed and primitive calculator Calculator computes energies and forces temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures, not negative volumes (V,) float64 9 from 0.97 to 1.09 the volumes of the phonons, as ratios to the volume of system; five or more pressures (V,) float64 GPa instead of volumes, the pressures under which the box and the positions relax; five or more pressure float64 0 GPa the pressure \(P\) supercell int32 or (3,) int32 repeats of the cell for the phonons, as in phonons mesh int32 or (3,) int32 20 wave vectors along each reciprocal lattice vector for the thermal properties displacement float64 0.01 Å displacement of the atoms for the force constants max_force float64 1e-6 eV/Å convergence of the relaxation at each volume max_stress float64 1e-4 GPa convergence of the relaxation of the box max_steps int32 5000 largest number of steps of each relaxation symmetry bool or None None use the symmetry operations of the crystal, found by spglib, in the phonons, as in phonons: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed
