docs.text:
It returns a QuasiHarmonicResult, all per atom; arrays are read-only.

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures pressure float64 GPa the pressure volume (T,) float64 Å³ the equilibrium volume \(V(T)\) gibbs_energy (T,) float64 eV the Gibbs energy \(G(T, P)\) entropy (T,) float64 eV/K the entropy \(S\) bulk_modulus (T,) float64 GPa the isothermal bulk modulus \(B_T\) thermal_expansion (T,) float64 1/K the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient \(\alpha\); a third of it is the linear one of a cubic crystal heat_capacity (T,) float64 eV/K the heat capacity at constant pressure \(C_P\) volumes (V,) float64 Å³ the volumes of the phonons energies (V,) float64 eV the static energy at each volume free_energies (V, T) float64 eV the free energy of the vibrations at each volume and temperature cells tuple of System the relaxed cell at each volume

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: quasi_harmonic raises InvalidParameter for a negative temperature, both volumes and pressures, fewer than five of them, a relaxation that does not converge within max_steps, imaginary frequencies at a volume, and an equilibrium volume outside the volumes, as well as for the errors of phonons. It also raises it, before any phonons, for a pair of atoms that comes within displacement of the cutoff of the calculator at some volumes and not at others: the force constants of most potentials, NEP and tabulated EAM among them, jump there, and the free energy with them. Narrow the volumes or the pressures, or choose another potential.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
At each temperature \(T\), the free energy

\[ F(V, T) = E(V) + F_\mathrm{vib}(V, T) + PV, \]

with \(E\) the static energy and \(F_\mathrm{vib}\) the harmonic free energy of the vibrations at volume \(V\), is fit by the third-order Birch–Murnaghan form, a cubic polynomial in \(V^{-2/3}\), by least squares. Its minimum is the equilibrium volume \(V(T)\) and the Gibbs energy \(G = F(V(T), T)\), its curvature there the bulk modulus \(B_T = V\,\partial^2F/\partial V^2\). The entropy \(S_\mathrm{vib}\) and the heat capacity \(C_V\) of the vibrations, fit alike, give at \(V(T)\)

\[ S = S_\mathrm{vib}, \qquad \alpha = \frac{1}{B_T}\left(\frac{\partial S_\mathrm{vib}}{\partial V}\right)_T, \qquad C_P = C_V + T V B_T \alpha^2. \]

docs.title: Sheets
docs.text:
Elastic constants and phonons of two-dimensional materials such as graphene. A box that is periodic along two vectors in the x-y plane and not along a third along z makes a system a sheet; nothing else changes in the calls.

import mdapy
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import elastic_constants, phonons
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

potential = LAMMPS("pair_style lcbop\npair_coeff * * C.lcbop C", elements=["C"])
crystal = build_crystal("graphene", 2.46, c=20.0, elements="C")
sheet = crystal.with_box(mdapy.Box(crystal.box.matrix, pbc=(True, True, False)))
sheet = minimize(sheet, potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-3).system

elastic = elastic_constants(sheet, potential)
elastic.constants  # (3, 3) N/m: 331, 73 and 129
elastic.young_modulus(), elastic.poisson_ratio()  # 315 N/m, 0.22

result = phonons(sheet, potential)
bands = result.band_structure("hexagonal")  # Γ-M-K-Γ
dos = result.dos(100)  # the mesh is 100 x 100 x 1
thermal = result.thermal([100, 300, 1000], mesh=100)  # F, E, S, C_V per atom

The phonons of graphene, drawn with the same calls as those of a crystal:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure(
        "single", ncols=2, sharey=True, width_ratios=[3, 1]
    )
    plot.band_structure(bands, ax=left)
    plot.phonon_dos(dos, ax=right)
    plot.save(fig, "images/sheets", formats=("png",))

Graphene with the LCBOP potential of LAMMPS. The lowest branch near Γ, the vibration across the sheet, is quadratic; the two above it are linear.

The height of the box does not matter and the atoms need no vacuum around them: a sheet has no images along z. A calculator that always takes the box as periodic, such as VASP, needs a box high enough that the images of the sheet do not meet.

docs.title: Elastic constants
docs.text:
elastic_constants strains the sheet along xx, yy and xy only and returns a SheetElasticResult, per unit of the area of the sheet, so that no thickness has to be chosen. The parameters are those of elastic_constants.

Attribute or method Type Meaning constants (3, 3) float64 elastic constants \(C\) in N/m, in the order xx, yy, xy; read-only young_modulus(axis="x") float64 the Young's modulus in N/m along "x" or "y" poisson_ratio(axis="x") float64 the contraction across a stretch along "x" or "y", over the stretch shear_modulus() float64 the shear modulus in N/m area_modulus() float64 the area modulus in N/m: the tension per unit of relative change of the area

With \(S = C^{-1}\) these are

\[ E_x = \frac{1}{S_{11}}, \quad E_y = \frac{1}{S_{22}}, \quad \nu_x = -\frac{S_{12}}{S_{11}}, \quad \nu_y = -\frac{S_{12}}{S_{22}}, \quad G = \frac{1}{S_{33}}, \quad K = \frac{1}{S_{11} + S_{22} + 2 S_{12}}. \]

docs.title: Phonons
docs.text:
phonons takes the parameters and returns the Phonons of a crystal, with these differences:

  • supercell repeats the cell along its plane only: one integer means both vectors, three integers end in 1, and by default it is the supercell nearest a square at least twice the cutoff of the calculator wide;
  • a mesh of one integer in dos and thermal means the plane, and three integers end in 1. The vibrations across the sheet make the thermal properties converge slowly with the mesh, so a mesh of 100 is a good start;
  • the paths "auto" and "hexagonal" of band_structure keep the sections in the plane: Γ-M-K-Γ for a hexagonal sheet.

primitive_cell takes a sheet and gives the primitive cell of its plane, in a box of the same height.

docs.title: In gigapascals
docs.text: A sheet has no thickness of its own, so its constants are in N/m. With a thickness \(h\) chosen by convention, such as the 3.35 Å between the layers of graphite, the constants of a material of that thickness are \(C[\mathrm{GPa}] = 10\, C[\mathrm{N/m}] / h[\text{Å}]\): 331 N/m is 988 GPa.

docs.title: Molecular dynamics
docs.text:
MolecularDynamics runs a sheet as it is. barostat="xy" controls the pressure in the plane and keeps the height of the box:

from mdapy.simulation import MolecularDynamics

with MolecularDynamics(sheet, potential) as md:
    md.velocities(600.0, seed=1)
    md.run(20000, ensemble="npt", temperature=300.0, pressure=0.0, barostat="xy")

LAMMPS divides the forces by the volume of the box, with its vacuum. A tension of \(\sigma\) in N/m is therefore the pressure \(-10\, \sigma / h\) GPa, with the height of the box \(h\) in Å; at zero pressure the height does not matter.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
elastic_constants, phonons and primitive_cell raise InvalidParameter for a box that is not periodic in every direction and is not that of a sheet. phonons raises it for a supercell that leaves the plane, dos and thermal for a mesh with more than one wave vector along z. The methods of SheetElasticResult raise it for an axis other than "x" or "y" and for constants that cannot be inverted.

quasi_harmonic and elastic constants from molecular dynamics need a box periodic in every direction: a sheet has no volume to scan. The moduli of ElasticResult, for a sheet in a periodic box with vacuum, raise InvalidParameter, as its constants cannot be inverted.

docs.title: Stacking faults at finite temperature
docs.text:
mdapy.simulation.stacking_fault_free_energy(crystal, potential, direction, temperatures) gives the free energy of a stacking fault per area at each temperature: the difference of the free energies of the crystal with and without it, in one box of the size the crystal has at that temperature and pressure. The energy at rest is the business of stacking_fault_energy.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.simulation import minimize, stacking_fault_free_energy

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
a = 3.615
layers = minimize(
    build_crystal(
        "fcc",
        a,
        elements="Cu",
        orientation=[(1, 1, -2), (-1, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1)],
        repeat=(6, 10, 4),
    ),
    potential,
    cell="axes",  # keeps the plane normal to z, whatever the rounding of a potential
    max_stress=1e-3,
).system

result = stacking_fault_free_energy(
    layers,
    potential,
    [a * np.sqrt(6) / 6, 0, 0],  # 1/6 [11-2]
    [230, 460, 690, 920, 1150],
    repeats=8,
)
result.energy, result.error  # J/m²

The harmonic part of the same difference, for comparison: classical atoms in the phonons of a perfect and a faulted cell of 24 (111) layers, each at the volume per atom of the crystal at that temperature. The free energy of the vibrations of classical atoms is \(k_BT\sum\ln(h\nu/k_BT)\) over the modes, so the difference of two cells of as many atoms is \(k_BT\) times the difference of their sums of \(\ln\nu\), here averaged over a mesh of wave vectors that misses Γ. At 0 K only the static part is left, the fault at rest:

from mdapy import units
from mdapy.build import slip
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import phonons

grid = (np.arange(10) + 0.5) / 10
mesh = [[x, y, z] for x in grid for y in grid for z in (0.25, 0.75)]
harmonic = []
for temperature, volume in zip([0, *result.temperatures], [a**3 / 4, *result.volume]):
    side = (4 * volume) ** (1 / 3)  # the lattice constant at this temperature
    perfect = build_crystal(
        "fcc",
        side,
        elements="Cu",
        orientation=[(1, 1, -2), (-1, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1)],
        repeat=(1, 1, 8),
    )
    faulted = slip(perfect, [side * np.sqrt(6) / 6, 0, 0])  # the box tilts with it
    energy, logs = [], []
    for cell in (perfect, faulted):
        cell = minimize(cell, potential, max_force=1e-5).system
        frequencies = phonons(cell, potential, supercell=(4, 7, 1)).frequencies(mesh)
        energy.append(potential.compute(cell).energy)
        logs.append(np.log(frequencies).sum(axis=1).mean())
    kt = units.BOLTZMANN * temperature
    area = perfect.box.matrix[0, 0] * perfect.box.matrix[1, 1]
    difference = energy[1] - energy[0] + kt * (logs[1] - logs[0])
    harmonic.append(difference / area * units.EV_PER_A2_TO_J_PER_M2)

The fault gets cheaper with the temperature:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    every = [0, *result.temperatures]
    ax.plot(every, 1e3 * np.array(harmonic), "--", color="0.6", label="harmonic")
    ax.plot(0, 1e3 * harmonic[0], "s", color="0.25", label="at rest")
    ax.errorbar(
        result.temperatures,
        1e3 * result.energy,
        1e3 * result.error,
        fmt="o",
        capsize=2,
        label="free energy",
    )
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="0.75", lw=0.5, zorder=0)
    ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (K)")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"Stacking fault energy (mJ/m$^2$)")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/stacking-fault-temperature", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al., 1440 atoms and a plane of 684 Å², 44 mJ/m² at rest. Up to about 500 K the free energy follows the harmonic part; above that it falls more slowly: 23 mJ/m² against -5 mJ/m² at 1150 K. The harmonic part leaves out the anharmonic vibrations, which the switching of the free energy takes in.

The wider the plane the smaller the error: the error of the free energy of all atoms grows with their square root, the free energy of the fault with the area. The error also grows towards the melting point, where 192 atoms of this copper gave ±33 mJ/m² at 1250 K against ±7 mJ/m² at 1040 K: look at error and dissipation. The crystal must keep its fault during the runs: a slip vector that leads to no minimum of the energy, as a partial in a potential with no stable stacking fault, slides back, and gives something lower than the energy at rest.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning crystal System the crystal, relaxed, with an element column, periodic in every direction, with the plane of the fault normal to the Cartesian axis of axis, such as fcc with z along [111] potential LAMMPS the interaction direction (3,) float64 Å (3,) the slip vector in the plane, such as a/6 [11-2] temperatures float64 or (T,) float64 K the temperatures height float64 between the two layers nearest the middle the fault, as a fractional coordinate along the box vector of axis axis int32 or str z the Cartesian axis normal to the fault pressure float64 0 GPa the pressure timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step equilibration float64 10 ps the time of each equilibration switching float64 50 ps the time of each switching between the crystal and the springs repeats int32 4 independent free energies of each crystal at each temperature max_force float64 1e-4 eV/Å convergence of the relaxation of the fault at each size of the box max_steps int32 10000 the largest number of steps of each relaxation seed int32 1 the seed of the random numbers progress callable None called as progress(done, total) with the steps run cancel CancelToken None stops the calculation, which raises Cancelled

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures energy (T,) float64 J/m² the free energy of the fault per area error (T,) float64 J/m² its standard error from the repeats; zero for one repeat area float64 Å² the area of the fault at the first temperature volume (T,) float64 Å³ the volume per atom of the crystal dissipation (T,) float64 eV half the difference of the work there and back per atom, the largest over the runs

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
\[ \gamma(T) = \frac{F_\mathrm{fault}(T) - F_\mathrm{crystal}(T)}{A}, \]

where both free energies are those of free_energy for solids, of the same atoms in one box but for the box vector that the fault tilts. Classical atoms, as in molecular dynamics. With the phonons of the two cells, the harmonic part of this difference is cheaper and free of noise, but it gets worse with the temperature.

docs.text:

Please cite

docs.title: Elastic constants at finite temperature
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.thermal_elastic_constants(qha, calculator, *, method="quasi-harmonic", strain=5e-3, supercell=None, mesh=20, displacement=0.01, max_force=1e-6, max_steps=5000, symmetry=None) gives the isothermal and adiabatic elastic constants of a crystal at the temperatures of a quasi-harmonic calculation.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import (
    primitive_cell,
    quasi_harmonic,
    thermal_elastic_constants,
)

cell = primitive_cell(crystal)  # relaxed, as for the phonons
qha = quasi_harmonic(cell, potential, np.arange(0, 901, 100))
result = thermal_elastic_constants(qha, potential)
result.isothermal[:, 0, 0]  # C11 in GPa at each temperature
result.adiabatic[:, 3, 3]  # C44
fast = thermal_elastic_constants(qha, potential, method="quasi-static")

The isothermal constants of copper by both methods:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

t = qha.temperatures
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    for name, (i, j) in {"C11": (0, 0), "C12": (0, 1), "C44": (3, 3)}.items():
        (line,) = ax.plot(t, result.isothermal[:, i, j], label=name)
        ax.plot(t, fast.isothermal[:, i, j], ":", color=line.get_color())
    ax.set_xlabel("Temperature (K)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Isothermal elastic constant (GPa)")
    ax.legend()
    plot.save(fig, "images/thermal-elastic", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al., quasi-harmonic (solid) and quasi-static (dotted): the crystal softens as it heats. The quasi-static constants, which see only the expansion, soften less; at low temperature the zero-point vibrations make the quasi-harmonic ones a little stiffer.

The elastic constants at a temperature are the second derivatives of the free energy with respect to strain, at the volume of that temperature. They are found in the cells of the quasi-harmonic grid around the volumes of the temperatures, two more on either side, and taken at each volume by a cubic polynomial through those cells.

  • "quasi-harmonic": the free energy is the static energy and the free energy of the vibrations, from the phonons of each strained cell. This takes 73 phonon calculations for each cell, a few seconds with an EAM potential.
  • "quasi-static": the static energy alone, at the volume of each temperature; the crystal softens only as it expands. Without phonons, it is much faster, and close to the quasi-harmonic constants well below the melting point, but stiffer as it nears.
Name Type Default Unit Meaning qha QuasiHarmonicResult the quasi-harmonic calculation, with its cells calculator Calculator computes energies and forces, as for the quasi-harmonic calculation method str "quasi-harmonic" "quasi-harmonic" or "quasi-static" strain float64 5e-3 the magnitude \(h\) of the Lagrangian strains of the finite differences supercell, mesh, displacement of the phonons of the strained cells, as in phonons max_force float64 1e-6 eV/Å convergence of the relaxation of the positions in each strained cell max_steps int32 5000 largest number of steps of each relaxation symmetry bool or None None compute one of each set of strains that the operations make from each other, and use symmetry in the phonons; with the symmetry operations of the crystal, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed

A cubic crystal takes 12 of the 73 strains of the differences, hcp 36. The strained cells keep the supercell of their cell and the periodic images its force constants go to, so that their free energies change smoothly with the strain, even in a supercell thinner than the force constants reach.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A ThermalElasticResult; arrays are read-only.

Attribute Type Unit Meaning temperatures (T,) float64 K the temperatures isothermal (T, 6, 6) float64 GPa the isothermal elastic constants \(C^T\), in Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy adiabatic (T, 6, 6) float64 GPa the adiabatic elastic constants \(C^S\), those of sound waves method str the method

Under a pressure, the constants are the stress–strain coefficients, which give the speed of sound and the stability of the crystal under it.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: thermal_elastic_constants raises InvalidParameter for an unknown method, a strain that is not positive, a result without cells, a relaxation that does not converge within max_steps, imaginary frequencies in a strained cell, and symmetry=True without spglib. With the quasi-harmonic method it also raises it, before any phonons, for a pair of atoms that comes within displacement of the cutoff of the calculator in some strained cells and not in others, where the force constants jump, as in quasi_harmonic; a smaller strain avoids it.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
A cell of the grid, of volume \(V\), is deformed by the Lagrangian strain \(\eta\) as \(\sqrt{1 + 2\eta}\), its positions relax, and

\[ C_{ij} = \frac{1}{V}\frac{\partial^2 F}{\partial\eta_i\,\partial\eta_j}, \]

in Voigt notation with engineering shears, by central differences of step \(h\); \(F\) is the static energy \(E\) and, but for the quasi-static method, the free energy of the vibrations. Under a pressure \(P\) the stress–strain coefficients are \(B_{ijkl} = C_{ijkl} - P(\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl} + \delta_{il}\delta_{jk} - \delta_{ij}\delta_{kl})\). With the thermal expansion tensor \(\alpha\), from the cells of the grid against volume, and the heat capacity at constant volume \(C_V\), the adiabatic constants are

\[ C^S_{ij} = C^T_{ij} + \frac{T V \lambda_i\lambda_j}{C_V}, \qquad \lambda_i = \sum_k C^T_{ik}\,\alpha_k \]

(Wallace (1972)).

docs.title: Phonons at finite temperature
docs.text:
mdapy.lattice_dynamics.thermal_phonons(cell, potential, temperature) gives the phonons of a crystal at a temperature from molecular dynamics in LAMMPS: the force constants that best give the forces on the moving atoms. They hold what harmonic phonons leave out: the vibrations feel the crystal away from its minimum, and the box has the size it has at that temperature. phonons_from_frames does the same with frames from any dynamics, such as ab initio molecular dynamics.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import LAMMPS
from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import phonons, primitive_cell, thermal_phonons
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

potential = LAMMPS(
    "pair_style eam/alloy\npair_coeff * * Cu_mishin1.eam.alloy Cu", elements=["Cu"]
)
crystal = minimize(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu"), potential, cell="full", max_stress=1e-4
).system
cell = primitive_cell(crystal)

cold = phonons(cell, potential)
hot = thermal_phonons(cell, potential, 1000.0)  # a Phonons, as phonons gives
hot.band_structure("fcc")
hot.dos(20)
hot.thermal([1000.0])

The result is a Phonons: its frequencies, band structures, densities of states and thermal properties are read as those of harmonic phonons.

The bands of copper at rest and hot. The hot crystal is larger, so its path through the Brillouin zone is shorter in reciprocal space; its bands are drawn along the path of the crystal at rest, stretched by the ratio of the lengths, so that the special points meet:

from mdapy.visualization import plot

at_rest = cold.band_structure("fcc")
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure("single")
    for result, name, color in ((cold, "at rest", "0.6"), (hot, "1000 K", "#0072B2")):
        bands = result.band_structure("fcc")
        along = bands.distances * at_rest.distances[-1] / bands.distances[-1]
        lines = ax.plot(along, bands.frequencies, color=color, lw=1.2)
        lines[0].set_label(name)
    bands = at_rest
    ax.set_xticks([d for d, _ in bands.labels], [label for _, label in bands.labels])
    for d, _ in bands.labels:
        ax.axvline(d, color="0.8", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlim(bands.distances[0], bands.distances[-1])
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_ylabel("Frequency (THz)")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
    plot.save(fig, "images/thermal-phonons", formats=("png",))

Copper with the EAM potential of Mishin et al.: the bands at rest, and at 1000 K, softer by 10 to 15 %, as the crystal has expanded and the atoms feel their neighbors further from where they rest.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning cell System the cell of the crystal, relaxed, periodic in every direction, with an element column; best its primitive cell potential LAMMPS the interaction temperature float64 K the temperature supercell int32, (3,) int32 or (3, 3) int32 as in phonons; by default the supercell nearest a cube that is at least twice the cutoff of the potential thick in every direction pressure float64 or None 0 GPa the pressure at which the box takes its mean size first, with the symmetry of the crystal; None to keep the box of cell timestep float64 0.001 ps the time step equilibration float64 10 ps the time of each equilibration production float64 100 ps the time over which the frames are taken num_frames int32 200 the number of frames symmetry bool or None None average the force constants over the symmetry operations of the crystal, found by spglib: True, False, or by default whenever spglib is installed seed int32 1 the seed of the random numbers progress callable None called as progress(done, total) with the steps run cancel CancelToken None stops the calculation, which raises Cancelled

The cell of the result has the mean box at the temperature. The vibrations are those of classical atoms, as in molecular dynamics, so well below the Debye temperature harmonic phonons with the quasi-harmonic approximation are better.

docs.title: From frames of any dynamics
docs.text:
phonons_from_frames(cell, frames, *, supercell, symmetry=None) takes the atoms of the supercell with a forces column, in the order phonons makes them: cells of atoms in the order of cell, the third vector varying fastest. Frames are best far enough apart in time to differ.

from mdapy.lattice_dynamics import phonons_from_frames

result = phonons_from_frames(cell, frames, supercell=4)
Name Type Default Meaning cell System the cell of the crystal with the atoms at their places at the volume of the frames, periodic in every direction, with an element or a mass column frames iterable of System the atoms of the supercell, with forces supercell int32, (3,) int32 or (3, 3) int32 repeats of the cell symmetry bool or None None as above

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
With \(u_i\) the displacement of atom \(i\) from its place and \(f_i\) the force on it, the force constants \(\Phi\) minimize

\[ \sum_\mathrm{frames} \sum_i \Big| f_i + \sum_{j \ne i} \Phi_{ij} (u_j - u_i) \Big|^2, \]

the same in every cell of the supercell, so that the crystal can translate freely (Hellman et al. (2011)). They are then made symmetric under the exchange of the atoms of a pair and, with symmetry, averaged over the symmetry operations of the crystal.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
thermal_phonons raises InvalidParameter for a box that is not periodic in every direction, a temperature or a time that is not positive, a potential that is not a LAMMPS calculator, too few frames for the force constants, or if LAMMPS fails; MissingProperty for a system without an element column; Cancelled when cancelled. phonons_from_frames raises InvalidParameter for a frame with another number of atoms, too few frames or an invalid supercell, and MissingProperty for a frame without forces.

Please cite

Hellman et al. (2011) for the method.

docs.title: VASP
docs.text:
from mdapy.calculators import VASP
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

vasp = VASP(
    {"ENCUT": 520, "EDIFF": 1e-6, "ISMEAR": 1, "SIGMA": 0.1, "NCORE": 8},
    kpoints=(4, 4, 4),
    setups={"Ni": "Ni_pv"},
    command="srun vasp_std",  # as the job script of the cluster runs VASP
    directory="relax",
)
result = vasp.compute(system, ("energy", "forces", "virial"))
relaxed = minimize(system, vasp, max_force=0.01).system

VASP(incar=None, *, kpoints=None, potcars=None, setups=None, command=None, directory="vasp", restart=True) makes VASP a calculator: each call writes POSCAR, INCAR, KPOINTS and POTCAR in the directory, runs VASP there with the command and reads the energy, forces and stress of its OUTCAR. A Python script on a cluster, in the job script, so drives VASP through minimize, elastic constants or defect energies as any other calculator.

Name Type Default Unit Meaning incar mapping None INCAR tags; NSW, IBRION and ISIF are set for a single point with the stress and may not be given kpoints (3,) int32 None a Gamma-centered mesh of k-points; without it VASP takes KSPACING from the INCAR potcars path $VASP_PP_PATH or its potpaw_PBE the folder of the POTCARs, one folder per element or setup setups mapping None the POTCAR of an element when not its symbol, such as {"Ti": "Ti_sv"} command str $MDAPY_VASP_COMMAND, $ASE_VASP_COMMAND or "vasp_std" the command that runs VASP in the directory, such as "mpirun -np 128 vasp_std" directory path "vasp" where VASP runs, made when missing restart bool True keep WAVECAR and CHGCAR between calls, so that each run starts from the wave functions of the last Attribute or method Meaning cutoff 0: VASP needs no neighbor list compute(system, properties, *, neighbors=None) the free energy (TOTEN) in eV, forces in eV/Å and virial in eV; neighbors is not used

The system needs an element column. VASP holds the atoms of each element together: the POSCAR lists the elements in the order they first appear, the POTCAR follows it, and the forces come back in the order of the atoms of the system. Python booleans become .TRUE. and .FALSE. in the INCAR, and sequences numbers separated by spaces, as for MAGMOM.

The constructor raises InvalidParameter for NSW, IBRION or ISIF in the INCAR and k-points that are not three positive integers; compute raises InvalidParameter without POTCARs or for an element without its POTCAR, MissingProperty without an element column, and CalculationFailed when VASP stops with an error or leaves no converged electronic step, with the end of what VASP wrote.

Please cite

Kresse and Furthmüller (1996).

docs.title: Coloring atoms
docs.text:
Three functions color the atoms of a system and keep the colors in its color column, which render draws by default and the next coloring starts from:

Function Colors As OVITO's color_coding(system, column, *, colormap="rainbow", value_range=None, atoms=None) by the values of a column through a colormap color coding color_by_type(system, column, *, atoms=None) one color for each value of a column color by type assign_color(system, color, *, atoms=None) in one color assign color

Each colors all atoms, or those given as atoms, a mask such as System.where gives, or indices; the others keep the colors they had.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.visualization import (
    assign_color,
    atom_colors,
    atom_radii,
    color_by_type,
    color_coding,
    render,
)

alloy = build_crystal("fcc", 3.6, elements="Cu", repeat=(8, 8, 8))
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
alloy = alloy.with_columns(element=rng.choice(["Cu", "Ni", "Al"], size=len(alloy)))

by_height = color_coding(alloy, "positions.z")  # rainbow from bottom to top
by_element = color_by_type(alloy, "element")
layer = alloy.where("positions.z > 12 and positions.z < 16")
marked = assign_color(by_element, "#222222", atoms=layer)

The three systems drawn, each with a legend. A color column holds colors only, so the legend is told what they mean: a bar needs the values and the colormap, and colors of types a mapping of names to colors:

from mdapy.visualization import write_png

element = np.asarray(alloy["element"])
kinds = {kind: by_element["color"][element == kind][0] for kind in np.unique(element)}
options = dict(view="iso", width=520, height=400)
write_png(
    "images/colors.png",
    np.hstack(
        [
            render(
                by_height,
                color=alloy["positions.z"],
                colormap="rainbow",
                legend="z (Å)",
                **options,
            ),
            render(by_element, legend=kinds, **options),
            render(marked, legend=kinds | {"the layer": "#222222"}, **options),
        ]
    ),
)

Left: rainbow from the lowest to the highest z, drawn from the values with the same colormap. Middle: one color for each of Al, Cu and Ni. Right: a layer in dark gray over the colors by element.

docs.text:
Name Type Default Meaning column str for color_coding, a column of numbers, a component such as "velocities.z" or an expression; for color_by_type, a column of one component, such as "element", "type" or "cluster", or an expression colormap str "rainbow" one of COLORMAPS value_range (float64, float64) finite range the values at the ends of the colormap; by default the lowest and highest finite value of the atoms colored; values beyond take the color of their end color color "#rrggbb", a name such as "red", or three numbers from 0 to 1 atoms mask or indices all the atoms colored

color_by_type gives the values, in increasing order, the colors of LABEL_COLORS in turn: twelve distinct colors, the thirteenth value taking the first again.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Each returns the system with the (N, 3) colors from 0 to 1 in its color column; its other columns as they are.

docs.title: The colors and radii of atoms
docs.text:
atom_colors(system, color=None, *, colormap="viridis", value_range=None, elements=None) gives the (N, 3) colors render draws: those of color as render takes it, by default the color column, or without one the colors of the elements, those given in elements, such as {"Cu": "#d4875a"}, in place of their own. atom_radii(system, kind="display", *, elements=None, scale=1.0) gives the (N,) radii in Å: the radius column, or without one those of the elements of that kind ("display", "covalent" or "vdw"), those given in elements in place of their own; each times scale.

A system with a type column and no element column, as a LAMMPS dump of id type x y z, has its atom types in place of the elements, named Type 1, Type 2 and so on: each in a color of its own, as OVITO's, type k taking TYPE_COLORS[(k - 1) % 9], and all of one radius, as types say nothing of their sizes. elements takes those names, such as {"Type 2": "#222222"}; atom_names(system) gives the name of each atom, atoms of the element X named after their type too.

To give the types their elements, read the file with elements=: the colors and radii are then those of the elements, and files written from it hold them.

from mdapy.io import read_trajectory, write
from mdapy.visualization import atom_names

typed = alloy.with_columns(type=np.arange(len(alloy)) % 2 + 1).drop("element")
write("types.dump", typed)
frames = read_trajectory("types.dump", elements=["Cu", "X"])
print(sorted(set(atom_names(frames[0]))))  # ['Cu', 'Type 2']

colors = atom_colors(alloy, elements={"Al": "#9ecae1"})
radii = atom_radii(alloy, elements={"Al": 1.0}, scale=0.8)
picture = render(alloy, color=colors, radius=radii, width=400, height=400)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: InvalidParameter for an unknown colormap or color, a column of text for color_coding, a column of several components, or a wrong mask.

docs.text: • OVITO Color coding, Color by type and Assign color.

docs.title: Movies
docs.text:
mdapy.visualization.write_movie writes pictures as a movie with FFmpeg, which must be on the PATH: conda install ffmpeg, brew install ffmpeg or apt install ffmpeg. MDAPY does not ship it.

from mdapy.io import read_trajectory
from mdapy.visualization import render, write_movie

frames = read_trajectory("run.dump")
camera = dict(view="iso", focus=(50.0, 50.0, 50.0), span=150.0)
pictures = (
    render(frame, width=1280, height=720, device="auto", **camera) for frame in frames
)
write_movie("run.mp4", pictures, fps=30)

Give the pictures as a generator, as here: each is drawn when the movie needs it, so a long movie is not held in memory. Fix the frame with focus and span, or each picture frames its own atoms and the movie jumps.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
write_movie(path, pictures, *, fps=30)

Name Type Default Unit Meaning path str or path-like the file; its suffix, such as .mp4, tells FFmpeg the format pictures iterable of (H, W, 3) or (H, W, 4) uint8 (H, W, 3) or (H, W, 4) uint8 images of one size, as render gives them fps float64 30 1/s pictures per second

The movie is H.264 where FFmpeg offers it, the usual choice for .mp4, with a picture of odd size padded to even sizes for players. Draw the pictures with a background: a movie has no transparency.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
write_movie raises:

  • FileNotFoundError when FFmpeg is not on the PATH;
  • InvalidParameter when fps is not positive, there are no pictures, a picture is not an image of the size of the first, or they hold more than 8192 × 4320 pixels, the largest size of H.264;
  • CalculationFailed when FFmpeg fails, with what it says.

The tutorial A movie that flies through a crystal makes a movie from one system.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
mdapy.visualization.plot sets matplotlib up for the figures of journals and plots the results of MDAPY: parity plots of energies and forces, radial distribution functions, structure factors, bond angles, mean squared displacements, stacking fault energies, counts of structures, phonon band structures and densities of states, the moduli of a crystal along every direction, and two columns of the atoms against each other. It needs matplotlib.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.analysis import RadialDistributionFunction
from mdapy.build import build_crystal, random_alloy
from mdapy.visualization import plot

alloy = random_alloy(
    build_crystal("fcc", 3.6, repeat=(5, 5, 5)), {"Cu": 1, "Ni": 1}, seed=1
)
rdf = RadialDistributionFunction(cutoff=8.0, bins=160).compute(alloy)

with plot.style():
    fig, (left, right) = plot.figure("double", nrows=1, ncols=2)
    plot.rdf(rdf, ax=left, partial=True)
    reference = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=500)
    plot.parity(
        reference, reference + 0.02, ax=right, label="test", unit="meV/atom", scale=1000
    )
    plot.panel_label(left, "a")
    plot.panel_label(right, "b")
    # plot.save(fig, "figure")  # figure.pdf, figure.svg and figure.png
    fig.savefig("images/plots.png", dpi=200)

a: the partial radial distribution functions of a random CuNi alloy. b: a parity plot with its error in the legend.

In a notebook the figures of a with plot.style(): show when it ends, as the style holds only inside it. Add to a figure, and save it, inside the with.

docs.title: Columns of the atoms
docs.text:
scatter draws two columns of the atoms, components or expressions against each other, a point for each atom: here the number of neighbors of the atoms of a copper nanoparticle, shaken as by heat, against their distance from its center.

from mdapy.analysis import CoordinationNumber

crystal = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu", repeat=(8, 8, 8))
center = crystal.box.matrix.sum(axis=0) / 2
particle = crystal.filter(np.linalg.norm(crystal["positions"] - center, axis=1) < 12)
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
particle = particle.with_columns(
    positions=particle["positions"] + rng.normal(0, 0.1, (len(particle), 3))
)
particle = particle.with_columns(
    **CoordinationNumber(cutoff=3.0).compute(particle).columns(),
    distance=np.linalg.norm(particle["positions"] - center, axis=1),
)
with plot.style():
    fig, ax = plot.figure()
    plot.scatter(particle, "distance", "coordination", ax=ax)
    ax.set_xlabel("distance from the center (Å)")
    fig.savefig("images/scatter.png", dpi=200)

12 neighbors inside the nanoparticle, fewer at its surface, about 12 Å from its center.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Function Does style(*, font_size=None, line_width=None, colors=None, settings=None) a context in which matplotlib uses STYLE and the colors COLORS; font_size in points sets the text, its tick labels and legends 6/7 of it (default 7), line_width in points the lines of data (default 1), colors the colors that lines and points take in turn, one or several, and settings any other setting of matplotlib by its name, ahead of the options; Figures with MDAPY shows them at work figure(width="single", height=None, *, nrows=1, ncols=1, **options) a figure one column (88 mm) or two (180 mm) wide, or width mm; height in mm, by default 3/4 of a panel's width per row; options go to plt.subplots panel_label(ax, text, *, x=-0.12, y=1.02) a bold label at the top left of a panel save(fig, path, *, formats=("pdf", "svg", "png")) the figure in each format, the text of SVG kept as text parity(reference, predicted, *, ax=None, label="", unit="", scale=1.0, density=False, color=None) predicted against reference values with the diagonal, the root mean square error, times scale, in the legend; density draws a hexagonal map scatter(system, x, y, *, ax=None, atoms=None, max_points=20000, color=None) two columns, components or expressions of the atoms (or of those of the mask or indices atoms) against each other, as system[x] takes them, the atoms with finite values; at most max_points of them, picked at random with a fixed seed rdf(result, *, ax=None, partial=False) g(r), or the partial functions structure_factor(result, *, ax=None) S(q) warren_cowley(result, *, ax=None, shell=None, vmin=-2.0, vmax=1.0, cmap="GnBu") the Warren–Cowley parameters as a matrix of colors with their values written in, the central element along x and its neighbor along y; shell chooses one of several shells, and a value that cannot be told shows as – bond_angles(result, *, ax=None) the density of bond angles msd(result, *, timestep=1.0, ax=None, fit=None) the MSD against time in ps; fit=(first, last) fits a line over those lags, its slope over 6 the diffusion coefficient in the legend stacking_fault(result, *, ax=None, **options) a generalized stacking fault energy in mJ/m², a point for each slip joined by a line; options go to ax.plot, such as label structure_counts(result, *, ax=None) the atoms of each structure type, in its color band_structure(result, *, ax=None, color=None) phonon frequencies along a path, the special points marked; a color for each branch, or one for all phonon_dos(result, *, ax=None, projected=False) a phonon density of states, frequencies upward to stand beside a band structure, and that of each atom of the cell elastic_surface(result, quantity="young_modulus", *, ax=None, extreme=None, points=60, colormap="viridis") the "young_modulus", "linear_compressibility", "shear_modulus" or "poisson_ratio" of elastic constants along every direction, as a surface as far from the origin along each direction as the size of the value there, in the color of the value, unshaded so that the colors read on the color bar; the shear modulus and the Poisson ratio take a second direction across the first, and extreme, "min" or "max", draws their smallest or largest value over it; points directions from the z axis to its opposite, twice as many around it; ax must be in 3D, made with projection="3d" elastic_section(result, quantity="young_modulus", normal=(0, 0, 1), *, ax=None, extreme=None, points=360, color=None, label=None) the same along the directions of the plane normal to normal, as a curve, dashed where the value is negative; the axes of the plot are the axis of the box most nearly in the plane, laid into it, and the direction across it in the plane, named by their indices

Each plot draws on ax, by default a new figure, and returns the axes.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: STYLE follows the artwork guides of Nature: sans-serif text of 5 to 7 points, lines of 0.5 to 1 point, no top and right spines, fonts embedded as TrueType. COLORS are those of Okabe and Ito, safe for color blindness. MM, SINGLE and DOUBLE give millimetres and the widths of the columns in inches.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: style raises InvalidParameter for a font_size or line_width that is not positive, no colors, and a color or a setting that matplotlib does not know, with matplotlib's message. figure raises InvalidParameter for a width that is neither single, double nor a positive number, parity for values of different sizes, scatter for a column of several components or max_points below 1, and warren_cowley without a shell that exists for parameters of several shells, or with one for parameters of one shell. elastic_surface and elastic_section raise it for another quantity, a shear modulus or Poisson ratio without extreme or another quantity with one, and points below 3; elastic_surface for a colormap that matplotlib does not know or axes not in 3D, and elastic_section for a normal of another shape, zero or not finite. Without matplotlib the plots raise ImportError.

docs.title: Coordination polyhedra
docs.text:
CoordinationPolyhedra builds the convex hull of the neighbors of some atoms, as OVITO's coordination polyhedra do: the octahedra of oxygen about the titanium of a perovskite, the tetrahedra of a silicate. The polyhedra come as one triangle mesh for render, with the volume of each.

import numpy as np
from mdapy.analysis import CoordinationPolyhedra
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.visualization import render

srtio3 = build_crystal(
    "perovskite", 3.905, elements=["Sr", "Ti", "O"], repeat=(3, 3, 3)
)
titanium = np.asarray(srtio3["element"]) == "Ti"
octahedra = CoordinationPolyhedra(2.2).compute(srtio3, atoms=titanium)
octahedra.volumes  # 27 octahedra of 4/3 (a/2)³ = 9.92 Å³

# the octahedra in blue, strontium and oxygen as small atoms
strontium = np.asarray(srtio3["element"]) == "Sr"
render(
    srtio3,
    "images/polyhedra.png",
    atoms=~titanium,
    radius=np.where(strontium, 0.9, 0.45),
    mesh=octahedra.mesh,
    mesh_color="#4f86c6",
    mesh_alpha=0.85,
    view=(-1.0, -0.6, -0.45),
    width=600,
    height=600,
    legend=True,
)

SrTiO₃ repeated 3 × 3 × 3 times: the TiO₆ octahedra (blue), the oxygen (red) at their corners and the strontium (green) between them. The octahedra about the atoms on the faces of the box reach out of it, whole. mesh_color also takes one color per triangle, such as that of the atom of each, colors[octahedra.atoms[octahedra.owners]].

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
CoordinationPolyhedra(cutoff=None, *, num_neighbors=None, bonds=False)

Name Type Default Unit Meaning cutoff float64 Å the neighbors closer than this num_neighbors int32 the nearest neighbors, this many bonds bool False the atoms bonded to each, by the bonds of the topology, as OVITO does

Give exactly one of them. compute(system, *, atoms=None) builds the polyhedra about the atoms of a boolean mask or of indices, all by default. Neighbors are found through the periodic boundaries with the neighbor lists of MDAPY; each polyhedron is built about its atom, whole, even where it reaches out of the box. Neighbors in one plane make one face, cut into triangles.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A CoordinationPolyhedraResult:

Attribute Type Meaning mesh TriangleMesh the triangles of every polyhedron, counterclockwise seen from outside; their vertices are the neighbors next to the atom atoms (M,) int64 the atom in the middle of each polyhedron owners (F,) int64 the polyhedron of each triangle, an index of atoms volumes (M,) float64 the volume of each polyhedron in Å³; 0 for fewer than four neighbors or neighbors in a plane

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: CoordinationPolyhedra raises InvalidParameter unless exactly one of cutoff, num_neighbors and bonds is given; compute raises InvalidParameter for atoms that are not a mask or indices of the system and as NeighborList.build does, and MissingProperty with bonds for a system without bonds.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
mdapy.visualization.render draws a system by ray tracing: atoms as spheres, optionally bonds, the box, Voronoi cells, surfaces, dislocations and arrows of vectors, with ambient occlusion, shadows and outlines, in four styles. A Scene takes any spheres, cylinders and polygons for pictures made by hand.

import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.build import build_crystal, build_polycrystal
from mdapy.identify import CommonNeighborAnalysis
from mdapy.visualization import render

copper = build_crystal("fcc", 3.615, elements="Cu")
grains = build_polycrystal(copper, mp.Box(60.0), 6, seed=1)
structures = CommonNeighborAnalysis().compute(grains)

image = render(grains, color=structures, width=800, height=600)  # (600, 800, 4)
boundaries = render(
    grains, atoms=structures.structure != 1, color=structures, style="flat"
)

import numpy as np
from mdapy.visualization import STYLES, write_png

pictures = [
    render(grains, color=structures, style=style, width=600, height=450, device="auto")
    for style in STYLES
]
write_png(
    "images/styles.png",
    np.vstack([np.hstack(pictures[:2]), np.hstack(pictures[2:])]),
)

The four styles on a polycrystal colored by common neighbor analysis: fast and matte (top), shiny and flat (bottom).

color is one of: None for the color column of the system, which color_coding, color_by_type and assign_color set, or without one the colors of the elements; a single color, "#rrggbb", a name such as "red" or three numbers from 0 to 1; (N, 3) colors; a column, a component such as "positions.z", an expression over the columns or (N,) values, through the colormap; or a structure result such as that of CommonNeighborAnalysis, in its colors. The colors and display radii of the elements are those of OVITO, and for the elements OVITO leaves out the colors of Jmol and the covalent radii; covalent radii are those of Cordero et al. (2008), van der Waals radii those of Alvarez (2013), 1.5 Å and 2 Å for elements without one. Covalent bonds, covalent_bonds(system), join the atoms closer than the sum of their covalent radii and 0.45 Å, as in Jmol. Bonds are drawn as two halves in the colors of their atoms; a bond to a periodic image is drawn as the half next to each atom only, so nothing leaves the box.

docs.title: Colormaps
docs.text:
colormap(values, name="viridis", value_range=None) gives the (N, 3) colors of values; COLORMAPS holds the names. rainbow (OVITO's default), viridis, magma, jet, hot, blue_white_red and gray are computed as OVITO's color coding computes them, viridis and magma from their tables of 256 colors; plasma and coolwarm are MDAPY's own.

labels is for discrete values such as clusters, layers or grains: render(system, color="grain", colormap="labels", legend=True). Each value takes one of LABEL_COLORS, in increasing order, and the colors start again after the twelfth. It takes no value_range, and the legend lists the values with their colors, up to twelve of them.

The options are those of Scene.render:

Name Type Default Meaning width, height int32 1200, 900 size in pixels view str or (3,) float32 "iso" top, bottom, front, back, left, right, iso, or a direction of view up (3,) float32 of the view the direction up in the picture perspective, fov bool, float32 False, 30 a perspective camera and its vertical angle in degrees zoom float32 1 magnification of the scene framed to fill the picture focus (3,) float32 middle of the scene the point in Å at the middle of the picture span float32 the scene framed the length in Å the picture shows from bottom to top at the focus, in place of the framing and zoom: with focus, the region a viewport shows style str "matte" one of the styles below background color or None "white" None for transparent device str "cpu" "cpu", "gpu", or "auto" for the GPU when there is one; see below progress, cancel None as in Parallelism Style Look fast quick, as the viewports of OVITO: an ambient part, a light from the viewer and a broad highlight from the upper left, neither occlusion nor shadows matte matte spheres, as the pictures of the Tachyon renderer of OVITO: a bright sky darkened by ambient occlusion, a weak light from the viewer with sharp shadows shiny shiny spheres with a metallic sheen, after the pictures of the OSPRay renderer of OVITO: light from a sky and a wide key light that bounces once between the atoms, soft shadows and small highlights; about three times slower than matte flat plain colors, every atom outlined, as ASE draws atoms; for small systems

Any setting of a style can be changed by name: ambient, diffuse, specular, shininess, metalness (from 0 to 1: metals reflect less light diffusely and color their highlights), key, highlight and fill (directions toward the key light, the light of the highlights, by default the key light, and the fill light: right, up and toward the viewer), fill_intensity, base_light (light every surface gets, whatever hides it), srgb (light the colors as given in sRGB, as the renderers of OVITO do, in place of linear light: stronger contrast), ao_samples, ao_distance (Å, default 3 times the median radius), ao_strength, shadows, shadow_strength, flat, toon_levels, outline_width (pixels, at most 100), outline_depth (Å), outline_color, fog, supersample (rays per pixel along each axis), samples (rays per subpixel, the first through its middle and the others anywhere in it: more for smoother soft shadows, depth of field and global illumination), light_size (the angular radius of the key light in radians, 0 for a point, wider for softer shadows) and, for global illumination, bounces (0 for none). style_settings(style) gives every setting of a style as a dictionary.

docs.title: Soft shadows
docs.text: A key light light_size radians wide casts soft shadows in every style. They are sampled by the rays of each pixel and look grainy with few of them: raise samples for smoother pictures, at a cost in time that grows with it.

docs.title: On the GPU
docs.text:
With device="gpu" the rays are traced on the GPU: with Metal on macOS, with Direct3D 12 on Windows, which comes with the system, and with Vulkan on Linux, whose loader and driver come with the graphics drivers of NVIDIA, AMD and Intel (a build from source needs Vulkan's headers, see Installation). gpu_available() tells whether there is a GPU. A driver that runs on the processor, as in a virtual machine without a GPU, does not count: MDAPY's own threads trace faster there, so device="auto" uses them. A GPU with ray tracing units uses them: on Linux and Windows those of NVIDIA RTX, AMD Radeon RX 6000 and later and Intel Arc, for every ray; on macOS those of M3 and later, for the rays of occlusion and shadows. The environment variable MDAPY_GPU_RAY_TRACING=0 turns them off. The picture is the same as on the processor, with the same random samples in the same precision, up to rounding at a few edges. For a million atoms at 1920 × 1080:

Device matte shiny Apple M5, GPU 0.3 s 1.6 s the same without its ray tracing units 0.9 s 2.2 s Apple M5, processor 3.9 s 11.2 s NVIDIA RTX A2000 0.4 s 1.0 s the same without its ray tracing units 1.2 s 2.8 s Intel Core i5-12600K, processor 4.2 s 11.8 s NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop 0.2 s 0.5 s the same without its ray tracing units 0.7 s 1.5 s AMD Ryzen 9 7945HX, processor 2.3 s 7.4 s 
from mdapy.visualization import gpu_available

device = "gpu" if gpu_available() else "cpu"
picture = render(grains, color=structures, device=device)

docs.title: Molecules
docs.text:
Organic molecules are drawn with covalent bonds, found from the elements:

import numpy as np

# benzene: C-C 1.39 Å, C-H 1.09 Å
angles = np.arange(6) * np.pi / 3
ring = np.stack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles), np.zeros(6)], axis=1)
benzene = mp.System(
    np.vstack([1.39 * ring, 2.48 * ring]), elements=["C"] * 6 + ["H"] * 6
)
drawn = {
    representation: render(
        benzene,
        representation=representation,
        box=False,
        view=(0.3, 0.6, -1.0),
        style="shiny",
        width=520,
        height=400,
        device="auto",
        legend=True,
    )
    for representation in ("ball_and_stick", "licorice", "space_filling")
}
write_png("images/molecules.png", np.hstack(list(drawn.values())))

Benzene in the representations ball_and_stick, licorice and space_filling, in the shiny style.

docs.title: Vectors
docs.text:
An arrow along a vector of each atom, such as its displacement, velocity or force: here the displacements of the atoms of copper around an extra atom, put at an octahedral site and relaxed, in the plane of that atom.

import numpy as np
import mdapy as mp
from mdapy.build import build_crystal
from mdapy.calculators import EAM
from mdapy.simulation import minimize

a = 3.615
crystal = build_crystal("fcc", a, elements="Cu", repeat=(9, 9, 9))
site = np.array([4.5, 4.0, 4.0]) * a  # the middle of an edge of a cubic cell
start = mp.System(np.vstack([crystal["positions"], site]), crystal.box, elements="Cu")
relaxed = minimize(start, EAM.zhou(["Cu"]), max_force=1e-4).system
moved = relaxed["positions"] - start["positions"]
start = start.with_columns(displacement=moved)

distance = np.linalg.norm(start["positions"] - site, axis=1)
plane = np.abs(start["positions.z"] - site[2]) < 0.5
render(
    start,
    "images/vectors.png",
    atoms=plane & (distance < 10.5),
    color=np.linalg.norm(moved, axis=1),
    value_range=(0, 0.2),
    legend="displacement (Å)",
    radius=0.3,
    vectors="displacement",
    vector_scale=5,
    vector_radius=0.08,
    vector_color="atom",
    view="top",
    box=False,
    width=800,
    height=700,
)

The displacements of the atoms of copper around an extra atom in the middle, five times their length, from where the atoms were, in the color of their length: its four nearest neighbors in this (001) plane move out by 0.44 Å, the next ones by 0.13 Å, and the rest by less.

The arrows are those of OVITO's vector display with normal shading: a shaft of vector_radius, which is OVITO's arrow width, and a head 2.5 times as wide and 4.5 times as long as that radius; an arrow shorter than its head is a cone only, narrowed in proportion. OVITO draws flat arrows facing the viewer by default. Zero vectors and atoms not shown get no arrow.

docs.title: Scenes
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from mdapy.visualization import Scene

scene = Scene()
scene.add_spheres([[0, 0, 0], [2.5, 0, 0]], 1.0, [[0.8, 0.5, 0.2], [0.2, 0.5, 0.8]])
scene.add_cylinders([[0, 0, 0]], [[2.5, 0, 0]], 0.3, (0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
scene.add_triangles([[[-2, -2, -1.5], [4, -2, -1.5], [1, 3, -1.5]]], "gray", alpha=0.5)
picture = scene.render(width=400, height=300, style="shiny", view="front")
Method Adds add_spheres(centers, radii, colors, *, ids=None) spheres add_cylinders(starts, ends, radii, colors, *, ids=None) cylinders without caps add_triangles(vertices, colors, *, alpha=1.0, ids=None) (T, 3, 3) triangles, seen from both sides, opaque or not add_polygons(vertices, corner_offsets, corners, colors, *, alpha=1.0, ids=None) convex polygons, in the layout of VoronoiPolyhedra add_box(box, *, radius=0.15, color="black") the twelve edges of a box

Outlines separate primitives of different ids. write_png(path, image) writes a picture, (H, W, 4) RGBA or (H, W, 3) RGB uint8; voxel_faces(values, box) gives the cells of a grid over the box as triangles on its faces, for mesh (see Isosurfaces and voxels); colormap(values, name, value_range), element_colors(elements) and element_radii(elements, kind="display") give the colors and radii used by render.

docs.title: In a notebook
docs.text:
render returns the picture, and show_image shows it in a notebook such as Jupyter, without saving a file. It also takes a PNG or JPEG file, and width sets the width on the page in pixels. It needs IPython.

from mdapy.visualization import render, show_image

show_image(render(system))
show_image("picture.png", width=400)

docs.title: Results
docs.text: An (height, width, 4) uint8 array of RGBA pixels in sRGB, rows from the top, the same for any number of threads.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
They raise InvalidParameter for an unknown style, view, colormap, color or option, a size that is not positive or is above the limits below, arrays of the wrong shape, an opacity out of [0, 1], a polygon of fewer than three corners, a negative id or an invalid mask of atoms; Cancelled when cancelled.

A picture has at most 8192 pixels on a side, and supersample times that side is at most 16384, as larger pictures can use up the memory: 8192 × 8192 pixels with supersample=2 take about 5 GB, and each doubling of the side four times as much.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Every pixel traces supersample² × samples rays from an orthographic or perspective camera into a bounding volume hierarchy of the primitives; through a lens, each ray starts at a random point of it and passes through the point where the ray from its middle meets the sharp plane. At the nearest hit, the color of the primitive, in linear RGB (or as given with srgb), is lit by base_light, by an ambient term weighted by ambient occlusion, the fraction of ao_samples rays that leave without hitting anything closer than ao_distance (cosine-weighted about the normal, one in each of ao_samples rings of equal weight, their turns a golden angle apart), by the diffuse light of the key light, darkened by its shadow toward a random point of the light, and of the fill light, and by a Phong highlight, the light from highlight mirrored about the normal toward the viewer. A metal reflects 1 − 0.6 metalness of the diffuse light and colors its highlights, as the rasterizer of OVITO approximates metals. See-through triangles add their color and let the ray go on. An outline is drawn on the pixels next to a different primitive that lies at least outline_depth closer, or next to the background. The rays of a pixel are averaged, over the background, into sRGB.

With bounces above 0, each ray instead follows samples paths, the first through the center of its part of the pixel and the others anywhere in it. At each surface a path adds the light of the key light, sampled over a disk light_size wide and blocked by anything in the way, then turns into a cosine-weighted direction about the normal (the first turns of the paths of a subpixel spread over rings of equal weight): if it leaves the scene it adds the sky, of brightness ambient, otherwise it goes on to the next surface, its light now colored by the surfaces it met, for at most bounces more surfaces. Shadows soften and corners darken without ambient occlusion, and colors bleed onto neighbors; the noise falls as the samples grow.
